courses.title: Introduction to Accounting
courses.description: Serves as the first university-level accounting course most accounting students take. Highlights five major fields of accounting: the accounting cycle, business decision-making, taxation, fraud detection and prevention, and financial statement analysis. Develops students' knowledge and practice in each field through learning teams, case studies, and experiential learning. Provides an understanding of career opportunities available to accounting graduates, different career paths, and the effort required to complete the accounting major at BYU-Idaho.

courses.title: Accounting Software
courses.description: Takes an in-depth look at accounting software using Intuit QuickBooks® Online. Topics include invoicing, inventory control, payments, and a complete setup of a new or existing company. Only introductory accounting knowledge is required.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ACCTG210 - Principles of Accounting I (3) ; AGBUS201 - Agricultural Financial Accounting (3)

courses.title: Principles of Accounting I
courses.description: Prepares business and non-business students to create and analyze budgets and financial statements. The course applies managerial and financial accounting principles to support effective business decision-making.

courses.title: Principles of Accounting II
courses.description: Applies an integrated approach to financial and managerial accounting concepts. Students analyze business transactions and prepare accounting information to facilitate decision-making for internal and external decision-makers.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; AGBUS201 - Agricultural Financial Accounting (3) ; ACCTG210 - Principles of Accounting I (3) ; Note: ACCTG210 or AGBUS201 must be completed with at least a C- to be allowed to take this course.

courses.title: Special Projects
courses.description: This arranged course allows students to undertake a special project for further research in the field of Accounting.  This course does not count toward a degree.

courses.title: Intermediate Financial Accounting I
courses.description: Builds upon principles learned in Accounting 210 and 211 through rigorous study of financial accounting standards and the conceptual framework for financial reporting, the accounting cycle, recording of specific transactions for revenues, cash, receivables, and inventory, financial statement measurement and reporting, presentation of financial statements, financial statement disclosures, and time value of money concepts. The course is intended to provide students with some of the core skills needed to work in either public or private accounting or to pursue graduate education. Students also become familiar with accounting research techniques and how to apply accounting principles to case studies.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ACCTG211 - Principles of Accounting II (3) ; Students must earn a B- or greater in ACCTG211 to register for ACCTG301AND ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; BA215 - Spreadsheet Analysis for Business (3) ; -or- ACCTG233 (last offered 2025)

courses.title: Intermediate Financial Accounting II
courses.description: Builds on the principles in Accounting 201 and 301. Students learn to account for many of the following topics: current and non-current liabilities, investments, property, plant, and equipment, leases, dilutive securities, earnings per share, stockholders' equity, and income taxes. The course also prepares students for Accounting 403, 440, and 499. An understanding of present value, capital expenditures, accrual accounting, and the matching principle is very important for success in the course.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ACCTG301 - Intermediate Financial Accounting I (3)

courses.title: Cost Accounting
courses.description: Builds upon concepts learned in Accounting 202. The course emphasizes the use of cost data in the decision-making process and seeks to sharpen analytical, practical, and interpretative skills. Students study the impact of cost allocation in business decisions using various costing systems and methodologies.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ACCTG211 - Principles of Accounting II (3)

courses.title: Income Taxation I
courses.description: Studies the basic features of the federal income tax laws as applied to individual taxpayers. It emphasizes compliance procedures, the determination of taxable income, and the determination of the tax liability.  Students learn to communicate using common income tax terminology and obtain practical experience with tax compliance by preparing income tax returns.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ACCTG210 - Principles of Accounting I (3) ; ACCTG211 - Principles of Accounting II (3)

courses.title: Auditing
courses.description: Provides an introduction to auditing. The objectives include the principles and practices used by public accountants and internal auditors in examining financial statements and supporting data. Special emphasis is given to assets and liabilities.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ACCTG301 - Intermediate Financial Accounting I (3)

courses.title: Professional Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

Professional internships correlate actual work experience with accounting and business classroom theory.  Internships approved by the accounting internship director provide students with knowledge of career opportunities and how they might prepare to take advantage of them.  The ideal internship would take place during the winter semester (the accounting busy season) of the junior or senior year and would be off-site.  Two hundred and seventy (270) hours of quality accounting work experience are required. There will be an initial report, a final written report, and an employer evaluation.

courses.title: Income Taxation II
courses.description: Builds on the foundation established in Accounting 321 and provides an opportunity for students to acquire an understanding of more complex tax topics. The course focuses on tax planning and research, corporate taxation, and taxation of flow-through entities (i.e., partnerships and S corporations). Assignments develop the skills necessary for effective oral and written communication, tax research, tax return preparation, and teamwork. Successful students learn to think like a tax accountant and planner.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ACCTG321 - Income Taxation I (3)

courses.title: Advanced Spreadsheet Application
courses.description: Focuses on developing analysis and problem-solving skills using Microsoft Excel Visual Basic for Applications. The two main tools used in this course are Excel and Visual Basic for Applications (VBA). The course also focuses on building custom procedures and functions in Excel, using VBA, to provide customized solutions and Excel applications. Students learn the fundamentals of programming, including sequence, selection, and iteration, and build a complex application using these constructs.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ACCTG211 - Principles of Accounting II (3)AND ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; BA215 - Spreadsheet Analysis for Business (3) ; ACCTG233 - Spreadsheet Application (1) ; NOTE: ACCTG233 is a retired course and is no longer offered. It was last offered in 2025.

courses.title: Accounting Information Systems
courses.description: Develops students' ability to design and develop accounting information systems using the Event-Based Accounting technique, focusing on the Revenue cycle, Purchase cycle, Payroll cycle, and Production cycle. This approach helps students understand the purpose of accounting information systems, their strengths and weaknesses, how they are constructed, what and how data is captured and stored, and how information to facilitate decision-making is retrieved. In addition, students learn internal control concepts related to accounting information systems. They learn how to use audit software to perform a variety of auditing procedures to identify errors and irregularities. Students also learn how to use data analytics software to identify errors and irregularities and make management recommendations.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ACCTG301 - Intermediate Financial Accounting I (3)AND ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; BA215 - Spreadsheet Analysis for Business (3) ; -or- ACCTG 233 (last offered in 2025)

courses.title: Agriculture Orientation
courses.description: Orients students to career decision-making in the broad field of agriculture. Surveys occupational opportunities in agribusiness, introduces students to career marketing related to personal career searches, and develops study skills to enhance their university experience.

courses.title: Agricultural Financial Accounting
courses.description: Introduces students to agricultural financial accounting. Presents an approach to compiling and analyzing accounting information specific to agricultural operations. Builds on current accounting practices in agriculture. Explains cash-basis accounting, prevalent in many farm operations, through an accrual-adjusted system.

courses.title: Agricultural Economics
courses.description: This course is a systematic introduction to basic economic concepts and issues as they relate to the agribusiness sector in the U.S. economy.

courses.title: Agricultural Policy and Trade
courses.description: This is an advanced course in the study of agricultural policy formulation and government actions on the agrifood and agrifiber industry. The influence of policy on the domestic and global agricultural sectors of production, marketing, and finances will be discussed and assessed.  The course will also address the case for policy when market imperfections exist (i.e. negative environmental impacts, inefficient resource allocation, health and societal concerns, etc.).
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3)

courses.title: Agricultural Marketing
courses.description: This course involves fundamental marketing principles applied to agricultural marketing.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3) ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3)

courses.title: Agribusiness Operations Analysis
courses.description: This course involves the principles and procedures in the analysis and research of agricultural business operations.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ECON255 - Financial Analytics (3) ; AGBUS347 - Agricultural Marketing (3)

courses.title: Occupational Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

Internships provide actual work experience that will add to or enhance the career preparation and learning of individual students.  The ideal internship would take place during a student's flex semester and requires a minimum of seven weeks of quality full-time work experience.  Internships must be approved by the department internship coordinator.

courses.title: Agricultural Price Analysis
courses.description: This course involves the application of statistical tools for price analysis.  Emphasis is on the price discovery process for making specific agricultural commodities.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECON255 - Financial Analytics (3) ; AGBUS347 - Agricultural Marketing (3)

courses.title: Agriculture Commodity Marketing
courses.description: This is an advanced agricultural marketing course intended to provide students with an understanding of the structure and operation of agriculture commodity markets and their critical role in the agribusiness sector as well as the overall economy.  This course will develop future managers of agribusiness who can complete fundamental and technical analysis on the futures and options markets to effectively manage price risk.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AGBUS347 - Agricultural Marketing (3)

courses.title: Agribusiness Finance
courses.description: Covers the theory of financial decision-making as applied to farms and firms related to agriculture. This advanced course provides students with an understanding of the structure and operation of agricultural finance.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECON255 - Financial Analytics (3)

courses.title: Agriculture Business Management
courses.description: This course involves the application of approved practices, concepts, principles, and tools of management in an agricultural business.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AGBUS201 - Agricultural Financial Accounting (3) ; ECON255 - Financial Analytics (3)

courses.title: Strategic Food and Agribusiness Management
courses.description: A comprehensive examination of the economic and strategic management of food and agribusiness firms within a global business environment. Topics include organizational strategies and policies and business operations in agricultural food industries.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AGBUS347 - Agricultural Marketing (3)

courses.title: Soil Science
courses.description: Studies the principles of soil formation, classification, water management, chemistry, biology, nutrient cycles, and management. Students use quantitative analysis to understand the principles of soil properties.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; CHEM101 - Introductory Chemistry (3) ; CHEM105 - General Chemistry I (3) ; BIO180 - Introduction to Biology I (3)

courses.title: Soil Fertility and Plant Nutrition
courses.description: Provides instruction and hands-on experience in soil fertility and plant nutrition for agricultural and horticultural crops. Students study the methods of nutrient uptake, nutrient cycles of the primary nutrients, secondary and micronutrients, nutrient management strategies, environmental impacts, and economics of fertilizing and liming. The laboratory section of the course provides practical experience in measuring the availability of nutrients in soils and other soil fertility-determining properties.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CHEM101 - Introductory Chemistry (3) ; CHEM105 - General Chemistry I (3)AND ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; APS220 - Horticultural Soils (3) ; AGRON301 - Soil Science (3)

courses.title: Forage Crops
courses.description: Teaches how forage crops are grown, harvested, and preserved for use primarily as livestock feed. Students also learn about poisonous plants, insects, weather-related conditions, and other factors that degrade the quality of the feed.

courses.title: Soil Management
courses.description: The course is a study of the biological, chemical, and physical properties of soils as affected by human management of the land for crop production.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; APS220 - Horticultural Soils (3) ; AGRON301 - Soil Science (3)

courses.title: Crop Science
courses.description: Advanced principles of crop science, production, and management are covered in this course. The course reviews field scouting, cultivar selection, planting, in-season management of irrigation, plant nutrients, and pests, harvesting, and storage of major agronomic crops.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; APS122 - Introduction to Plant Science (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; APS220 - Horticultural Soils (3) ; AGRON301 - Soil Science (3)

courses.title: Crop Physiology
courses.description: Examines the science and application of crop science and physiology. The lectures apply cellular and biochemical analysis of plant physiology to the more applied aspects of plant growth, specifically agricultural crops. The course also examines the ways physiological processes are integrated into crop management practices to increase biological and economic yield. Course topics include photosynthesis, respiration, canopy development, carbohydrate and nitrogen storage, crop morphology, seed development, yield components, crop growth, crop reproduction, mineral nutrition, water relations, temperature stress, crop growth regulators, and indeotypes. The course examines how these topics apply to wheat, barley, corn, alfalfa (and other forages), soybeans, potatoes, and other crops grown in the Western United States. Students apply scientific principles from crop science and physiology to solve agricultural and environmental problems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3) ; APS122 - Introduction to Plant Science (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CHEM101 - Introductory Chemistry (3) ; CHEM105 - General Chemistry I (3)

courses.title: Crop Advisor Certification
courses.description: The international Certified Crop Advisor program is designed to provide qualified credentials to professionals in Agriculture who consult and make nutrient and pesticide recommendations to Grower/Producers. Completion of the course prepares students to take two required examinations for CCA certification.

courses.title: Plant Pathology
courses.description: This course will help plant growers to understand the potential for plant disease, to recognize symptoms of disease, understand the life cycle of the pathogen, and find a way to control, minimize, or eliminate it.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; APS122 - Introduction to Plant Science (3) ; BIO208 - Introduction to Plant Biology (4) ; BIO182 - Introduction to Biology III (4)

courses.title: Agroecology
courses.description: Studies sustainable agriculture, including modern agricultural impacts on natural ecosystems. Examines the application of modern agricultural technology to improve agricultural and economic sustainability.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Technology
courses.description: Provides an exploratory introduction to fundamental agricultural and horticultural technology systems. Students gain proficiency in utilizing the problem-solving cycle, unit conversions and the unit factor method, SI units and significant figures, data collection, analysis, and visualization, with strong emphasis on critical thinking, systematic problem solving, and effective communication. Introduces the basic laws of energy, force, and mass applied to technology systems such as mechanical systems, electrical and electronic applications, and thermal systems. Prepares students to apply these physical principles of technology and technology systems to plant science, horticultural systems, and agricultural technology.

courses.title: Introduction to Agriculture Technology
courses.description: Provides an exploratory experience in modern agricultural machinery and technology. Topics include discussion and hands-on application of the fundamentals of modern agriculture as a system, including machine and environment interactions, machinery and technology support systems, engine and power systems, and agricultural project management. The course introduces agricultural machinery and its integration with advanced technology, both current and emerging. The course content is designed for any academic discipline or experience level.

courses.title: Introduction to Precision Agriculture
courses.description: Examines the technology and application of global positioning systems (GPS) in agriculture. The course covers topics in GPS error and correction methods for GPS error as they apply to agricultural situations. Students learn how to use and apply recreational, iPad, DGPS, and RTK GPS systems for collecting agriculture-related data. Students use iPad GPS systems to collect detailed data such as field boundaries and areas of interest (weed patch). The DGPS and RTK GPS sections will include collecting large amounts of data over large areas, such as yield maps. Auto-steer and guidance steering systems will be discussed and demonstrated.

courses.title: Agricultural Safety
courses.description: Develops skills for preventive maintenance, care, and safe operation of agricultural and horticultural equipment while introducing skills for selecting and managing agricultural and horticultural machinery.

courses.title: Power and Control Systems
courses.description: Introduces key principles of electrical and hydraulic systems used in modern agricultural machinery and equipment. Through lectures and practical lab experiences, students gain an introductory understanding of both electrical and hydraulic systems, including the creation, transfer, and storage of energy, as well as the operation and control of various components and devices. Topics include electrical fundamentals, sensors, motors, fluid power principles, hydraulic components, and electro-hydraulics. The course also introduces emerging technologies such as smart controls, electric/hybrid solutions, and autonomous equipment.

courses.title: Processing and Handling Systems
courses.description: Covers the theory and application of materials handling, machinery, and systems used in crop processing, handling, and storage systems and facilities. Students learn the theory of materials handling and the technology and machinery involved in processing, handling, and storing crops. Students study the operation of different systems and operations, with emphasis on the application of technology and integration of operations, structures, and technology. Introduces system design.

courses.title: Machinery Management
courses.description: Provides an overview of agricultural machinery and power systems. Students study the principles of tractor power, engine performance, and machinery management. The course covers fundamental concepts and emerging technologies in agricultural equipment, emphasizing machinery selection, performance analysis, and cost-effective management strategies. Special emphasis is placed on data collection strategies, machinery performance analysis, and the integration of advanced technologies in modern farming. Through lectures and practical lab experiences, students develop skills to analyze, select, and manage agricultural machinery systems for efficient and cost-effective farm operations.

courses.title: Precision Agriculture
courses.description: This course is an in-depth evaluation of farming management strategies based on observing, measuring, and responding to temporal and spatial variability that is commonly gathered though precision practices with the end goal of improving agricultural sustainability in crop production.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; AGTEC186 - Introduction to Precision Agriculture (3) ; Complete 1 of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; GIS350 - Web and Mobile GIS (2) ; GIS355 - Remote Sensing (3) ; -or- GEOG230 (last offered 2022) ; -or- GEOL340 (last offered 2022)

courses.title: AI Fundamentals
courses.description: Equips students across all disciplines with a comprehensive foundation for understanding and using artificial intelligence (AI) systems. The curriculum integrates technical, practical, and ethical perspectives to prepare students for responsible use of AI in academic, professional, and personal contexts.

courses.title: Advanced AI
courses.description: Equips students across all disciplines with the ability to create custom AI agents to perform intellectual tasks important to them. The curriculum integrates technical, practical, and ethical perspectives to prepare students for responsible use of AI in academic, professional, and personal contexts.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AI101 - AI Fundamentals (1)

courses.title: Introduction to Cultural Anthropology
courses.description: Presents anthropological approaches and perspectives on humans, their culture, and their society, along with basic concepts for analyzing cultural behavior.

courses.title: Home Decor Design
courses.description: This introductory course teaches construction techniques for home decor sewing. Project categories include pillows, bedding, quilts, table linens, and window treatments. Techniques taught include, but are not limited to, embroidery, zippers, buttons, piecing, applique, cording, and hems. Students are required to furnish the fabric and notions for individual projects. Materials cost approximately $30 to $60 or more.

courses.title: Children's Apparel Design
courses.description: Introduces basic construction techniques for children's apparel. Projects include a knit shirt, pants, booties, a sleeper, a baby cap, as well as a bib, a blessing dress, and a lined coat. Some pattern design is included. Students are introduced to the sewing machine, serger, cover stitch, and embroidery machine. Students are required to furnish the fabric and notions for individual projects. Materials cost approximately $45 to $70 or more.

courses.title: Pattern Making
courses.description: Covers the principles of pattern making using basic drafting and flat-pattern techniques in half- and full-size patterns for woven fabrics. Students learn how to measure and create a personal women's dress or men's torso sloper, which will be used to create their full-scale final design.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; FCS207 - Apparel Construction I (2)

courses.title: CAD Pattern Making
courses.description: Covers the principles and applications of pattern design using Gerber AccuMark CAD Pattern Design. Principles of flat-pattern design techniques are now transferred to applications on CAD systems used in the garment industry. Using the newly acquired CAD skills, students study and reproduce a ready-made jacket.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; FCS207 - Apparel Construction I (2) ; APD245 - Pattern Making (3)

courses.title: Fashion History
courses.description: Students will examine the social, economic, political, and religious forces which have influenced the manner and style of dress throughout the centuries. They will gain knowledge of how historical fashion evolved from ancient to modern-day civilizations.

courses.title: Fitting and Alteration
courses.description: Instructs students to develop and create personalized slopers for a variety of body types using tissue and fabric fitting techniques. Students develop skills in fitting and altering ready-to-wear men's and women's apparel. Materials cost approximately $40-$70.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; APD245 - Pattern Making (3) ; FCS207 - Apparel Construction I (2)

courses.title: Special Studies in Apparel Design
courses.description: Special updates in Apparel Industry topics.  Topics could include semester courses in bridal, draping, tailoring, line collection, and knits and swimwear.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; FCS207 - Apparel Construction I (2) ; FCS307 - Apparel Construction II (4) ; APD245 - Pattern Making (3) ; APD345 - Fitting and Alteration (3)

courses.title: Apparel Entrepreneurship Internship
courses.description:
Students will gain internship experience working in an Apparel Entrepreneurship career. This internship MUST be at least 100 hours and at LEAST 7 weeks to qualify for a creditable Apparel Entrepreneurship Internship.

Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

courses.title: Home Gardening
courses.description: Covers plant selection, environmental considerations, plant production, and efficient home garden designs. Students participate in the planning, planting, growing, and harvesting of a garden. They also participate in processing the fruits of their labor. The course is an exploratory class for all majors who may be interested in working with plants as a part of their career.

courses.title: Introduction to Plant Science
courses.description: Explores the world of plant science, covering the relationship between plants and people, plant morphology and physiology, plant production, and how environmental factors affect plant growth. Field- and greenhouse-scale production practices are discussed. There is a 1-credit lab associated with the lecture that may be taken concurrently or during another semester.

courses.title: Introduction to Plant Science Laboratory
courses.description: Helps students learn to implement the scientific method to understand plant-related topics. Students become familiar with plant propagation and management through the manipulation of specimens.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; APS122 - Introduction to Plant Science (3)

courses.title: Horticultural Soils
courses.description: This course provides a basic understanding of soils and their importance in crop and food production. It examines the formation of soils and their physical, chemical, and biological properties. The course will demonstrate diagnosing and correcting plant nutrient deficiencies for various crops and rotations. The effect of soil physical, chemical, and biological on agricultural systems will be discussed. Environmental effects such as soil erosion and chemical pollution, and the management/remediation of these problems.

courses.title: Soils Lab
courses.description: This course is a hands-on experience determining soil texture, structure, color, measuring soil pH, nitrates, and fertilizers.

courses.title: Agriculture Leadership and Management
courses.description: This discussion-based course introduces students to leadership, ethics, and basic business practices as they relate to the agricultural industry. The vocabulary, tools, and skills needed to understand business processes are explored.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; APS122 - Introduction to Plant Science (3) ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: Special Problems
courses.description: The purpose of the special problems course is to provide opportunities for students to enrich their learning experience with areas of study that are not generally covered in the regular curriculum. There are also at times opportunities outside the classroom for experiences that further enhance the education that is provided in the Applied Plant Science programs. It should be noted that this class is not intended as a substitute for other courses in the department.

courses.title: Seminar
courses.description: Students learn from leaders in the agriculture technology, agronomy, and horticulture industries about career opportunities and how to prepare for employment.

courses.title: Irrigation and Water Management
courses.description: Provides students with a fundamental working knowledge of irrigation principles and practices encompassing agronomic and horticultural applications. Covers water conservation and drainage.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; APS122 - Introduction to Plant Science (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; APS220 - Horticultural Soils (3) ; AGRON301 - Soil Science (3)

courses.title: Alternative Cropping Systems
courses.description: Studies and applies alternative cropping systems. Covers hydroponics, crop tunnels, row covers, hoop houses, trellises, soil amendments, LED lighting, and alternative energy sources.

courses.title: Plant Breeding and Genetics
courses.description: Provides students with a working understanding of population genetics as well as molecular genomes and techniques available to plant breeders to improve crop qualities.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; APS122 - Introduction to Plant Science (3) ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3)

courses.title: Agronomy  Practicum
courses.description: Application of classroom instruction to research and field experiences. The course helps students gain hands-on learning experiences related to crops, soils, and environmental quality.

courses.title: Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

APS398R is a cooperative work or internship experience that is required of all APS majors.

courses.title: Integrated Pest Management
courses.description: Incorporates the identification and control of insects, weeds, and diseases affecting ornamental plants. Includes the use, limitations, and methods of applying pesticides, including laws concerning their use.

courses.title: Crop Insect Management
courses.description: Insect pests inflict billions of dollars worth of damage each year to agricultural and horticultural crops globally. This course prepares students to identify insect pests in the field, understand the life cycles of the pests and the crops they affect, and effectively manage crop production systems to minimize the negative impacts of harmful insects.

courses.title: Integrated Weed Management
courses.description: This course is a study of weeds and their impacts on agricultural production. The course will include instruction on weed physiology, identification, control practices, and ecological impacts.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; APS220 - Horticultural Soils (3) ; AGRON301 - Soil Science (3) ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3)

courses.title: Special Topics in Applied Plant Science
courses.description: This special topics course is used by faculty to discuss novel or emerging areas within agricultural technology, agronomy, crop science, environmental science, horticulture, or soil science.

courses.title: Mentored Student Research
courses.description: Student Mentored Research provides opportunities for BYU-Idaho students to work with faculty members to design, conduct, analyze, and report research. The focus is to help students prepare for research related careers in agriculture.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; APS122 - Introduction to Plant Science (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; APS220 - Horticultural Soils (3) ; AGRON301 - Soil Science (3)

courses.title: Arabic I
courses.description: Provides an introduction to Arabic while developing active speaking and listening skills in Arabic, along with reading and writing skills in Modern Standard Arabic. Uses the dialect spoken in Palestine, Lebanon, Jordan, and Syria. Introduces students to the culture, religion, and politics of the Middle East.

courses.title: Arabic II
courses.description: Builds on the skills developed in Arabic 101. Students learn the Levantine (Shaami) dialect along with Modern Standard Arabic. Enables students to carry on basic conversations with native speakers across the Arab World. The course expands students' cultural understanding of the region and identifies regional differences in the Arabic language.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ARAB101 - Arabic I (4)

courses.title: Introduction to the Visual Arts
courses.description: This is an art appreciation course that surveys the concepts, techniques, materials and history of the visual arts.

courses.title: Freshman Art Orientation Seminar
courses.description: This freshman-focused advising seminar helps art students explore the different degrees offered in the Art Department and discover the various art careers these degrees can lead to. Students will learn about which courses to take each semester in order to make the most of their degree. Students will also have the opportunity to meet with full-time faculty from their major to begin making connections that will help them throughout their education.

courses.title: Design and Color
courses.description: In this course, students will learn the elements and principles of design and basic color theory used to solve visual design problems.

courses.title: Drawing I
courses.description: This introductory drawing course explores observational drawing strategies. Emphasis is given to linear construction, perspectival concepts, development of organic and geometric forms, the preliminary exploration of tonal drawing methods, and drawing as a fundamental tool of the visual artist.

courses.title: Adobe CC Basics
courses.description: This course is a practical introduction to the core features and concepts within Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign (also referred to as the core 3 CC apps). Each software program will be broken into 2 modules (beginner and intermediate features). Students will be tested on their ability to demonstrate how each of these features works or what the concepts mean etc.

courses.title: Introduction to Graphic Design
courses.description: This course covers the exploration of contemporary visual communications within graphic design and related fields.

courses.title: Media Experimentation
courses.description: This course is an exploration and expansion of painting and drawing media, techniques, and processes for 2-dimensional art.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART107 - Design and Color (3) ; ART110 - Drawing I (3)

courses.title: Photography I
courses.description: Students through classroom discussion and practical experience of the lab, will gain a foundation for black and white photography.

courses.title: Art History I
courses.description: This course surveys art from prehistoric to Renaissance with an emphasis on artists and art in their political, social, and religious contexts.

courses.title: Art History II
courses.description: This course surveys art from Renaissance to Modern with an emphasis on artists and art in their political, social, and religious contexts.

courses.title: Drawing II
courses.description: This course is an intermediate drawing class with in-depth study of proportion, composition, light and shadow.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART110 - Drawing I (3) ; ART107 - Design and Color (3)

courses.title: Introduction to Art Education
courses.description: This course acquaints students with Secondary Art Education philosophy. Students will address the importance of advocacy for the arts in the public schools and the community, the basic history of art education, and current trends in the field. Topics also include aesthetics and art criticism, with a focus on contemporary visual culture, contemporary art, and art from non-Western cultures.

courses.title: Ceramics I
courses.description: This course is an introduction to ceramics process including skill development in hand building, throwing on the potter's wheel, and glazing with an emphasis on craftsmanship and design.

courses.title: Typography I
courses.description: This course is an introduction to typography as a fundamental element of graphic design. This course will also reinforce student knowledge of InDesign.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART130 - Introduction to Graphic Design (3)

courses.title: Design Thinking: Inquiry and Innovation
courses.description: This course brings elements from the disciplines of Design, Humanities, and Business together into a fast-paced workshop-style experience that teaches students how to challenge their assumptions and think like an innovator. Students will solve human-centered design challenges using the latest innovations and Design Thinking methods and mindsets. Students will practice ethnographic research, frame insights, compose actionable questions to define a consumer's needs and wants, tailor a positive experience with a product or service to the customer, and verify desirability, feasibility, and viability. Students will develop the ability to work and communicate efficiently in diverse groups as they practice essential principles of Emotional Intelligence.

courses.title: Graphic Design
courses.description: This course involves graphic design projects with an emphasis on creative, conceptual, and practical solutions.  Students will also reinforce their understanding of Photoshop.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART130 - Introduction to Graphic Design (3) ; ART230 - Typography I (3)

courses.title: Graphic Design Portfolio Lab
courses.description: The class will introduce students to the concept of gathering their visual work into a well-structured portfolio. It will also require students to submit a portfolio for consideration of advancement in the graphic design degree.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ART235 - Graphic Design (3)

courses.title: Introduction to Illustration
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the field of Illustration, its media, techniques, and processes.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART110 - Drawing I (3) ; ART107 - Design and Color (3) ; ART142 - Media Experimentation (3)

courses.title: Illustration Portfolio Lab
courses.description: The class will introduce students to the concept of gathering their visual work into a well-structured portfolio. It will also require students to submit a portfolio for consideration for advancement in the Illustration degree.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ART240 - Introduction to Illustration (3)

courses.title: 2D Digital Illustration
courses.description: This course explores digital media to produce narrative and conceptual illustrations.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; ART240 - Introduction to Illustration (3) ; ART334 - Typography II (3)

courses.title: Character Animation I
courses.description: This course will introduce the student to the principles of animation by focusing on basic character animation.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART210 - Drawing II (3)

courses.title: Color for Illustrators
courses.description: Students will learn more about color theory through lecture, presentations and assignments. Students will also have the chance to apply what they learn about color in class exercises, demonstrations and out of class assignments. Students will explore palettes, color schemes, mood, and hue relationships. Temperature of colors will also be studied. Students will learn vocabulary, terms and explanations concerning color. Drawing, values, and composition will play an important role through out the class. Time management will be a vital skill for students to be able to complete all that is required, workload is heavy.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART110 - Drawing I (3) ; ART107 - Design and Color (3)

courses.title: Painting I
courses.description: This course teaches students proper studio practices related to oil painting as well as the fundamentals of color mixing and value structure.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART107 - Design and Color (3) ; ART110 - Drawing I (3)

courses.title: Watercolor
courses.description: This course is an introduction to watercolor painting. Students will create paintings that apply a variety of painting techniques and knowledge unique to the medium.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART110 - Drawing I (3) ; ART107 - Design and Color (3)

courses.title: Printmaking I
courses.description: This course teaches the fundamentals of printmaking, including image making, printing, and print conservation.

courses.title: Intermediate Photography
courses.description: Students, through classroom discussion and practical experience in the field and in the lab, will build upon the foundation of basic photography. Students will create photographs in various areas including: landscape, portraiture, and still life, among others.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART125 - Adobe CC Basics (3) ; ART160 - Photography I (3)

courses.title: Sculpture I
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the basic processes of sculpture: modeling, casting, and assembling, with an emphasis on the human figure.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: This course is a variable credit independent study for portfolio enhancement. This course is recommended to be taken after freshman year.  Independent study may be taken to fill an Art emphasis requirement and must be approved by the faculty member within the emphasis the student would like to study.  It may not be taken to fulfill a required Art course.  More information about this course is available in the Art Department office.

courses.title: Art Seminar
courses.description: This course is a visiting artist program designed to introduce students to a variety of artists from a variety of disciplines.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ART106 - Freshman Art Orientation Seminar (.5) ; ART101 - Introduction to the Visual Arts (3)

courses.title: Greek and Roman Art
courses.description: This course surveys the ancient Greek and Roman worlds.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART201 - Art History I (3)

courses.title: Medieval Art
courses.description: This course surveys western art from the time of Constantine the Great to the beginning of the Renaissance.

courses.title: History of Design and Illustration
courses.description: This course surveys the history of graphic design and illustration.

courses.title: History of Photography
courses.description: This course is an in-depth study of the technical and theoretical history of photography.

courses.title: Theories in Art
courses.description: This is a course designed to inform the student of contemporary art and related theories through a variety of readings and discussions. This course will present diverse ideas from a number of contemporary sources. A gospel perspective on this subject is also featured.

courses.title: Figure Drawing
courses.description: This course is an introduction to drawing the human form with a focus on proportional analysis, gesture, superficial anatomy, and composition. A variety of drawing media and mark-making systems are explored as students examine the graphic, expressive and conceptual potential of the human figure.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART107 - Design and Color (3) ; ART110 - Drawing I (3)

courses.title: Secondary Art Methods I
courses.description: The purpose of this class is to acquaint students with Secondary Art Education methods including lesson planning, curriculum development, presentation skills, art classroom motivation, and management.  You will complete this through written lesson planning and lesson presentation, completing studio processes in Art Education, and participation in a secondary art classroom.

courses.title: Elementary Art Methods
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to acquaint you with the skills of disciplines necessary to prepare you to teach art in the elementary classroom. It will introduce the techniques and skills necessary for the production of art works, methods, and examples of using contemporary art education methods in the classroom, and will provide an overview of the art modes mediums, and materials used by artists and how to adapt those methods to the elementary classroom.

courses.title: Ceramics II
courses.description: In this course, students explore and expand technical design skills learned in Ceramics l.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART220 - Ceramics I (3)

courses.title: User Interface Design
courses.description: Project-based course for creating working user interface prototypes that are as aesthetically pleasing as they are functional. Students will apply motion design principles to user interface designs to improve usability.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART125 - Adobe CC Basics (3) ; ART235 - Graphic Design (3) ; ART235L - Graphic Design Portfolio Lab (0.5)

courses.title: Surface Pattern Design
courses.description: This course is an exploration of the Surface and Pattern Industry. Students will explore employment opportunities, create production-ready patterns, and discover new forms through playful experimentation. The course will help students develop a narrative-based, career-ready portfolio for a specific audience.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART107 - Design and Color (3) ; ART110 - Drawing I (3) ; ART125 - Adobe CC Basics (3) ; ART235 - Graphic Design (3) ; ART235L - Graphic Design Portfolio Lab (0.5)

courses.title: Typography II
courses.description: This course is an in-depth study and experimentation of typography and typeface design.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART125 - Adobe CC Basics (3) ; ART235 - Graphic Design (3) ; ART235L - Graphic Design Portfolio Lab (0.5)

courses.title: Identity Design
courses.description: This course is an advanced overview of identity/branding logo development.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART125 - Adobe CC Basics (3) ; ART235 - Graphic Design (3) ; ART235L - Graphic Design Portfolio Lab (0.5)

courses.title: Narrative Illustration
courses.description: This is a portfolio-building course that concentrates on visual storytelling and creating visual ideas. Design techniques, markets, styles, and professional issues will be addressed. Personal development of skill, art vocabulary, and expression will be emphasized. Traditional and digital mediums will be utilized.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ART240 - Introduction to Illustration (3) ; ART240L - Illustration Portfolio Lab (0.5) ; Students must complete ART 240L with a minimum B grade or higher.

courses.title: Entertainment Illustration I
courses.description: This course focuses on an in-depth study of the entertainment field. Environment design, character design, lighting, pacing, and storytelling will be covered. Areas of focus include: film, television, and computer games.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ART240 - Introduction to Illustration (3) ; ART240L - Illustration Portfolio Lab (0.5) ; Students must complete ART 240L with a minimum B grade or higher.

courses.title: Layout and Story
courses.description: Students will create environmental drawings that feature 1pt, 2pt, and 3pt perspective while also emphasizing story, mood, and emotion.  Students will additionally learn the foundational theories of story development and story boarding, which may be applied to either live action or animated film, television, multimedia, and advertising markets.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART110 - Drawing I (3) ; ART107 - Design and Color (3)

courses.title: 3D Digital Illustration
courses.description: This course explores digital 3D modeling as an illustration and entertain medium.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ART240 - Introduction to Illustration (3) ; ART240L - Illustration Portfolio Lab (0.5) ; Students must complete ART 240L with a minimum B grade or higher.

courses.title: Painting II
courses.description: In this course, students will focus on developing their voice by exploring different mediums and 2D techniques, developing ideas, and expanding their awareness of contemporary artists.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ART250 - Painting I (3) ; ART252 - Printmaking I (3)

courses.title: Book Arts
courses.description: This course incorporates a variety of ways to make handmade books and boxes.

courses.title: Figurative Painting
courses.description: This course provides targeted instruction on how to make creative figurative paintings that make use of the pictorial, conceptual and narrative potential of the human form. Design thinking, composition, and conceptualization are explored in detail. Projects emphasize the development of painterly sensibilities with regard to mark-making, layering, interpretation, paint body, and color impact.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART110 - Drawing I (3) ; ART107 - Design and Color (3) ; ART250 - Painting I (3)

courses.title: Painting Methodologies
courses.description: In this course, students will experiment with different approaches to painting mediums as well as approaches to composing images and conceptualizing ideas. This process will prepare students to grow an individual artistic vision and a more competitive portfolio.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART250 - Painting I (3)

courses.title: Advanced Photography
courses.description: This course is designed to teach the fundamentals of creative digital photography. We will use various computer hardware (digital cameras, scanners, and printers) and software to record, produce, manipulate, and output images. Having a solid understanding of the myriad of possibilities which digital photography affords you is critical to succeeding as an artist in the rapidly changing field of photography. Additionally, knowing the background and historical context of the different photographic styles we will study should deepen your appreciation for the contributions of historical and contemporary art photographers.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART160 - Photography I (3) ; ART125 - Adobe CC Basics (3)

courses.title: Introduction to Studio Lighting
courses.description: This course will introduce the student to the controlled environment of the photographic studio. The student will be introduced to practical and creative lighting solutions for photographing people and objects. Large format cameras and architecture will also be briefly introduced. Students must have access to a digital, single lens reflex camera.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ART260 - Intermediate Photography (3) ; ART361 - Advanced Photography (3)

courses.title: Advanced Black and White Photography
courses.description: This course incorporates advanced principles of black-and-white photography, including darkroom printing, darkroom experimentation, camera exploration, and fine digital black-and-white printing will be explored.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART160 - Photography I (3)

courses.title: Commercial Photography
courses.description: This course will prepare students for success in commercial photography and broaden their opportunities in Fine Art.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART362 - Introduction to Studio Lighting (3)

courses.title: Printmaking II
courses.description: This is a portfolio course for printmaking students providing experience with intaglio processes.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART252 - Printmaking I (3)

courses.title: Sculpture Medium and Methodology
courses.description: This course is an exploration of six different types of approaches to sculpture. It is also research and concept-driven.

courses.title: Business for the Professional Artist
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce art students to basic business principles for professional visual artists. Students will be given an in-depth look at operating their art career as a small business, and teach them from a hands-on perspective how to excel in the competitive world of the visual arts.

courses.title: Travel Study in the Arts (A)
courses.description: In this course, various art venues are studied in Salt Lake City, UT area (or other near by areas) including workshops, galleries and museums, architecture, sculpture, painting, printmaking, drawing, illustration, graphic design, and photography. For further questions regarding this course contact the Art Office at (208) 496-4900.

courses.title: Travel Study in the Arts (B)
courses.description: This course, various art venues are studied in a variety of cities such as: San Francisco, Los Angeles, or Seattle including workshops, galleries and museums, architecture, sculpture, painting, printmaking, drawing, illustration, graphic design, and photography. For further questions regarding this course contact the Art Office at (208) 496-4900.

courses.title: Travel Study in the Arts (C)
courses.description:
This course explores various art venues in cities such as New York and Washington D.C., including workshops, galleries, museums, architecture, sculpture, painting, printmaking, drawing, illustration, graphic design, and photography. 

For further questions regarding this course, contact the Art Office at (208) 496-4900.

courses.title: Travel Study in the Arts (D)
courses.description: In this course, various art venues are studied in a variety of cities including workshops, galleries and museums, architecture, sculpture, painting, printmaking, drawing, illustration, graphic design, and photography.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: This is a Special Topics course.

courses.title: Renaissance Art
courses.description: This course will survey Italian and Northern Renaissance art from 1300 to 1600.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART201 - Art History I (3) ; ART202 - Art History II (3)

courses.title: Baroque Art
courses.description: This course will survey European art from 1600 to 1750.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART201 - Art History I (3) ; ART202 - Art History II (3)

courses.title: Nineteenth Century Art
courses.description: This course will survey European and American art of the 19th century.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART201 - Art History I (3) ; ART202 - Art History II (3)

courses.title: Modern and Contemporary Art and Theory
courses.description: This course examines the artistic movements, the driving theories behind them, and the historical context of the modern, post-modern, and contemporary world. It will begin with Cezanne and his influence on modernism and end with the contemporary art impulse with possibilities for the future.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART201 - Art History I (3) ; ART202 - Art History II (3)

courses.title: Special Topics in Art History
courses.description: This course has varying topics depending on the semester taught.  It may focus on, but is not limited to, a specific area of art history like an artist or stylistic movement or approach art history from a thematic or artist driven lens.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART201 - Art History I (3) ; ART202 - Art History II (3)

courses.title: Advanced Figure Drawing
courses.description: In this course, students will use advanced figure drawing with costumed models emphasizing composition, lighting, and varied media.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART312R - Figure Drawing (3)

courses.title: Secondary Art Methods II
courses.description: This course will acquaint students with the skills and methods necessary to prepare them to teach art in the secondary classroom. It will build on the student's Art Education theory and how to practically apply its concepts into curriculum development and lesson planning.

courses.title: Ceramics III
courses.description: In this course, students will learn advanced ceramic techniques with personal direction for portfolio development.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART320R - Ceramics II (3)

courses.title: User Experience Design
courses.description: This course focuses on learning how to create effective user experiences. Students will learn to follow and present an iterative design process that includes developing scenarios, creating prototypes, conducting usability tests and analyzing the results.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART125 - Adobe CC Basics (3) ; ART235 - Graphic Design (3) ; ART235L - Graphic Design Portfolio Lab (0.5)

courses.title: Design Thinking: User Research
courses.description: This course bridges the gap between Design Thinking methodology and User Experience (UX) Design in a slow-paced, deep dive studio experience. Students will learn how to leverage Design Thinking methods and mindsets and UX research tools to identify and document a user's total experience with a product or service. They will identify areas of the user experience that are inconsistent with a company's marketing, mission, or product intent. With this insight, teams will work collaboratively to create solutions that can show measured improvements to the customers' overall experience. The studio will mimic a design consultancy where students participate in teams researching, creating, testing, and presenting.

courses.title: Three-Dimensional Graphic Design
courses.description: This course explores a wide range of design problems in three-dimensional forms  including: package, signage, environmental, exhibit, and retail design.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART125 - Adobe CC Basics (3) ; ART235 - Graphic Design (3) ; ART235L - Graphic Design Portfolio Lab (0.5)

courses.title: Motion Design
courses.description: This is a project based studio course covering the principles of design applied to motion and storytelling. Students will begin learning Adobe After Effects and all processes related to creating an animated piece.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART125 - Adobe CC Basics (3) ; ART235 - Graphic Design (3) ; ART235L - Graphic Design Portfolio Lab (0.5)

courses.title: Professional Projects
courses.description: The professional projects course will provide the opportunity for students to work on real client projects. Students will work collaboratively in teams which will be modeled after a typical design studio structure. The course will teach and apply principles of effective teamwork, project management, and other essential business practices including assessing client/project needs, creating effective client presentations and, preparing digital files for final delivery to client. Students will also be able to evaluate their current portfolios of work in preparation for entering into the workforce.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART125 - Adobe CC Basics (3) ; ART235 - Graphic Design (3) ; ART235L - Graphic Design Portfolio Lab (0.5)

courses.title: Illustration Senior Project
courses.description: This course is an in-depth study of visual storytelling and the narrative tradition of illustration.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ART240 - Introduction to Illustration (3) ; ART240L - Illustration Portfolio Lab (0.5) ; Students must complete ART 240L with a minimum B grade or higher.

courses.title: Illustration Capstone
courses.description: This course serves to prepare illustration students for employment upon graduation.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ART240 - Introduction to Illustration (3) ; ART240L - Illustration Portfolio Lab (0.5) ; Students must complete ART 240L with a minimum B grade or higher.

courses.title: Advanced 2D Studio
courses.description: In this course, students will learn to manage a 2D studio practice while working on a personal project that builds their portfolio and art career.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART350R - Painting II (3)

courses.title: Portrait Photography
courses.description: This course is an in-depth study of the human form and lighting for commercial portrait photography.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART362 - Introduction to Studio Lighting (3)

courses.title: Historic Photographic Processes
courses.description: This course introduces photographic processes of the 19th and 20th centuries.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART260 - Intermediate Photography (3) ; ART361 - Advanced Photography (3)

courses.title: Printmaking III
courses.description: This is a portfolio course for Printmaking students.  Students will focus on their preferred Printmaking media to develop a portfolio of sufficient breadth and depth.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART370 - Printmaking II (3)

courses.title: Advanced Book Arts
courses.description: This course is an introduction to advanced techniques of book arts and further development of technical ability.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ART352 - Book Arts (3)

courses.title: Figure Sculpture
courses.description: This is an advanced course in sculpture that allows students to develop a personal direction of expression.

courses.title: Independent Study II
courses.description: This course is an independent study as needed for upper division courses or credits. Independent study may be taken to fulfill an Art emphasis requirement and must be approved by the faculty member within the emphasis the student would like to study.  It may not be taken to fulfill a required Art core course. More information about this course is available in the Art Department office or the Career and Academic Advising.

courses.title: Portfolio Capstone
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to synthesize a student's art education into a portfolio and artist's packet that best represents his/her learning, preparing him/her to integrate into the world of art, further education, professional practice, or quality life experiences.

courses.title: Fine Art Capstone
courses.description: Fine Art students will broaden their understanding of professional art practices and synthesize their art education into a portfolio and artist's packet, preparing them for a career in the fine arts.

courses.title: Internship in the Arts
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

This is an independent internship course that is designed to give students a hands-on introduction to their intended purposes.

courses.title: Career Exploration in Animal Science
courses.description: Provides entry-level Animal Science students with career perspectives. Guides students in researching and discussing various careers within the animal science industry to support the creation of a detailed curriculum plan and career development portfolio.

courses.title: Introduction to Meat Products
courses.description: Introduces students to the biochemical properties of food, food safety, and processing procedures in an experiential manner. Demonstrations using meat products as a medium help students understand how and why certain ingredients are used and their long-term effects on food safety, quality, and affordability. Explores and discusses current issues in our society relevant to food safety to help students make more informed food decisions.

courses.title: Introduction to Animal Science
courses.description: Introduces the seven pillars of animal science emphasized in the Animal Science program: preconception/genetics, reproduction and pregnancy, nutrition, production management, behavior/handling/welfare, health and disease, and benefit and use to mankind. The laboratory supports class learning and introduces students to the program's facilities and animals.

courses.title: Animal Anatomy and Physiology
courses.description: Uses a systems approach to the study of animal anatomy and physiology. Students study the structure and functions of the cell, skeletal, muscular, nervous, digestive, and reproductive systems. Studies practical applications of anatomy and physiology and their relation to diseases and disorders.

courses.title: Animal Anatomy and Physiology Lab
courses.description: Involves a laboratory experience covering microscopic cellular anatomy, cadaver dissection, and live animal palpation. The course meets for two hours per week and includes hands-on study of animal systems that complements the course lecture.

courses.title: Feeds and Nutrition
courses.description: Covers the study of the principles of animal nutrition as applied to nutrient digestion and metabolism, feedstuff characteristics, and principles for formulating nutritionally balanced diets.

courses.title: Veterinary Parasitology
courses.description: Introduces students to common veterinary parasites. Covers the life cycles, pathogenesis, identification, and treatment of the common parasites affecting most domestic animals. Examines the relationship between parasites and the overall health of the host animal. Explores the zoonotic potential of disease transmission by parasites.

courses.title: Introduction to Animal Biotechnology
courses.description: Emphasizes the growing importance of molecular biology techniques in animal breeding and agricultural practices (e.g., genomic selection, genetic testing, and gene editing). Teaches students basic techniques used to manipulate DNA and conduct basic computer analysis of DNA and protein sequences (bioinformatics).

courses.title: Animal Handling and Behavior
courses.description: Introduces students to animal handling and behavior through pressure and release techniques for low-stress livestock handling. Students develop a higher level of communication with all species of animals, including cattle, sheep, horses, and humans. Students discuss theory in a classroom setting while gaining hands-on experience in the laboratory.

courses.title: Animal Science Seminar
courses.description: Provides instruction and insight into issues in food animal production. Teaches students to interpret food animal research and summarize and present research data.

courses.title: Animal Health and Diseases
courses.description: Provides instruction in the areas of animal health evaluation, livestock disease prevention, and treatment, leading to the development of the basic skills required to evaluate animal health status and programs.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AS215 - Animal Anatomy and Physiology (3)

courses.title: Artificial Insemination
courses.description: Provides instruction on the benefits and limitations of artificial insemination in cattle, basic reproductive anatomy and physiology, semen thawing and handling, estrus synchronization, genetic principles of sire selection, and the requirements for implementation in a cattle AI program.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AS336 - Animal Reproduction (3)

courses.title: Artificial Insemination Lab
courses.description: Accompanies AS 330. The use of proven sires through AI represents the greatest tool for genetic improvement available to cattle producers. Focuses on semen straw thawing and handling, as well as the manual technique required for transcervical placement of semen in the bovine uterus.

courses.title: Animal Genetics
courses.description: This course covers the genetic principles and technologies involved in improving animal breeding in the context of productivity, sustainability, and welfare. Students will explore the  principles and technologies underlying the current mating systems used in animal breeding and maintenance.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH221B - Biostatistics (3)

courses.title: Animal Reproduction
courses.description: Studies reproduction in cattle, sheep, horses, and pigs. Covers basic reproductive anatomy and the processes involved in prenatal development, puberty, conception, and parturition.  Applies reproductive principles to estrus synchronization, insemination, ultrasonography, and embryo transfer.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AS215 - Animal Anatomy and Physiology (3)

courses.title: Horse Production
courses.description: Discusses production practices in the selection, care, and evaluation of horses. Provides students with a better understanding of the modern equine industry. Covers principles of horse health, breeds of horses, their characteristics, and their uses, as well as equine behavior, anatomy and physiology, nutrition, and reproduction. Enables students to create a business plan that involves the equine field in which they are interested.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AS215 - Animal Anatomy and Physiology (3)

courses.title: Small Animal Production
courses.description: Provides a hands-on, in-depth study of how to economically and efficiently produce swine, sheep, goats, and poultry. Students learn how to transform their investment of dollars and time into a profitable and rewarding farm enterprise. The course is centered on production traits of swine, sheep, goats, and poultry.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AS150 - Introduction to Animal Science (3) ; AS220 - Feeds and Nutrition (3) ; AS336 - Animal Reproduction (3)

courses.title: Principles of Meat Science
courses.description: Incorporates everything from the growth and development of beef, swine, and sheep to case-ready beef products. Exposes students to every aspect of meat science. Emphasis is placed on carcass merits and value and includes grading, evaluation, and appraisal of meat. Also includes techniques of slaughter, fabrication, labeling, food safety, and finished retail product.

courses.title: Beef Production
courses.description: Applies techniques and principles of beef production and management. Lectures help students better understand the demands, trends, and management tools of the beef industry. Students receive hands-on training concerning health care, reproduction, nutrition, cattle selection, breeds, best management practices, and economic tools used in management decisions.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AS220 - Feeds and Nutrition (3) ; AS336 - Animal Reproduction (3)

courses.title: Applied Ruminant Nutrition
courses.description: Uses a team-based, service-learning approach to provide Animal Science students with hands-on, real-world experience in both feeding and assessing feed practices of ruminant animals (especially cattle). Activities include multiple site visits to commercial production operations, assessment of the feed-related practices of the operation, and delivery of feed recommendations to the producer based on the assessment. Students are given access to necessary financial and logistical information, are exposed to conventional practices in the animal nutrition world, and learn to interact with industry personnel. The course would ideally be taken concurrently with AS 360 (Beef Production).
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AS220 - Feeds and Nutrition (3)

courses.title: Dairy Production
courses.description: Addresses core principles and practices inherent to an industrial dairy production operation. Covers basic dairy cattle husbandry practices, genetics, nutrition, lactation, health, milk production, and marketing.

courses.title: Companion Animal Management
courses.description: Introduces students to the care and management of companion animals. Covers common varieties of pets, the human-animal bond, behavior, nutrition, reproduction, health, husbandry, human interactions, and social issues.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AS215 - Animal Anatomy and Physiology (3) ; AS215L - Animal Anatomy and Physiology Lab (1)

courses.title: Internship
courses.description:
Internships are exempt from tuition, but are charged this independent course fee.

An internship is a cooperative program between BYU-Idaho Department of Animal and Food Science and approved Experience Providers (employers). Internships provide actual work experience that will add to or enhance the career preparation and learning of individual students. Internships approved by the department or college internships coordinator provide students with knowledge of career opportunities and actual work experience in preparation for employment after graduation. The ideal internship would take place during the student's flex semester; however allowances can be made to adjust schedules to meet specific internships.  Students will not be allowed to start and finish their internships during the 7 week summer break. Required internships should generally be a stepping stone into your future career. Internships are typically 40-hour a week positions that last for a length of a semester (14 weeks).  A maximum of one credit hour will be available for a single approved internship.

courses.title: Advanced Animal Nutrition
courses.description: Provides instruction in advanced animal nutrition with an emphasis on nutrient digestion mechanics, absorption, and cellular metabolism.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AS220 - Feeds and Nutrition (3) ; CHEM105 - General Chemistry I (3) ; CHEM105L - General Chemistry Laboratory I (1)

courses.title: Applied Reproduction
courses.description: Develops students' skills in livestock reproduction technologies, including estrus synchronization, pregnancy detection, ultrasonography, and embryo transfer. Focuses on cattle.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AS330 - Artificial Insemination (1) ; AS336 - Animal Reproduction (3)

courses.title: Processed Meats
courses.description: Covers techniques of the modern meat processing industry and its use of science and technology. Includes fabrication, processing, preservation, sanitation, Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP), and utilization of manufactured and processed meat. Provides actual laboratory preparation of processed meats and by-products produced in today's meat packing industry. Familiarizes students with several key and general concepts relating to the safe production and marketing of processed meats.

courses.title: Research Practicum
courses.description: This course is designed to reinforce and improve upon selected occupational competencies.
