This course focuses on independent study, student mentored research, special assignment, and/or advanced inquiry in an area of special interest.  Registration is approved after consultation with instructor in charge (upon request).

courses.title: Animal Science Capstone
courses.description:
Challenges students to integrate their accumulated knowledge, technical, and social skills to identify and solve a problem relevant to issues encountered by professionals in their chosen discipline, and to communicate the results of their efforts to their peers. Provides students with the opportunity to demonstrate their ability to adapt to professional situations, appreciate the need for lifelong learning, and initiate professional and personal liaisons.

This course will be offered Winter and Fall semesters in odd-numbered years and the Spring semester in even-numbered years.

courses.title: Automotive Ownership and Maintenance
courses.description: Teaches the function and operation of the major automobile systems. Students learn the responsibilities of automobile ownership, including how to inspect, maintain, service, and purchase a vehicle.

courses.title: Electrical Systems
courses.description: Explains how electricity is generated, stored, and used to power various automotive devices.Teaches students how electrical circuits are constructed and how to diagnose faults.

courses.title: Electrical Systems Lab
courses.description: Students will learn electrical circuit testing and diagnostic skills, practicing them as they diagnose and repair electrical faults.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; AUTO131 - Electrical Systems (2)

courses.title: Engine Performance
courses.description: Teaches how an internal combustion engine works, including understanding the purposes and functions of individual engine components and the fuel, ignition, cooling, and lubrication systems. Covers various methods for testing and evaluating the performance of the engine and its related systems.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; AUTO131 - Electrical Systems (2)

courses.title: Engine Performance Lab
courses.description: Students will learn engine performance testing and diagnostic skills, practicing them as they diagnose and repair engine-related faults.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; AUTO132 - Engine Performance (2)

courses.title: Chassis Systems
courses.description: Covers the theory of operation, diagnosis, service, and repair procedures of automotive chassis (steering, suspension, and braking) systems.

courses.title: Career Planning
courses.description: Explores automotive career options. Guides students in choosing, preparing for, and obtaining an internship. Develops students’ professional networks through goal-based strategies and teaches interviewing skills, resume creation, and portfolio development.

courses.title: Drivetrains
courses.description: Focuses on the theories of operation, diagnosis, repair, and maintenance of automotive drivetrain systems. Provides instruction and hands-on experience with manual transmissions/transaxles, clutch assemblies, differential axles, drive shafts/u-joints, and four-wheel drive and all-wheel drive systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; AUTO155 - Chassis Systems (2) ; AUTO132 - Engine Performance (2)

courses.title: Climate Control
courses.description: Introduces students to the electrical, pressure, and temperature principles governing heating and air-conditioning systems. Teaches students to use professional service equipment to test, diagnose, and repair faults in these systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO132 - Engine Performance (2) ; AUTO131 - Electrical Systems (2)

courses.title: Climate Control Lab
courses.description: This course will introduce students to the electrical, pressure, and temperature principles that govern heating and air conditioning systems. They will learn to use professional service equipment to test, diagnose, and repair heating and air conditioning faults.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO131 - Electrical Systems (2) ; AUTO131L - Electrical Systems Lab (1) ; AUTO132 - Engine Performance (2) ; AUTO132L - Engine Performance Lab (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; AUTO223 - Climate Control (2)

courses.title: Braking Systems
courses.description: Covers the theory of operation, diagnosis, service, and repair procedures of automotive braking systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO131 - Electrical Systems (2) ; AUTO132 - Engine Performance (2)

courses.title: Braking Systems Lab
courses.description: Covers the theory of operation, diagnosis, service, and repair procedures for automotive braking systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO131 - Electrical Systems (2) ; AUTO131L - Electrical Systems Lab (1) ; AUTO132 - Engine Performance (2) ; AUTO132L - Engine Performance Lab (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; AUTO255 - Braking Systems (2)

courses.title: Chassis Dynamics
courses.description: Explains the operational principles of various suspension and steering systems. Teaches students to test, diagnose, maintain, and repair these systems and their components. Explores the function sand servicing of advanced driver assistance systems and dynamic safety systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO131 - Electrical Systems (2) ; AUTO132 - Engine Performance (2)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; AUTO255 - Braking Systems (2)

courses.title: Chassis Dynamics Lab
courses.description: Develops students' ability to test and diagnose steering and suspension systems and repair related chassis faults. Provides hands-on experience servicing, diagnosing, and repairing advanced driver assistance systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO131 - Electrical Systems (2) ; AUTO131L - Electrical Systems Lab (1) ; AUTO132 - Engine Performance (2) ; AUTO132L - Engine Performance Lab (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; AUTO255 - Braking Systems (2) ; AUTO255L - Braking Systems Lab (1) ; AUTO256 - Chassis Dynamics (2)

courses.title: Career Networking
courses.description: Continues to cultivate students' professional networks and facilitate informational interviews. Refines students' verbal, written, and portfolio communication skills. Advances students toward their career goals by expanding their experience, knowledge, and network relationships.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO195 - Career Planning (1)

courses.title: Automotive Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap. 

This course involves at least twelve consecutive weeks of supervised automotive-related work experience. Conditions of this internship are arranged on an individual basis by the students and the faculty coordinator for this relationship.

courses.title: Vehicle Electronics
courses.description: Explains how computers function as integrated components of automotive electrical systems. Covers input and output circuits and communication among modules and components.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO131 - Electrical Systems (2) ; AUTO132 - Engine Performance (2)

courses.title: Vehicle Electronics Lab
courses.description: Teaches electrical and electronic circuit testing and diagnostic skills. Students practice these skills as they diagnose and repair electrical and electronic faults.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO131L - Electrical Systems Lab (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; AUTO331 - Vehicle Electronics (2)

courses.title: Engine Management Systems
courses.description: Examines various engine management systems used in modern vehicles. Covers electronic fuel injection (EFI), ignition control, emission control, and air induction systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO132 - Engine Performance (2) ; AUTO131 - Electrical Systems (2)

courses.title: Engine Management Systems Lab
courses.description: Develops students' ability to test and diagnose engine management systems and repair related faults through hands-on practice.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO131L - Electrical Systems Lab (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; AUTO332 - Engine Management Systems (2)

courses.title: Internal Combustion Engines
courses.description: Deepens students' understanding of internal combustion engine theory and operation. Teaches students to apply diagnostic tests and component inspections to determine the causes of engine failure. Covers the specified machining and assembly processes required to restore an engine to its original state.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO331 - Vehicle Electronics (2) ; AUTO332 - Engine Management Systems (2)

courses.title: Internal Combustion Engine Lab
courses.description: Develops students' ability to diagnose, determine the cause of failure, and rebuild an internal combustion engine. Students ensure that all components, materials, and processes comply with engineered specifications. Students will demonstrate successful operation of the rebuilt engine in the vehicle.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO332L - Engine Management Systems Lab (1) ; AUTO255L - Braking Systems Lab (1) ; AUTO331L - Vehicle Electronics Lab (1) ; AUTO256L - Chassis Dynamics Lab (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; AUTO351 - Internal Combustion Engines (2)

courses.title: Drivetrain Systems
courses.description: Covers the theory of operation, testing, diagnosis, and repair of drivetrain system used in passenger cars and light trucks. Students study the hydraulic, electrical, and mechanical principles that govern the operation of a modern manual and automatic transmission.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO331 - Vehicle Electronics (2) ; AUTO332 - Engine Management Systems (2) ; AUTO255 - Braking Systems (2)

courses.title: Drivetrain Systems Lab
courses.description: Provides laboratory instruction in the theory of operation, testing, diagnosis, and repair of drivetrain systems used in passenger cars and light trucks. Students will study the hydraulic, electrical, and mechanical principles that govern the operation of modern automatic and manual transmission systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO331L - Vehicle Electronics Lab (1) ; AUTO332L - Engine Management Systems Lab (1) ; AUTO255L - Braking Systems Lab (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; AUTO366 - Drivetrain Systems (3)

courses.title: Career Strategies
courses.description: Develops a strategic approach to career attainment and advancement. Guides students in setting goals and reviewing progress, refining resumes and portfolios, cultivating a long-term professional network, and increasing communication and interviewing effectiveness.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO295 - Career Networking (1)

courses.title: Automotive Professional Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

This course is a customized internship designed to help automotive students obtain experience in the sector of the automotive industry in which they wish to obtain eventual full-time employment. The internship should last at least 12 weeks. Other conditions of the internship are arranged on an individual basis by the student and the faculty coordinator for the internship.

courses.title: Drivability and Diagnostics
courses.description: Builds on students' experience in other courses and develops their understanding of vehicle emissions systems and emissions testing. Teaches students to use vehicle onboard diagnostic system monitors to test and verify successful repairs. Examines fuel and ignition systems in greater depth.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO331 - Vehicle Electronics (2) ; AUTO332 - Engine Management Systems (2)

courses.title: Drivability and Diagnostics Lab
courses.description: Applies knowledge gained in the Drivability and Diagnostics course to live project vehicles with drivability problems. Uses advanced engine performance diagnostics, including scan tools and oscilloscopes, to diagnose and repair vehicles. Teaches students to run OBD II monitors to verify vehicle system repairs.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO331 - Vehicle Electronics (2) ; AUTO331L - Vehicle Electronics Lab (1) ; AUTO332 - Engine Management Systems (2) ; AUTO332L - Engine Management Systems Lab (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; AUTO481 - Drivability and Diagnostics (2)

courses.title: Data Acquisition and Analysis
courses.description: Teaches students to acquire vehicle data from various types of sensors and onboard data networks. Develops students' ability to analyze data, identify patterns and relationships, and communicate key findings to others.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO331 - Vehicle Electronics (2) ; AUTO332 - Engine Management Systems (2)

courses.title: Data Acquisition and Analysis Lab
courses.description: Teaches students to use data acquisition tools to log vehicle data from sensors and data networks. Develops students' ability to analyze acquired data, identify patterns and relationships, and communicate key findings to others.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; AUTO331 - Vehicle Electronics (2) ; AUTO331L - Vehicle Electronics Lab (1) ; AUTO332 - Engine Management Systems (2) ; AUTO332L - Engine Management Systems Lab (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; AUTO482 - Data Acquisition and Analysis (2)

courses.title: Hybrid and Electric Vehicle Technology
courses.description: Covers the application of electric vehicle technology in hybrid and battery-electric vehicles and safe work practices for high-voltage systems. Explains how energy flows through EVs to drive vehicles and charge batteries.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; AUTO332 - Engine Management Systems (2) ; AUTO331 - Vehicle Electronics (2)AND ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; AUTO155 - Chassis Systems (2) ; AUTO255 - Braking Systems (2)

courses.title: Hybrid and Electric Vehicle Technology Lab
courses.description: Provides laboratory experience in safely disabling high-voltage systems. Uses data acquisition tools to log information from electric vehicle systems to verify proper operation of electric vehicle systems. Develops students' ability to analyze data and communicate key findings to others.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; AUTO332 - Engine Management Systems (2) ; AUTO331 - Vehicle Electronics (2)AND ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; AUTO155 - Chassis Systems (2) ; AUTO255 - Braking Systems (2)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; AUTO483 - Hybrid and Electric Vehicle Technology (2)

courses.title: Special Projects
courses.description: With the help and approval of the instructor, students will establish learning outcomes and plans for an individualized automotive-related project. This project will allow students to apply and develop knowledge and skills that enhance their employability in the industry.  The number of credits awarded will be determined by the instructor based on the scope of the project.  Personal vehicle projects do not qualify as special projects for this course.

courses.title: Business Fundamentals
courses.description: Provides an experiential overview of the core functions of business, including product development, marketing, operations, human resource management, accounting, and finance. Through applied activities and integrated learning experiences, students develop fundamental management and decision-making skills while exploring how key business functions work together in real-world organizational contexts. The course exposes students to a variety of career opportunities in business and is also recommended for non-business students seeking a practical introduction to business management, leadership, and entrepreneurship.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; BUS115 - Applied Spreadsheets and Analysis (3) ; CIT110 - Introduction to Excel (3) ; ECON215 - Quantitative Methods (4) ; MATH108X - Math for the Real World (3) ; MATH109 - Precalculus (5) ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; MATH119 - Applied Calculus for Data Analysis (4) ; MATH221A - Business Statistics (3) ; MATH221B - Biostatistics (3) ; MATH221C - Social Science Statistics (3) ; MATH221D - Introductory Statistics with R (3) ; -or ACCTG233 (last offered 2025)

courses.title: Spreadsheet Analysis for Business
courses.description: Develops students' intermediate to advanced spreadsheet analysis skills in a business context. After individually completing spreadsheet tutorials and assignments, students then develop and apply their skills in a wide range of mini-projects and exams. The mini-projects and exams, which are designed to be realistic and representative of business activities students might encounter in the workplace, include elements of finance, marketing, and supply chain management.

courses.title: SQL for Analysts
courses.description: The course description you’re reading right now is served to you from a database. Come learn how stored data can help answer complex business questions! The course is query-focused, imitating questions analysts in industry might be asked by their leaders to drive business decisions. The course will not spend time on learning about database design or database administration. Students will learn about subqueries, common table expressions, window functions, query optimization, and how SQL and MS Excel can work together.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; BA215 - Spreadsheet Analysis for Business (3) ; BUS115 - Applied Spreadsheets and Analysis (3) ; OR ACCTG233 (last offered 2025)

courses.title: Business Analytics
courses.description: Develops essential skills for retrieving, cleaning, loading, and analyzing data to glean meaningful insights. Uses Microsoft Power BI as the primary data analysis tool for obtaining insights. Covers data retrieval, data wrangling, data analysis, and data insights, along with data storytelling, the pitch, and strategic action items.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; BA215 - Spreadsheet Analysis for Business (3) ; BUS115 - Applied Spreadsheets and Analysis (3) ; CIT110 - Introduction to Excel (3) ; OR ACCTG233 (last offered 2025)

courses.title: Business Analytics Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

Required for all Business Analytics students. Students must be registered for this course within the first two weeks of the semester they are completing the internship. Students will find a professional business internship in an approved business, complete the application and obtain approval through the College of Business and Communication Career Services, be enrolled in the course, write reports, submit evaluations, and complete at least 270 hours of work in seven weeks or more. During their internship students will gain a greater vision of becoming a business professional and establish career networking links. Students will earn one to three credits and may receive compensation from the employer and letters of recommendation from both the employer and BYU-Idaho.

courses.title: Special Topics in Business Analytics
courses.description: An arranged research or special project course. Contact the department for registration information.

courses.title: Introductory Biology for Allied Health
courses.description: This course is a one-semester introduction to Biology.

courses.title: Introduction to Biology I
courses.description:
This course is the first semester of a year-long Introduction to Biology course. It includes the areas of biological chemistry, cellular structure and function, and metabolism. This course is a prerequisite for most other upper division courses in Biology.

Not a General Education or Foundation Science course.

courses.title: Introduction to Biology I Lab
courses.description: Develops critical thinking skills that enable students to perform in a variety of professional settings. Uses comprehension of scientific literature and laboratory bench experience to achieve this aim. Increases students' understanding of scientific format and process in the literature; teaches new lab techniques and guides students in designing their own labs based on those techniques; and teaches students to illustrate scientific experiments and decipher scientific figures. Repeated use of skill sets is a core feature of the lab, giving students opportunities to learn and then practice skills. Attendance in labs is mandatory for full credit. Each lab has an associated weekly homework assignment.

courses.title: Introduction to Biology II
courses.description: This course is the second semester of a year-long Introduction to Biology course.  It includes the areas of classical genetics, molecular biology, ecology, and evolution. There is a weekly lab in addition to the lecture.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO180 - Introduction to Biology I (3)

courses.title: Introduction to Biology II Lab
courses.description: Develops critical thinking skills that enable students to perform in a variety of professional settings. Uses comprehension of scientific literature and laboratory bench experience to achieve this aim. Increases students' understanding of scientific format and process in the literature; teaches new lab techniques and guides students in designing their own labs based on those techniques; and teaches students to illustrate scientific experiments and decipher scientific figures. Repeated use of skill sets is a core feature of the lab, giving students opportunities to learn and then practice skills. Attendance in labs is mandatory for full credit. Each lab has an associated weekly homework assignment.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3)

courses.title: Introduction to Biology III
courses.description: Provides a one-semester introduction to the diversity of life on Earth, offering an overview of the evolution and general features of bacteria, archaea, protists, fungi, plants, and animals. Information presented in this course will help students prepare for the biodiversity sections of the PRAXIS, DAT, or GRE-Biology subject exams. BIO 182 is designed primarily for Biology Education majors, and it is not recommended for students who are Biology majors in the Zoology Emphasis.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3) ; BIO101 - Introductory Biology for Allied Health (3)

courses.title: Wildlife and Natural Resource Career Orientation
courses.description: Introduces students to degree and career opportunities in wildlife and natural resource management. Explores job opportunities in the field and routes of preparation and advising for eventual employment. Includes resume preparation, meetings with advisors, reading scientific literature about careers in natural resources, and attendance at a campus career workshop.

courses.title: Biology Orientation
courses.description: Includes six modules: 1. General Overview (*required for all students*); 2. Ecology/Wildlife; 3. Graduate Programs/Academic Careers; 4. Pre-Professional Careers (med, dent, opt, vet, etc.); 5. Industry Careers (lab, pharmaceutical reps, etc.); and 6. Allied Health (chiropractics, PA, OP, PT, etc.).  Each student is expected to attend all of Module 1: General Overview, then select three of the remaining five modules. Modules may be taught by different faculty members. Each module includes unique information pertinent to the topics covered and a set of requirements for students who attend that module. These requirements may include reading assignments, reports, summary sheets, or written papers.

courses.title: Basic Skills and Safety for Field Biologists
courses.description: Develops students' confidence and competence in fundamental skills necessary for internships and employment in wildlife and natural resource management. Uses online modules and hands-on labs in which students demonstrate competence in skills such as trailering, animal handling, first aid, power tools, GPS navigation, bear safety, field survey techniques, and taxonomic identification.

courses.title: Introduction to Plant Biology
courses.description: This course is an introduction to Botany including cell structure/function, plant physiology, heredity, evolution, reproduction, and plant anatomy.  Lab is required.

courses.title: General Microbiology
courses.description: This course explores the key differences between bacteria and viruses (both beneficial and harmful to the body) and the ability of these microbes to cause human infectious disease.  Students learn current methods used to identify microbes, control their spread, and ways the body can defend against infection.  Students learn to apply scientific reasoning to validate current clinical approaches to controlling infectious disease to assist in future efforts to protect their health and the health of others.  This course is a common prerequisite for nursing and other allied health programs.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; BIO222 - General Microbiology Lab (1)

courses.title: General Microbiology Lab
courses.description: In this course, students use the microscope to study different types of microorganisms and learn the methods used to grow, identify, and characterize them.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; BIO221 - General Microbiology (3)

courses.title: Range Management
courses.description: In this course, subject material will focus on: rangeland management history, physical characteristics descriptions of rangelands, rangeland plant physiology, ecology, inventory, monitoring, stocking rates, grazing methods, wildlife livestock distribution, animal nutrition, multiple use management, livestock production on rangelands, rangeland wildlife, and manipulation of range vegetation.

courses.title: Essentials of Human Anatomy and Physiology
courses.description: This course provides an overview of human anatomy and physiology.  It is a one-semester course that covers the primary structures and functions of all organ systems of the human body. It is designed for students who would like to gain a greater understanding and appreciation for the human body.  It is required for students majoring in social work, health psychology, public health, health care administration, therapeutic recreation, and biology education.  The course does not fulfill graduation requirements for nursing, health science, or biology majors.

courses.title: Neurobiology
courses.description: This is an introductory course in Neuroscience. It covers the elements of Neurobiology by providing an introduction to the nervous system; examines cellular communication, sensory, motor and integrating systems, such as, the neural basis of behavior; and explores the plasticity of neural systems in learning, during development and via hormonal influences.

courses.title: Environmental Biology with Lab
courses.description: This course will use basic ecological principles to examine environmental issues. The environmental issues range from local to global and include direct and indirect human impact on ecosystems. This class includes a 2-hour lab (BIO 250L) to allow hands-on understanding of what is covered in lecture.

courses.title: Range Plant Taxonomy
courses.description: This is an introductory course in vascular plant taxonomy, with a primary focus on the classification of flowering plants.  Characteristics of some of the major plant families will also be examined.  Basic taxonomic skills will be taught to build a foundation for successful plant identification using a dichotomous key.  The principal plant communities of the western United States will be presented.  A secondary focus will be on the identification of selected range plants, including their forage value, toxicity, invasiveness, and habitat value.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO180 - Introduction to Biology I (3) ; BIO208 - Introduction to Plant Biology (4)

courses.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology I
courses.description: Human Anatomy and Physiology I is the first part of a two-semester course that prepares students for further study in the health and medical fields. The second course is BIO 265: Human Anatomy and Physiology II. Both of these courses have a corresponding lab that is taken separately (BIO 264L and BIO 265L). Most students must take BIO 264 and BIO 265 as well as the corresponding lab courses to fulfill prerequisite requirements to apply for specific medical professional programs. This course includes 12 modules. The modules begin by examining important physiological chemistry principles. Then the course instructs students in the biology and physiology of the cell. The rest of the course will examine the nervous and muscular systems. Please note that this course is not acceptable for biology major credit. If you are a biology major, you should probably be in a different course.

courses.title: Human Anatomy  and Physiology I Lab
courses.description: This is the laboratory accompaniment of the first part of a two-semester course studying the anatomy and physiology of the human body.  While the lecture mainly focuses on physiology, most of the anatomical learning occurs in this lab. The course is designed for students of nursing and the allied health professions.  Students wishing to apply to the nursing program must complete both the lecture and lab components.  This course is not acceptable for biology major credit.  (These students should take Bio 460 and 461 instead of 264 and 265.)

courses.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology II
courses.description: Human Anatomy and Physiology II is the second of a two-semester course that prepares students for further study in the health and medical fields. You should have already completed BIO 264: Human Anatomy and Physiology I. Both of these courses have a corresponding lab that is taken separately from the lecture portion of the course. Most students must take BIO 264 and BIO 265 as well as the corresponding lab courses to fulfill prerequisite requirements to apply for specific medical professional programs. This course includes 10 modules. Please note that this course is not acceptable for biology major credit. If you are a biology major, you should probably be in a different course.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO264 - Human Anatomy and Physiology I (3)

courses.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology II Lab
courses.description: This is the laboratory accompaniment of the second part of a two-semester course studying the anatomy and physiology of the human body.  The course is designed for students of nursing and the allied health professions.  Students wishing to apply to the nursing program must complete both the lecture and lab components.  This course is not acceptable for biology major credit. (These students should take Bio 460 and 461 instead of 264 and 265.)

courses.title: Ecology I
courses.description: This course is an introduction to Ecology including climates and distribution of life, adaptations of life to environmental conditions, life history characteristics, population characteristics, competition, predation, and parasitism.  Lab is required.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3) ; BIO208 - Introduction to Plant Biology (4) ; GEOL112 - Historical Geology (4)

courses.title: Ecology II
courses.description: This course is a continued introduction to Ecology including energy and nutrient cycling, community composition, succession, disturbance management, ecosystem function, distribution, and characteristics of major biomes.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Introduction to Biometry and Experimental Design
courses.description: This course will teach students in the biological sciences about study and sampling design, measures of center and spread, elementary probability, sampling distributions, descriptive statistics, and statistical inference. Students will also learn to archive and analyze data, and to use the statistical program RStudio to graphically represent data.  Upon completion of this course, students will have a strong foundation in the scientific process and basic statistics using R and RStudio for biology data, which will help them in upper-level courses, internships, employment, graduate school, or other endeavors.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Scientific Writing and Communication
courses.description: The goal of this course is to familiarize students with the principles of effective scientific communication.  This course will cover areas of scientific communication that students will need to know to be successful in their careers.  Students will learn the basic rules of word, grammar, and punctuation usage; as well as an approach to the style of writing.  Students will then apply these principles when writing papers, reports, resumes; and when preparing scientific presentations and posters.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Invertebrate Zoology
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the diversity, anatomy, physiology, ecology, and evolution of invertebrate animals.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4) ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3)

courses.title: Biology of Microorganisms
courses.description: The topics covered in this course will include microbial diversity, the methods used to study microorganisms, microbial metabolism and genetics, the role of microorganism in causing disease, the immune response, the methods used to control microorganisms, and the use of microorganisms by man.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3)

courses.title: Range Ecology Systems Management
courses.description: Areas of discussion in this course include pasture lay out, fence design, water systems, herding effect, grazing systems, leasing, permits, BLM, state ground, private ground, lease ground, forage estimates, photosynthesis, energy store, tools of land management, and drought management.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO225 - Range Management (3)

courses.title: General Entomology
courses.description: This course is an introduction to Entomology with lectures and laboratories on insect structure, development, classification, behavior, and control.  An insect collection and fieldwork are required.

courses.title: Principles of Wildlife Management
courses.description: This course introduces students to the art and science of wildlife management.  This course will provide a foundation course from which students who major in Ecology and Wildlife may build a successful collegiate experience and professional career.  It will also provide insight into the wildlife discipline for non-wildlife majors.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Rangelands and Range Plants
courses.description: This course requires identification of some 200 species from the intermountain area of the west.  Successful students will be able to identify mounted specimens by common, scientific, and family names.  Species are taken from a variety of habitats. There is a mandatory field trip.

courses.title: Principles of Fish Management
courses.description: This course will provide students with a foundation of fisheries management principles. Successful fisheries scientists must be creative and be able to think critically to develop and implement fisheries management programs. Students will be introduced to the process and tools used by fisheries biologists to obtain necessary information to manage fish and their habitats. Additionally, students will have opportunities to further develop the oral and written communication techniques necessary for communicating with diverse stakeholders.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Fisheries Techniques and Analysis
courses.description: This course introduces fisheries techniques and analyses. Successful fisheries scientists must be creative and be able to think critically to develop innovative methods for completing fisheries projects. Students will be introduced to and will practice common sampling and analytical techniques fisheries biologists use to obtain necessary information to manage fish and their habitats. Additionally, students will have opportunities to develop further oral and written communication techniques necessary for communicating with diverse stakeholders.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO311 - Scientific Writing and Communication (3)

courses.title: Stream Ecology
courses.description: This course will provide you an introduction to structure and function of stream ecosystems. We will explore physical and chemical properties of running water and how these properties influence the biotic communities of running waters. The ecological focus of this course will include implications of management and policy.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3) ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Conservation Genetics
courses.description: This course will introduce students to the field of conservation genetics, which focuses on the application of genetic analyses to conservation, management and recovery of species. This course will provide expanded coverage to include application of genetic techniques to general questions in wildlife and fisheries biology and management.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Genetics and Molecular Biology
courses.description: This course consists of an investigation of the transmission of heritable material in prokaryotes and eukaryotes. Topics include classical genetics (patterns of inheritance, linkage and chromosome mapping), molecular biology (DNA structure and function, gene expression, biotechnology), and population genetics.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3) ; BIO208 - Introduction to Plant Biology (4)

courses.title: Cell and Molecular Biology
courses.description: This course covers principles, processes, and methodology of molecular and cell biology. Students will gain knowledge of interactions at the cellular level through structure and function of membranes, organelles and cytoskeletal elements, energy metabolism, signal transduction, cell cycle, cell-cell communication, and cellular movement.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3) ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Techniques in Biochemistry Molecular Biology
courses.description: This is a comprehensive laboratory course designed to familiarize students with essential laboratory techniques in molecular biology, cellular biology, genetics, and biochemistry. The course topics demand a rigorous but rewarding schedule that enables students to follow several multi-session projects from start to finish. Students successfully completing the course will find they have most of the skills necessary to work as an entry level laboratory technician.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CHEM106 - General Chemistry II (3) ; MATH325 - Intermediate Statistics (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3) ; BIO208 - Introduction to Plant Biology (4)

courses.title: Histology with Lab
courses.description: This course covers microscopic anatomy of cells and tissues and their relationship to the function of the cell.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; BIO264 - Human Anatomy and Physiology I (3) ; BIO265 - Human Anatomy and Physiology II (3) ; Take the following course(s): ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3)

courses.title: Pathophysiology
courses.description: This course is a study of the derangement of bodily function as seen in diseased states.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CHEM101 - Introductory Chemistry (3) ; CHEM105 - General Chemistry I (3) ; Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; BIO461 - Principles of Physiology (5) ; Take the following course(s): ; BIO264 - Human Anatomy and Physiology I (3) ; BIO265 - Human Anatomy and Physiology II (3)

courses.title: Bioinformatics
courses.description: This course will introduce you to bioinformatics, an exciting and relatively new field of biology.  The course will include a mixture of traditional lecture, problem solving, and hands-on practice using computational tools to solve a variety of biological problems. Topics include: database searching, sequence alignment, protein structure prediction, construction of phylogenetic trees, comparative and functional genomics.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3) ; BIO181L - Introduction to Biology II Lab (1) ; MATH221B - Biostatistics (3)

courses.title: Human Embryology
courses.description: This course is intended to provide a foundation of understanding for the processes involved in creating gametes and their participation in the process of conception.  A discussion will then continue to discover the processes important in the development of a fully formed and functional fetus.  This course will examine the cellular and morphological development of most of the major human body systems.  The study of human embryology is important to provide a logical framework for understanding structure and function in the study of anatomy and physiology.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO180 - Introduction to Biology I (3) ; BIO265 - Human Anatomy and Physiology II (3)

courses.title: Principles of Biochemistry
courses.description: Principles of Biochemistry is a one-semester course in Biochemistry with topics in enzymology, bioenergetics, chemical and physical structure of carbohydrates, lipids, and amino acids, and their metabolism in the body. The course is intended for students majoring in biology and biomedical sciences, and those preparing for graduate work in the biological and medical sciences.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3) ; FS350 - Food Chemistry (3) ; Take the following course(s): ; CHEM106 - General Chemistry II (3)

courses.title: Range and Wildland Restoration
courses.description: Restoration ecology is the study of the restoration of degraded and damaged ecosystems. This course will examine the current state of knowledge in this area through case studies and project design/implementation.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Range and Wildland Plant Ecology
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to elaborate on information gained in ecology (Bio 302). Students will explore plants' complex interactions with their environments, looking often to adaptations which enable species to exploit particular ecological niches. Understanding such interactions will require the incorporation of concepts drawn from various other fields including: geology, chemistry, climatology, and mathematics.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Occupational Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

This course is designed to award university credit for occupational training-based internships in any biomedical or ecological field.  This course is meant for students engaged in the operational duties of a facility.  Students wishing to engage in research-based internship training are encouraged to enroll in the department's research internship (BIO 498R).

courses.title: Readings in Biology
courses.description: This course consists of selected readings in biology.

courses.title: Immunology
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the functions of the cells and proteins that make up the immune system of the body.  The topics that will be discussed include innate immunity, structure and function of immune system molecules, the genetics of the immune system, lymphocyte development and activation, failure of immunity, and immune system diseases.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; BIO321 - Biology of Microorganisms (4) ; Take the following course(s): ; BIO221 - General Microbiology (3) ; BIO375 - Genetics and Molecular Biology (3)

courses.title: Medical Microbiology
courses.description: This course includes the study of bacteriology, mycology, and virology.  The major areas of emphasis will focus on host-parasitic interactions between humans and bacteria. Paradigms in bacterial virulence factors will be stressed.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO321 - Biology of Microorganisms (4)

courses.title: Virology
courses.description: This is an introductory course that highlights the features of many of the most common types of viruses. Emphasis is placed on the various replication strategies used by specific phage and animal viruses, as well as the interaction of these viruses with host cells.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO321 - Biology of Microorganisms (4)

courses.title: Advanced Microbiology Lab
courses.description: This course is a comprehensive laboratory experience designed to familiarize students with the essential and commonly practiced techniques in the field of microbiology.  Topics include microbial culturing, staining, and detection through biochemical, fluorescent, and serological methods, as well as experience with animal tissue culture.  Students will learn and practice common technical procedures that apply to a variety of molecular and microbiological laboratory settings. Students will develop proficiency in experimental design, aseptic technique, data analysis, record-keeping, and scientific writing.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO377 - Techniques in Biochemistry Molecular Biology (3) ; BIO321 - Biology of Microorganisms (4)

courses.title: Principles of Limnology
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the physical, chemical, and biological aspects of inland water systems with a particular focus on lakes, ponds, and reservoirs.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3) ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Natural Resources Law and Policy
courses.description: Introduction to theory, processes, and techniques for the management of natural resource based activities. Emphasis will be on site impacts and user management. In-depth analyses of legal mandates (federal and state) from a resource protection paradigm. Environmental law and evidence collection in relation to the atmosphere associated with the judicial system will be covered.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Principles of Pharmacology
courses.description: This course is designed to help Biology students understand the basic principles of pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and the clinical application of drugs. The mechanisms of drug action are emphasized to correlate physiological and pharmacological principles.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO265 - Human Anatomy and Physiology II (3) ; BIO461 - Principles of Physiology (5)

courses.title: Ichthyology
courses.description: In this course students will study the biology of fishes.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3) ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Ornithology
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth study of avian (bird) biology including evolutionary history, systematics, anatomy, physiology, behavior, and reproduction. A lab is required.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Mammalogy
courses.description: In this course, students will study mammalian diversity, systematics, evolution, anatomy, physiology, distribution, and natural history.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Fisheries and Wildlife Field Studies
courses.description: In this course, students will study rangeland ecology and vegetation measurements including condition, trend, utilization, suitability, and production.

courses.title: Human Anatomy with Lab
courses.description: This course involves regional human anatomy for Biomedical Sciences Majors. Comprehensive regional study of gross human anatomy with emphasis on the limbs, and the thoracic, abdominal, and pelvic cavities will be covered.

courses.title: Principles of Physiology
courses.description: This course is designed to give an in-depth coverage of general physiologic principles and homoeostatic mechanisms regulating human organ system function. In addition, it is hoped that students will gain an appreciation for the intricate interrelationships of the human body. Material will be presented through lectures and lab exercises as well as through independent study by the students. This is an upper-division class; therefore, it is assumed that the students will be dedicated and highly motivated to learn the material. As a precaution, one of the things that makes learning physiology difficult is the fact that everything ultimately is connected to everything else. Disturbances to one part of one system will give rise to consequences that involve many organs or organ systems. Therefore, it is imperative that we integrate information as we progressively build the human body. In addition, many of the students enrolled in this course will be going on to professional schools and the topics learned in this class will be invaluable as education is continued.  The most successful students will take an active interest in their learning and work to master as much of the course material as possible.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO180 - Introduction to Biology I (3)

courses.title: Head and Neck Anatomy
courses.description: This course introduced Biology Majors to the anatomy of the human head and neck. Comprehensive, in depth study of the development, organization and relationships of the anatomical structures of the head and neck will be covered.  The lecture component of the course introduces the content, while the lab allows the opportunity to study the regions of interest from models, atlases, and from dissected cadavers.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO460 - Human Anatomy with Lab (4) ; BIO264 - Human Anatomy and Physiology I (3)

courses.title: Rangeland Inventory and Improvement
courses.description: In this course, students will learn how to inventory rangeland plant communities by determining represented species and their relative abundance and distribution.   The course will also present principles of assessing the health of a range community and teach both principles and practices of manipulating plant communities to improve overall range health.  Techniques include: prescribed fire, biological control, herbicide treatments, mechanical treatments, and manipulation by herbivory. Economic considerations of these techniques are investigated.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO225 - Range Management (3) ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4)

courses.title: Evolutionary Science
courses.description: In this course, basic Darwinian evolution and the history of evolutionary thought is presented. This course includes the study of the scientific processes through which both microevolution and macroevolution occur, the history of life on earth, phylogenetics, cladistics, molecular evolution, sexual selection, population genetics, and rates of evolution.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3) ; BIO208 - Introduction to Plant Biology (4)

courses.title: Advanced Neuroscience
courses.description: In this course, students will study the fundamentals of Neuroscience which covers neuroanatomy, cellular and molecular neuroscience, development of the nervous system, sensory systems, motor systems, regulatory systems, and behavioral and cognitive neuroscience.  The associated lab offers students the chance to perform hands-on experiments involving modern neuroscience techniques using state-of-the-art equipment and protocols.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; BIO240 - Neurobiology (4)

courses.title: Special Problems
courses.description: This course is determined by consultation with a faculty mentor.

courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: A capstone course in which participants discuss topics related to the practice of scientific writing. Each participant produces a written review paper or research proposal, and other relevant support documents such as a letter of application and a curriculum vitae.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO302 - Ecology I (4) ; BIO181 - Introduction to Biology II (3)

courses.title: Research and Occupational Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

This course is designed to award university credit for research-based internships in any biomedical or ecological field. This course is meant for students engaged in laboratory or field research. Students wishing to engage in occupational training (i.e., working in a doctor's office) are encouraged to enroll in the department's occupational internship (BIO 398).

courses.title: Undergraduate Research
courses.description: This course is designed to award University credit for student mentored research on the BYU-I campus by a faculty member in the Biology Department.

courses.title: Business Exploration and Orientation
courses.description: Explores business-related majors and career options. Guides students in using campus resources to successfully choose a major, navigate academic requirements, prepare a four-year graduation plan, and prepare for internships and careers.

courses.title: Exploration of Business and Communication Professions
courses.description: Students in this course will explore and participate in activities, in-class learning games, and assignments that introduce them to decisions made by professionals in communication and areas of business such as marketing, operations, finance, analytics, and management.  Students will get an in-depth look at what a career in these business-related fields is like on a day-to-day basis. They will begin building a map leading to career success that will include steps like networking, crafting a great resume, and honing their interviewing skills.  The course is designed specifically for Freshman Focus Group-designated students.

courses.title: Introduction to Entrepreneurship
courses.description: This course offers an introduction on how to develop a clear vision of what matters most to students as they begin their entrepreneurial journey. The course will also deliver practical life lessons and fundamental business tools required to become a successful entrepreneur. Students will develop some important mindsets in the area of thinking, learning and doing what the financially successful entrepreneurs do.

courses.title: Applied Spreadsheets and Analysis
courses.description: Develops spreadsheet analysis skills for business applications. Teaches students to analyze data, create financial models, and develop business solutions. Emphasizes real-world business scenarios and professional spreadsheet applications.

courses.title: Office Procedures
courses.description: This course develops business operations skills needed for professional office environments. Students master time management strategies, professional communication techniques, and systematic records management practices. Through practical scenarios, students learn to plan effective meetings, document key business decisions, and implement customer service solutions.

courses.title: Small Business Management
courses.description: Prepares students to approach various situations that small business managers confront every day and to contribute in a meaningful way to small businesses. Students use case studies to analyze, discuss, and solve real-world business problems that require understanding multiple aspects and functions of business.

courses.title: Small Business Creation
courses.description: This course introduces students to the basics of small business creation. It helps them understand the importance of creating systems and exposes them to the many career opportunities available in the field of entrepreneurship. Students learn about startups, buying existing businesses, franchises, and family-run businesses. Through class discussions, entrepreneur cases, guest entrepreneurs, selected readings, and team projects, students will gain a clear understanding of entrepreneur opportunities.  Each student will participate in actually starting a microbusiness during the semester, drafting a one-page business plan on their own big idea, and networking with entrepreneur mentors to support their entrepreneurial idea.

courses.title: Word Processing
courses.description: This course develops business document creation skills using industry-standard word processing tools. Through hands-on projects, students create reports, visual components, and correspondence that elevate organizational professionalism and streamline business communication.

courses.title: Human Resource Management
courses.description: This course is an overview of human resource management topics such as diversity, EEOC laws, recruiting, training, performance management, compensation and benefits, motivation, workplace organizational design, difficult interactions, employee relations, and safety. The course also considers organizational behavior topics in the context of human resource management such as teamwork, power dynamics, innovation, and groupthink. The course leverages case studies and professional/scholarly articles to gain a better understanding of real-life workplace challenges.

courses.title: Project-Based Internship
courses.description:
The Project-Based Internship (PBI) program provides students with an internship-like experience by working in teams of four to six on real-world projects for client organizations. Projects span a wide range of industries and are applicable to all majors.

Interns must meet weekly with their team and client at scheduled times. Students are expected to dedicate 8 to 10 hours per week throughout the semester, totaling a minimum of 100 hours. While PBI projects are completed remotely rather than at the client's office, the experience closely mirrors a part-time business internship.

The program begins with training sessions or recordings during the first three weeks. Project assignments are based on student interests, skills, and availability.

This course is available to both online and on-campus students. If you register for BUS 297R, it may or may not fulfill the basic internship requirement for your major.

For more information, visit https://www.byui.edu/internships/project-based-internships

courses.title: Beginning Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap. 

Students must be registered for this course within the first two weeks of the semester they are completing the internship.  For more information on how to register for an internship see your I-Plan homepage. This course is designed for students working full or part-time in business-related employment to gain introductory experience and understanding of the functions of a successful company.  Students must complete application and approval through the College of Business and Communication Career Services, contract with their employer to work for college credits, and work a minimum of 15 hours per week for a minimum of seven weeks.  Other requirements include writing reports, submitting self- and supervisor evaluations, and adhering to BYU-Idaho standards and policies. During their internship students will gain a greater vision of becoming a business professional and establishing career networking contacts. Students can earn 1 to 3 credits, receive compensation and letters of recommendation from their employer.

courses.title: IBC Business Basics
courses.description: This course allows students to learn principles of business basics through experiential learning in a student-run business environment known as the Integrated Business Core or I.B.C. Concepts to be applied and explored include general management, financial management, operations management, and continuous improvement.

courses.title: Advanced Writing in Professional Contexts
courses.description: Introduces the fundamentals of rhetorical principles and writing practices using a number of typical business situations. Students produce effective business letters, memos, reports, and employment packages -- some of which will be created independently and some of which will involve collaborative efforts. This prepares students for the demands of business careers that require significant time reading, drafting, and revising written communication.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: IBC Business Leadership
courses.description: This course allows students to learn principles of Business Leadership through experiential learning in a student-run business environment known as the Integrated Business Core or I.B.C. Concepts to be applied and explored include disciple leadership, emotional intelligence, motivation, and personal development.

courses.title: Project Management
courses.description: The Project Management Course equips students with the skills to lead teams, manage projects, and drive organizational success. Students will develop leadership competencies like ethical decision-making, strategic thinking, and emotional intelligence, while mastering project management methodologies to balance scope, time, and resources. The program emphasizes communication, collaboration, and problem-solving, preparing graduates to navigate complex challenges and align project outcomes with organizational goals.

courses.title: Launching New Ventures
courses.description:
This course is designed as an introduction to the process of perceiving an opportunity and creating an organization to pursue it.  Working alone and in teams students will learn to plan, finance, launch, manage, and harvest a new venture. In order to integrate ideas across departments and colleges, this course will be open to students in engineering, computer science, and business management.  All students who desire to lead a business plan team will have an opportunity to describe their ventures in the early class sessions to facilitate team member recruiting.  Class discussion, readings, lectures, and projects are learning tools. A student's project is developed throughout this course and involves completing a new venture plan and financial forecast.  Each team business plan also becomes a live case for the purposes of class discussion.

Ideally, a student will have completed BUS 210 before moving on to BUS 310.

courses.title: Organizational Leadership
courses.description: Addresses organizational effectiveness at three levels: individual, group, and organizational. Covers motivation, teams, group behavior, organizational design, structure, culture, communication, leadership, decision-making, and managing change.

courses.title: Social Innovation
courses.description: This course is intended to help students become better disciple leaders by Doing Good, Better. Learn how to become a change maker and embrace some element of the social spectrum -- anything from working for a non-profit to starting a hybrid or social business. Covers the broad spectrum of how individuals and organizations are solving the world's greatest problems in new and innovative ways. Understand the different ways to make a difference in the world when the opportunity presents itself to give back. Learn about the broad spectrum of social innovation including: non-profits, social businesses, NGO's, impact investing, philanthropy, and corporate social responsibility. Hybrid class; all course content will be completed outside of class.

courses.title: Business Law
courses.description: This course is an introduction to legal environment in which businesses operate as well as an overview of laws impacting business.  Topics include understanding the legal system, contracts, ethics, intellectual property, antitrust, employment, business organizations, and securities.

courses.title: International Business
courses.description: Provides an overview of international business with an emphasis on global trade and investment. Topics include cultural, political, legal, and economic environments and their effect on marketing, production, and human resource management strategy.

courses.title: Advanced Business Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

Required for all Business Management students. Students must be registered for this course within the first two weeks of the semester they are completing the internship. For more information on how to register for an internship see your I-Plan home page. Students will find a professional business management internship in an approved business, complete the application and obtain approval through the College of Business and Communication Career Services, be enrolled in the course, write reports, submit evaluations, and complete at least 270 hours of work in seven weeks or more. During their internship students will gain a greater vision of becoming a business professional and establish career networking links. Students will earn 1 to 3 credits and may receive compensation from the employer and letters of recommendation from both the employer and BYU-Idaho.

courses.title: Special Projects
courses.description: An arranged research or special project course. Contact the department for registration information.

courses.title: Principles of Advanced Business Management
courses.description: This capstone course examines management, entrepreneurship, and leadership principles through business case analysis. Students develop analytical, quantitative, entrepreneurial, and critical thinking skills while addressing common business challenges.

courses.title: Principles of Business Strategy
courses.description: This course is a business strategy capstone experience for junior-senior level students focusing on theories of strategy and problem solving through the case method. Emphasis in the course is focused on students understanding the causal mechanisms of strategic problems businesses encounter. Students will recommend solutions using problem-framing, analysis, and strategy that aim to address identified causes and produce the predicted outcomes.

courses.title: Experience BYU-Idaho
courses.description:
New BYU-Idaho students must take this course during their first semester. 

A primary purpose of BYU-Idaho is to help students grow and develop into disciples of Jesus Christ. This course focuses on developing discipleship by helping students learn what it means to be a BYU-Idaho student and invites them to join our learning community, learning about campus resources to find help when confronted with challenges, and teaching them the foundational skills to become a disciple learner.

courses.title: Sustaining Human Life
courses.description: This course is a focused major and career exploration class. It will cover majors and careers in Agriculture and Life Science. By the end of the semester, students should be able to determine a major that works well for them and how that major will translate into a productive career.

courses.title: Mission Impossible
courses.description: This course is a focused major and career exploration class. It will cover majors and careers in Business and Communication. By the end of the semester, students should be able to determine a major that works well for them and how that major will translate into a productive career.

courses.title: Intelligent Life
courses.description: This course is a focused major and career exploration class. It will cover majors and careers in Education and Human Development. By the end of the semester, students should be able to determine a major that works well for them and how that major will translate into a productive career.

courses.title: The Heroic Journey
courses.description: This course is a focused major and career exploration class. It will cover majors and careers in Language and Letters. By the end of the semester, students should be able to determine a major that works well for them and how that major will translate into a productive career.

courses.title: Mission to Mars
courses.description: This course is a focused major and career exploration class. It will cover majors and careers in Physical Science and Engineering. By the end of the semester, students should be able to determine a major that works well for them and how that major will translate into a productive career.

courses.title: Thriving in a Complex World
courses.description: This course is a  major and career exploration class. It will cover general areas that may be of interest to students in hopes of helping them select either a major or a general area to explore. By the end of the semester, students should be able to determine a major that works well for them or at least an area to focus on to find a suitable major.

courses.title: Introduction to Civil Engineering A
courses.description: Explores the geotechnical and water resources disciplines within civil engineering and aspects of professional engineering practice. Exposure to civil engineering design through group-based projects. The course includes strategies for success as an engineering student.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME101 - Introduction to Engineering and Technology (1)

courses.title: Introduction to Civil Engineering B
courses.description: Explores the transportation and structural disciplines within civil engineering and aspects of professional engineering practice. Provides exposure to civil engineering design through group-based projects. Introduces strategies for success as an engineering student.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME101 - Introduction to Engineering and Technology (1) ; CE161 - Fundamentals in 2D CADD (3)

courses.title: Fundamentals in 2D CADD
courses.description: Computer aided drafting and design using AutoCAD software. Topics include coordinate systems, display control, basic geometric construction and editing, scales, layer, annotation and dimensions, blocks, attributes, plotting.  Applications in mechanical, civil, electrical, and architectural disciplines.

courses.title: Land Surveying
courses.description: Introduces fundamental surveying principles and techniques, including field data collection using modern equipment. Develops students' ability to analyze survey data, maps, and plans and apply surveying principles to solve real-world engineering problems. Builds communication and teamwork skills for careers in civil and construction engineering.
courses.corequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; MATH109 - Precalculus (5) ; CE161 - Fundamentals in 2D CADD (3) ; Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3) ; MATH111 - Trigonometry (2) ; CE161 - Fundamentals in 2D CADD (3) ; Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; CE161 - Fundamentals in 2D CADD (3) ; CE161 and (ACT 27 or SAT 620 or 2016 SAT 640 or ALEKS 85)

courses.title: Civil Engineering Materials Lab
courses.description: Provides hands-on experience testing civil engineering materials, including wood, aggregates, concrete, asphalt, and steel. Guides students in performing ASTM and AASHTO standard tests to evaluate material properties, interpret results, and apply findings to engineering problems. Emphasizes safety, sustainability, and professional reporting.

courses.title: Civil Engineering Materials Science
courses.description: Learn the basics of materials engineering, including how materials behave, how the environment affects them, and the main types of materials. This course covers the properties and testing methods for important materials used in civil engineering, such as steel, aluminum, concrete, asphalt, wood, masonry, aggregates, and composites.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM105 - General Chemistry I (3) ; ME202 - Strength of Materials (3)

courses.title: Structural Analysis
courses.description: Structural engineering loads and basic structural systems. Analysis of statically determinate and indeterminate structures.  Deflection analysis of simple structures. Computer analysis of structures.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME142 - Engineering Computation (3) ; ME202 - Strength of Materials (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; MATH316 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra (4)

courses.title: Elementary Soil Mechanics
courses.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of soil mechanics and their applications in civil engineering. Covers soil classification, permeability, compaction, shear strength, consolidation, and stress distribution. Emphasizes understanding soil behavior, applying laboratory test results, and solving practical geotechnical engineering problems. Determination of stresses in soils, soil strength, consolidation, and settlement. Applications in fluid flow, lateral earth pressure, bearing pressure, and slope stability.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME202 - Strength of Materials (3) ; CE210 - Civil Engineering Materials Lab (2)

courses.title: Environmental Engineering
courses.description: Introduces students to environmental engineering, including natural processes in the environment and the effects of human activities on these processes. Describes methods and structures used to improve and maintain the environment, protect human health, protect natural ecosystems, and enhance quality of life.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM105 - General Chemistry I (3)

courses.title: Fluid Mechanics for Civil Engineers
courses.description: Introduces fluid properties, the mechanics of incompressible fluids, and the machines that add or remove energy from pressurized and open-channel systems. Covers incompressible fluid flow, fluid statics, fluid dynamics, control volume analysis of fluid flow, internal and external viscous flow, friction and minor losses, hydraulic and energy gradelines, turbomachinery, and open-channel flow.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME204 - Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics (3)

courses.title: Introduction to Transport Engineering
courses.description: Transportation system characteristics, traffic engineering, traffic operations, transportation planning, and public transport.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME142 - Engineering Computation (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; MATH330 - Engineering Statistics (3)

courses.title: Hydrology
courses.description: Explores the principles and processes governing water movement through the hydrologic cycle. Applies hydrologic statistics and frequency analysis techniques, supplemented by current software, to engineering hydrologic design problems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH330 - Engineering Statistics (3)

courses.title: Structural Steel Design
courses.description: Design of structural steel building members and connections based on current design specifications. Determination and application of code-specified vertical and lateral loads on steel structures.
