courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CE321 - Structural Analysis (3)

courses.title: Reinforced Concrete Design
courses.description: Design of reinforced concrete building components, including columns, beams, slabs, and footings based on ACI 318.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CE321 - Structural Analysis (3) ; CE341 - Elementary Soil Mechanics (3) ; CE310 - Civil Engineering Materials Science (3)

courses.title: Design of Wood Structures
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the design of wood structures. It deals with the fundamentals of structural design as governed by the International Building Code and the National Design Specification for Wood Structures. The course focuses on the behavior of wood structures under loads, the design of major structural components, and the design of wood connections.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CE424 - Reinforced Concrete Design (3)

courses.title: Water Resources Engineering
courses.description: Applies principles of fluid mechanics, hydraulics, hydrology, and environmental engineering to manage water resources and meet human and environmental needs. Analyzes and designs hydraulic structures and systems used in modern society to collect, transport, store, and regulate water.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CE351 - Environmental Engineering (3) ; CE360 - Fluid Mechanics for Civil Engineers (3)

courses.title: Geotechnical Engineering Design
courses.description: Focuses on applying soil mechanics principles to geotechnical engineering design. Covers slope stability analysis and design considerations for shallow foundations, deep foundations (piles and drilled shafts), and retaining walls. Emphasizes practical design approaches, engineering judgment, and solving real-world geotechnical problems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CE341 - Elementary Soil Mechanics (3)

courses.title: Water and Wastewater Treatment Process Design
courses.description: Covers the fundamental principles, theory, and design of water and wastewater treatment processes.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CE351 - Environmental Engineering (3)

courses.title: Geometric Design of Highways
courses.description: Design of highway systems including design criteria and controls, horizontal and vertical alignments, cross-sections, clear zone, signing and striping, pavements, and plan set creation.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; CE161 - Fundamentals in 2D CADD (3) ; CE361 - Introduction to Transport Engineering (3)AND ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CE162 - Land Surveying (3) ; CONST340 - Land Surveying (3)

courses.title: Civil Engineering Practice and Design
courses.description: Application of acquired knowledge and skills towards completing a team-based engineering capstone design project. Various professional practice topics are included to prepare students to enter the civil engineering industry.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CE361 - Introduction to Transport Engineering (3) ; CE424 - Reinforced Concrete Design (3) ; CE433 - Water Resources Engineering (4)

courses.title: Special Problems in Civil Engineering
courses.description: The special problems in civil engineering course is an elective course for the civil engineering BS degree. The course is a single-credit course offered by any faculty member. The course provides an opportunity for students to get academic credit for mentored research or to get credit for conducting faculty-supervised projects related to civil engineering.

courses.title: Special Topics in Civil Engineering
courses.description: The special topics in civil engineering course is an elective course for the civil engineering BS degree. The course is a variable credit (1 to 3 credits) course to provide an opportunity for students to get academic credit for significant mentored research projects or for faculty to teach current topics in civil engineering.

courses.title: Chemistry Connections
courses.description: This first-year course helps students explore chemistry as a major while building meaningful connections with peers, faculty, and the broader scientific community. Through engaging laboratory experiences, discussions, and career exploration activities, students will gain an understanding of chemistry subfields, academic planning, and professional opportunities. It also introduces key university resources, laboratory safety fundamentals, and problem-solving strategies to support student success in the chemistry program.

courses.title: Introductory Chemistry
courses.description: Introduces fundamental concepts of chemistry for students preparing for studies in nursing, agriculture, exercise physiology, health science, and other disciplines that require a one-semester introduction to chemistry.
courses.corequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; MATH108X - Math for the Real World (3) ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; MATH119 - Applied Calculus for Data Analysis (4) ; ECON215 - Quantitative Methods (4) ; MATH221A - Business Statistics (3) ; MATH221B - Biostatistics (3) ; MATH221C - Social Science Statistics (3) ; MATH221D - Introductory Statistics with R (3) ; The math requirement will be waived with an ALEKS score of 53 or higher. ; The math requirement will be waived with an ACT score of 23 or higher. ; The math requirement will be waived with an SAT score of 540 or higher. ; The math requirement will be waived with an SATR (SAT 2016 version) of 570 or higher.

courses.title: Introductory Chemistry Lab
courses.description: CHEM 101L is an introductory laboratory course designed to accompany CHEM 101 at BYU-Idaho. For this laboratory experience, students will meet at the designated time for 3 hours. This course will provide students with opportunities to address chemistry related questions, to generate data, and to compile/analyze the data to form conclusions. This process will largely take place in a collaborative environment. This laboratory will also serve to reinforce concepts in CHEM 101.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; CHEM101 - Introductory Chemistry (3)

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: This is the first semester of a two-semester course designed to meet the general chemistry requirements in engineering, science, and pre-professional majors.
courses.corequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; MATH109 - Precalculus (5) ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3) ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; MATH113 - Calculus II (3) ; MATH119 - Applied Calculus for Data Analysis (4) ; The math requirement can be waived with an ALEKS score of 70 or higher.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: This is a laboratory course designed to accompany Chemistry105.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; CHEM105 - General Chemistry I (3)

courses.title: General Chemistry II
courses.description: This is the second in a two-semester course designed to meet the general chemistry requirements in engineering, science, and pre-professional majors.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; CHEM105 - General Chemistry I (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; MATH109 - Precalculus (5) ; MATH113 - Calculus II (3) ; MATH119 - Applied Calculus for Data Analysis (4) ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3) ; The math requirement can be waived with an ALEKS score of 70 or higher.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: This is a laboratory course designed to accompany Chemistry106.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM105L - General Chemistry Laboratory I (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; CHEM106 - General Chemistry II (3)

courses.title: Quantitative Analysis
courses.description: This is a first-semester analytical chemistry course that emphasizes quantitative analytical techniques, laboratory instruments, and data evaluation. Course topics include solutions, experimental error, statistics and calibration curves, quality assurance, complex chemical equilibria and activities, acids and bases, titrations, electrochemistry, spectroscopy, and chromatography.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM106 - General Chemistry II (3)

courses.title: Quantitative Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: A first-semester analytical chemistry laboratory that emphasizes quantitative analytical techniques in the laboratory, an introduction to instrumental analysis, and supportive chemical principles and laboratory techniques. Topics include glassware, solutions, experimental error, standard addition, gravimetric analysis, calibration curves, potentiometry, acids and bases, titrations, spectroscopy, and chromatography.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM106 - General Chemistry II (3) ; CHEM106L - General Chemistry Laboratory II (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; CHEM220 - Quantitative Analysis (3)

courses.title: Introductory Organic and Biochemistry
courses.description: A one-semester introduction to the chemical properties of functional groups, principles of organic and biochemical reactions, DNA and RNA structure and function, major metabolic pathways, and cellular signaling. Students who also need an organic and biological chemistry laboratory should concurrently register for CHEM 250L.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; CHEM101 - Introductory Chemistry (3) ; CHEM105 - General Chemistry I (3)

courses.title: Introductory Organic and Biochemistry Lab
courses.description: This course is a laboratory experience that explores principles and techniques in the areas of spectroscopic analysis, organic synthesis, separations, aseptic techniques, DNA cloning, protein expression, and protein purification.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; CHEM101L - Introductory Chemistry Lab (1) ; CHEM105L - General Chemistry Laboratory I (1)

courses.title: Special Topics in Chemistry
courses.description: This course develops skills required for entry into specialized sub-disciplines in chemistry. Various faculty offer courses related to their respective areas of expertise. Contact the Department of Chemistry for details regarding current course topics.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM105 - General Chemistry I (3)

courses.title: Organic Chemistry I
courses.description: The first semester of a year-long sequence that involves the principles and theories of organic chemistry, including the properties, preparation, and reactions of organic compounds. The course is designed for students in majors such as Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Pre-medicine, Pre-dentistry, Pre-pharmacy, Pre-veterinary, and Biology.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM106 - General Chemistry II (3)

courses.title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: The first semester of a year-long laboratory experience that involves the principles and theories of organic chemistry, including the properties, preparation, and reactions of organic compounds. The course is designed for students in majors such as Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Pre-medicine, Pre-dentistry, Pre-pharmacy, Pre-veterinary, and Biology.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM106L - General Chemistry Laboratory II (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; CHEM351 - Organic Chemistry I (3)

courses.title: Organic Chemistry II
courses.description: The second semester of a year-long sequence that involves the principles and theories of organic chemistry including the properties, preparation, and reactions of organic compounds. The course is designed for students in majors such as Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Pre-medicine, Pre-dentistry, Pre-pharmacy, Pre-veterinary, and Biology.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM351 - Organic Chemistry I (3)

courses.title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: The second semester of a year-long laboratory experience that involves the principles and theories of organic chemistry including the properties, preparation, and reactions of organic compounds. The course is designed for students in majors such as Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Pre-medicine,Pre-dentistry, Pre-pharmacy, Pre-veterinary, and Biology.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM351 - Organic Chemistry I (3) ; CHEM351L - Organic Chemistry Laboratory I (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; CHEM352 - Organic Chemistry II (3)

courses.title: Physical Biochemistry
courses.description: This course will provide an introduction to physical biochemistry through the application of physical laws of chemistry to biological systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; CHEM351 - Organic Chemistry I (3)

courses.title: Technical Writing in Chemical Literature
courses.description: This course provides instruction and experience in advanced writing techniques for students planning careers in chemistry, biochemistry, or related scientific disciplines. The course will help students do the following: 1) prepare for further chemistry courses that require scientific writing as a part of their curriculum, 2) search the chemical literature using relevant database tools, 3) develop practical experience in writing for a professional, technical audience, 4) and become more effective written communicators in their future scientific careers. This course is a prerequisite for CHEM 220, CHEM 464, and CHEM 471.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM106 - General Chemistry II (3)

courses.title: Instrumental Analysis
courses.description: This is a second semester analytical chemistry course that builds upon and reinforces principles and concepts introduced in CHEM 220 Quantitative Analysis (e.g., the analytical process, data collection, and data analysis). Emphasis will be placed on the theories and applications of modern chemical instrumentation in the areas of spectroscopy, separations, mass spectrometry, and electrochemistry. The correct use and selection of chemical instrumentation for the purpose of solving chemical problems will be investigated.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM220 - Quantitative Analysis (3) ; CHEM352 - Organic Chemistry II (3) ; PH250 - Intermediate Physics Lab (1)

courses.title: Instrumental Analysis Lab
courses.description: This course will serve as the accompanying lab to Instrumental Analysis (CHEM 420). Students will gain hands-on experience using a selection of instruments to solve chemical problems. Laboratory experiments will include the use of the following: inductively coupled plasma spectrometer, ultraviolet/visible light spectrophotometer, spectrofluorometer, Fourier transform infrared spectrometer, gas chromatograph mass spectrometer, liquid chromatograph, capillary electrophoresis instrument, and a potentiostat.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM220L - Quantitative Analysis Laboratory (2) ; PH250 - Intermediate Physics Lab (1)

courses.title: Quantum Chemistry and Spectroscopy
courses.description: This course provides a theoretical and mathematical description of the physical behavior of chemical systems and covers mathematical methods, quantum chemistry, and spectroscopy.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM351 - Organic Chemistry I (3) ; PH223 - Engineering Physics (4) ; MATH215 - Multivariable Calculus (4)

courses.title: Statistical Mechanics, Chemical Thermodynamics, and Kinetics
courses.description: This course provides a theoretical and mathematical description of the physical behavior of chemical systems and covers mathematical methods, statistical mechanics, thermodynamics, and kinetics.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM351 - Organic Chemistry I (3) ; PH223 - Engineering Physics (4) ; MATH215 - Multivariable Calculus (4)

courses.title: Physical Chemistry Lab
courses.description: In this course, students will gain laboratory experience with modern instrumentation in performing physical chemistry experiments, and practice scientific writing.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM220 - Quantitative Analysis (3) ; PH250 - Intermediate Physics Lab (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; CHEM462 - Statistical Mechanics, Chemical Thermodynamics, and Kinetics (4)

courses.title: Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: This course involves a study of structure, physical and chemical behavior, and bond theory as applied to inorganic chemistry. A variety of inorganic systems will be analyzed in a systematic and detailed fashion through using concepts, models, and experimental data.  Underlying trends in both the elements and also their compounds will be explored and identified.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM461 - Quantum Chemistry and Spectroscopy (4)

courses.title: Advanced Laboratory
courses.description: This laboratory course includes exercises in the preparation and purification of inorganic compounds utilizing modern synthetic techniques and equipment.  Characterization of inorganic compounds will be performed by modern spectroscopic techniques such as nuclear magnetic resonance, UV-vis, infrared, and magnetic susceptibility.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; CHEM470 - Inorganic Chemistry (3)

courses.title: Biochemistry I
courses.description: The first course in a two-semester series in which students explore the structure and function of proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, and nucleic acids.  The course is intended for students majoring in chemistry, biochemistry or biology, and those preparing for advanced studies in graduate or professional schools.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM351 - Organic Chemistry I (3)

courses.title: Advanced Biochemistry Laboratory
courses.description: An advanced laboratory experience that explores the physical and chemical properties of major classes of biomolecules, spectroscopic characterization of biomolecules, DNA cloning techniques, and protein separation methods.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; CHEM220L - Quantitative Analysis Laboratory (2) ; CHEM250L - Introductory Organic and Biochemistry Lab (1) ; CHEM351L - Organic Chemistry Laboratory I (1) ; BIO377 - Techniques in Biochemistry Molecular Biology (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; CHEM481 - Biochemistry I (3)

courses.title: Biochemistry II
courses.description: The second course in a two-semester series in which students explore the metabolic  pathways of carbohydrates, lipids, amino acids, and nucleotides.  The course is intended for students majoring in chemistry, biochemistry or biology, and those preparing for advanced studies in graduate or professional schools.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHEM481 - Biochemistry I (3)

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Chemistry
courses.description: This course develops skills required for entry into graduate school or specialized fields in industry. Various faculty offer courses related to their respective areas of expertise. Contact the Department of Chemistry for details regarding current course topics.

courses.title: Student Research
courses.description: This course is a laboratory and/or field experience in which the student performs meaningful research under the mentorship of a faculty member.

courses.title: Chemistry/Biochemistry Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

All chemistry majors must find and experience a work internship. This would generally occur the semester after their junior year or during their senior year. The experience could involve working for a government agency, industry, an academic institution, or any organization that employs laboratory chemists on their staff. The student will have a contract agreement with the employer and be responsible to a faculty supervisor. Upon completion of the internship, a written report and a presentation will be made for the BYU-Idaho chemistry department as part of the requirement.

courses.title: Infants and Toddlers
courses.description: This course explores ways to foster the normal development of infants and toddlers, including physical, cognitive, social, and emotional domains of development.  Application to parenting and other caregiving situations will be investigated.

courses.title: Foundations of Early Childhood
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the early childhood profession and to the knowledge, skills, experiences, and values needed to be a competent, ethical, and effective early childhood educator in infant-toddler, preschool or after school settings. It provides an overview of the historical foundations of the early childhood profession, ethical and professional responsibilities, models of curriculum, developmentally appropriate educational practices, and components of quality programs for young children.

courses.title: Child Development
courses.description: This course is a theoretical, academically oriented course focused on the physical, cognitive, emotional, and social development of children from conception through adolescence. Students will explore the influences of family, peers, and social institutions on children's development.

courses.title: Curriculum for Young Children
courses.description: In this course students will learn the scope of the major areas of curriculum in early childhood education, focusing specifically on children ages 2–8. They will develop basic philosophy, skills, and materials needed to provide appropriate experiences for children that will foster their physical, cognitive, social, and emotional domains.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHILD150 - Foundations of Early Childhood (3) ; CHILD210 - Child Development (3)

courses.title: Fostering Development in Natural Settings
courses.description: This course focuses on understanding and exploring the natural environment as a critical element in developmental programs. Students will learn and practice addressing developmental objectives in the physical, cognitive, emotional, and social domains. They will spend a significant amount of time outdoors and demonstrate the skills needed to help others develop in a natural setting.

courses.title: Overview of the Profession
courses.description: Students will explore the career path they would like to pursue within the field of Child Development.  They will think more purposefully about what they need to do to prepare for their chosen career path.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHILD150 - Foundations of Early Childhood (3)

courses.title: Infant and Toddler Development
courses.description: This course involves an in-depth study of the child from conception to three years of age.  Students will become familiar with various theoretical perspectives in each of the developmental domains of infancy and toddlerhood. They will discuss ethical and developmental issues arising because of technological advancement and  investigate infant/toddler temperament, personality, and social/emotional development.  Students will also explore the influence of mothers and fathers, and the parenting and teaching techniques that are most appropriate for infants and toddlers.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; CHILD210 - Child Development (3) ; PSYCH201 - Developmental Psychology Lifespan (3)

courses.title: Early and Middle Child Development
courses.description: Students learn and practice applying 10 core concepts of developmental science, relevant developmental theories, and empirical research to foster optimal development of children in the physical, cognitive, emotional, and social domains.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; CHILD210 - Child Development (3) ; PSYCH201 - Developmental Psychology Lifespan (3)

courses.title: Adolescent Development
courses.description: In this course, adolescent and emerging adult experiences are examined within a developmental and social context. Contexts to be considered include family, peers, religion, community, schools, and broader cultural systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; CHILD210 - Child Development (3) ; PSYCH201 - Developmental Psychology Lifespan (3)

courses.title: Parent Education
courses.description: This course prepares students to teach parent education classes. It explores a variety of parent education programs and encourages students to think carefully and critically about parenting materials.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; FAML320 - Parenting (3)

courses.title: Observation and Assessment
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the observation and assessment of children and their environments. The course will cover methods of documentation that include informal and formal assessment and observation. Emphasis will be on ethical standards when assessing young children using standardized and authentic procedures. The selection, administration, and interpretation of observation and assessment tools and methods will be explored.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHILD150 - Foundations of Early Childhood (3) ; CHILD210 - Child Development (3)

courses.title: Experience with Young Children
courses.description: In this course students will practice and use developmental knowledge, collaboration with families and professionals, and guidance strategies to prepare and create developmentally appropriate experiences for young children (toddlers through third grade). Students will be expected to apply knowledge learned from this course in the practicum experience.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CHILD300 - Infant and Toddler Development (3) ; CHILD310 - Early and Middle Child Development (3) ; Take the following course(s): ; CHILD230 - Curriculum for Young Children (3) ; CHILD295 - Overview of the Profession (1)

courses.title: Experience with Young Children Lab
courses.description: In this course students will receive knowledge and practical hands-on experience working with toddler, preschool, or school age children both with and without special needs and their families in a campus lab setting with a home visit component.  In the lab, child focused planning will be determined by family collaboration, assessment, family identified goals and outcomes, Individualized Education Programs (IEP) identified goals and outcomes, and child interest.  This course will prepare the student to have experiential use and application of core principles, including developmentally appropriate practices, curriculum development and implementation, child guidance, observation and assessment, and collaboration with parents and others.

courses.title: Teaching Young Children
courses.description: This course focuses on curriculum development, teaching and guiding young children, and supporting young children's play, with emphasis on lead teaching skills.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHILD365 - Experience with Young Children (3)

courses.title: Teaching Young Children Lab
courses.description: This course is a second level practicum for students majoring in the AAS degree in Early Child Development.  Students will function primarily as a lead teacher in the campus laboratories, writing and implementing curriculum plans, and adapting curriculum for children with diverse abilities.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; CHILD365L - Experience with Young Children Lab (3) ; -or- ECD360L (last offered 2022)

courses.title: Special Topics in Child Studies
courses.description: This repeatable course deals with specialty areas related to the scholarly study of children.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHILD210 - Child Development (3)

courses.title: Professional Skills and Responsibilities
courses.description: This course explores the experiences, professional organizations, education, and skills that will help students be successful in child development careers.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHILD295 - Overview of the Profession (1)

courses.title: Research Methods
courses.description: This course helps students become informed consumers of social science research with an emphasis on child and family research.  This includes the skills and knowledge to answer research questions by designing a research study or by evaluating research conducted by others.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; FAML300 - Marital Dynamics (3) ; CHILD310 - Early and Middle Child Development (3)

courses.title: Program Administration
courses.description: This course explores the fundamental principles and skills for the administration of service-delivery programs for children, youth, and families. Course content includes DAP in various contexts, staff and program administration, budgeting, health and safety standards, nutrition/food services, family partnership, child maltreatment and intimate partner violence reporting, ethical guidelines, and other legal/policy guidelines.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; CHILD365L - Experience with Young Children Lab (3) ; -or- ECD350L (last offered 2022) ; -or- ECD360L (last offered 2022) ; -or- CHILD345L (last offered 2022)

courses.title: Launching into the Profession
courses.description: During this capstone course, students review disciplinary content across the five Child Development program learning outcomes and demonstrate competency through traditional assessments. Students further demonstrate the behavior of a citizen-professional by contributing to our field and program through professional engagement, service, and feedback.  Finally, students prepare to launch into the profession by finalizing a portfolio, practicing interview skills, and exploring strategies for succeeding in internships, graduate school, and careers.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHILD395 - Professional Skills and Responsibilities (1)

courses.title: Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

In this course, students arrange to work for an agency that serves children/families directly or indirectly. In their work students will apply concepts and developmental knowledge gained in major coursework to strengthen and enrich the lives of children and families, while deepening understanding and sharpening skills through hands-on experiences and professional mentoring. Students are required to serve at the internship placement for a minimum of 160 hours spread over a minimum of 8 weeks.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; CHILD440 - Program Administration (3)

courses.title: Beginning Mandarin I
courses.description: This course is a prerequisite for Chinese 102 and Chinese minor. It may also meet the requirements of other minors and clusters (check with your home program or department) and the needs of students with other interests, such as preparation to teach English in China or acquisition of a feeling about Mandarin Chinese and Chinese culture. This course assumes that students have NO training in Mandarin Chinese. The emphasis is, therefore, on developing the basic communicative skills.

courses.title: Beginning Mandarin II
courses.description: Continued emphasis on basic language skills.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHIN101 - Beginning Mandarin I (4)

courses.title: Intermediate Mandarin I
courses.description: This course is a prerequisite for Chinese 202 and Chinese minor. It may also meet the requirements of other minors and clusters (check with your home program or department) and the needs of students with other interests, such as a preparation to teach English in China.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHIN102 - Beginning Mandarin II (4)

courses.title: Intermediate Mandarin II
courses.description: Intermediate Mandarin Chinese language skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Mandarin-speaking returned missionaries are encouraged to begin with this course.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHIN201 - Intermediate Mandarin I (4)

courses.title: Advanced Mandarin I
courses.description: Focuses on the development of oral fluency, discourse grammar, and advanced reading skills.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHIN202 - Intermediate Mandarin II (4)

courses.title: Advanced Mandarin II
courses.description: Focuses on the development of oral fluency, discourse grammar, and advanced reading skills.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHIN202 - Intermediate Mandarin II (4)

courses.title: Chinese Culture
courses.description: This course consists of an examination of Chinese culture from ancient to modern times. Topics vary, but may include: geography, history, politics, family, social issues, religion, language, literature, and thought.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: Topics in Advanced Chinese
courses.description: Focuses on the development of oral fluency, discourse grammar, and advanced reading skills.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHIN202 - Intermediate Mandarin II (4)

courses.title: Chinese Teaching Methods
courses.description: Chinese teaching skills and theories of second language acquisition.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHIN302 - Advanced Mandarin II (3)

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Mandarin Chinese I
courses.description: Continued learning on advanced language skills. Semester in Beijing students only.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 2 of the following courses: ; CHIN301 - Advanced Mandarin I (3) ; CHIN302 - Advanced Mandarin II (3) ; CHIN347 - Topics in Advanced Chinese (3)

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Mandarin Chinese II
courses.description: Continued learning on advanced language skills. Semester in Beijing students only.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 2 of the following courses: ; CHIN301 - Advanced Mandarin I (3) ; CHIN302 - Advanced Mandarin II (3) ; CHIN347 - Topics in Advanced Chinese (3)

courses.title: Independent Study in Chinese
courses.description: Independent projects monitored through periodic conferences and assessments by instructor.  Instructor approval required for registration.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CHIN202 - Intermediate Mandarin II (4)

courses.title: Introduction to Excel
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the use of spreadsheets in business. Emphasis is on learning spreadsheet literacy concepts and a popular spreadsheet application to solve business problems.

courses.title: Operating Systems I
courses.description: This course provides a fundamental understanding of computer operating systems focusing on Linux.

courses.title: Operating Systems II
courses.description: This course provides students with the administration skills to plan, install/configure, manage, and troubleshoot a Windows Server Environment.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CYBER240 - Networking (3)

courses.title: Principles of Citizenship and Constitutional Government
courses.description: Develops the civic virtues expected of disciples of Jesus Christ.  While grounded in principles of the US Constitution, the course prepares students to become leaders who collaborate to build and improve their societies wherever they live.

courses.title: Introduction to Communication
courses.description: Provides information about different areas of study in the Department of Communication.  Practicum options are discussed as well as department requirements, general advising, resume planning, and faculty mentor services.

courses.title: Public Speaking
courses.description: Explores the fundamental principles and practices of effective informative and persuasive speeches.  This course examines basic elements of public speaking, including increasing speaker confidence, ethics of speaking, audience analysis and adaptation, appropriate methods of delivery, researching supporting materials, effective use of presentational aids, and effective outlining and delivery of speeches.

courses.title: Writing for Communication Career
courses.description: This course builds basic writing competence and other skills needed for today's media and communication careers.

courses.title: Visual Media
courses.description: Students will gain skills in visual communication as they learn, analyze and apply principles of design, typography, color, and photography to create various design projects. These skills enhance all types of business, education, church, community, and personal pursuits.

courses.title: Mass Media and Society
courses.description: This course surveys historical and contemporary mass media and examines their current situation and trends, with particular emphasis on concurrent impacts between the media and society.  Principal media theory is also explored.

courses.title: Interpersonal Theory and Practice
courses.description: Examines the basic elements and theory of human communication in a practical, relevant setting. Explores varied facets of interpersonal processes with an emphasis on improving communication skills and interpersonal relationships.

courses.title: Digital Media Brand Strategy
courses.description: The Digital Media Brand Strategy course, foundational to our new Digital and Social Media Certificate program, is an in-depth exploration of brand management strategies within the digital space. This course begins with a thorough grounding in strategic digital media brand principles, teaching students to effectively define, differentiate, and position a brand. Offering a blend of theory and practical application, students undertake a final project synthesizing course concepts and designing a strategic comprehensive brand management plan for a selected brand. This course prepares students for various roles in the rapidly evolving digital and social media landscape, filling a critical skills gap in the industry.

courses.title: PR Principles and Writing
courses.description: This course explores the history, principles, and practices of effective public relations. Students learn the necessities of persuasion, ethics, and credibility in public relations work across a variety of industries. Students will learn to write and produce professional-caliber public relations work across a variety of styles and platforms aimed at promoting a range of public relations efforts. Related assignments are provided for students to demonstrate these principles.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM111 - Writing for Communication Career (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; COMM140 - Mass Media and Society (3)

courses.title: Newsgathering Principles and Practices
courses.description: This course introduces the basics of newsgathering, reporting, and traditional journalism for print, broadcast, and the Internet.  It teaches how to make money as an independent journalist through blogging and free-lance writing.  It focuses on the ethics and culture of professional journalism.  Reporting techniques including interviewing, beat reporting, and basic research are included in the course. In essence, this course teaches students how to write, think, and research as a reporter would.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM111 - Writing for Communication Career (3)

courses.title: Organizational Principles
courses.description: This course is an analysis of communication principles and practices in organizations from a theoretical perspective. Students will review career opportunities in the field after learning methods to improve communication practices.

courses.title: Video Principles and Practices
courses.description:
This course is an introduction to today's disciplines and skills in video and audio production, television and radio broadcasting, digital and online media, and allied fields. Professional guest speakers theoretical explanations and hands-on lab training with the Adobe Creative Suite for video provide students with career preparation. 
Laptop/Adobe CC required

courses.title: Video and Film Production Essentials
courses.description: Students will study and practice intermediate video production techniques.  Students will learn the operation of field and studio equipment to enhance video production skills.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM260 - Video Principles and Practices (3)

courses.title: Professional Presentations
courses.description: This course explores key principles and skills that will facilitate a student's move from competency in presentations to excellence in professional presentations.  This course will emphasize audience-centered strategies in the planning, creating, slide design, and delivery of a variety of realistic presentations in a range of professional environments, including conference room, lecture hall, and local business settings.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM102 - Public Speaking (3)

courses.title: Communication Research Fundamentals
courses.description: This course explores communication research, clear thinking, and clear presentation. At its core, the course teaches skills that enable students to analyze and present data in clear and actionable ways -- that is, the course teaches students to become data storytellers. The course explores communication theory, research methods, sampling, basic stats like regression, clear writing, and identifying quality sources. It provides teaching towards basic proficiency in Excel, in Datawrapper, and in writing. The course provides insight into communication research for careers and life.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; COMM111 - Writing for Communication Career (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH108X - Math for the Real World (3) ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3) ; MATH221A - Business Statistics (3) ; MATH221B - Biostatistics (3) ; MATH221C - Social Science Statistics (3) ; MATH325 - Intermediate Statistics (3)

courses.title: Communication Practicum I
courses.description:
This course gives students experience in the various aspects and fields of professional communication by applying principles learned in their coursework to outside-of-class projects and work environments. Projects are primarily self-directed with minimal supervision, and students do not meet collectively as a class on a regular basis. 

Note: Communication majors may take any combination of 297R, 397R and 497R practicum courses in any sequence to fulfill their graduation requirements.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM102 - Public Speaking (3) ; COMM111 - Writing for Communication Career (3) ; COMM130 - Visual Media (3)

courses.title: Digital Imaging
courses.description: This course teaches skills and knowledge needed to create professional quality photography. Through hands-on experience it surveys different forms of photography and how to edit digital images in Adobe Lightroom and Photoshop. Students will learn to apply digital imagery to a variety of business applications.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM130 - Visual Media (3)

courses.title: Vector Graphics
courses.description: This course will help students build a solid foundation in Adobe Illustrator and further their understanding of the design principles, color theory and typography. Students will learn the importance of sketching, keeping layers panel organized and creating clean vector illustrations that clearly communicate their concept.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM130 - Visual Media (3)

courses.title: Ethics and Legal Issues
courses.description: This course requires students to recognize and practice legal reasoning in relation to issues of relevance to communication professionals. Students will learn to identify elements present in cases concerning libel, privacy, and intellectual property. Additionally, students will consider the legal constraints associated with commercial expression. Finally, students will explore ethical questions likely to arise within the field of professional communication, which cannot be adequately answered by legal means. Students will develop strategies for answering those questions and learn to apply relevant ethical principles as they do so.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM140 - Mass Media and Society (3) ; COMM111 - Writing for Communication Career (3)

courses.title: Creating Online Media
courses.description: This course is a technical introduction to search-engine optimization and standards-based web design and production.  Students will train in semantic HTML markup, CSS-based design and dynamic PHP scripting, overview of the history, current status, and future possibilities of HTML.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; COMM130 - Visual Media (3) ; ART130 - Introduction to Graphic Design (3)

courses.title: Design for Social Media
courses.description: This course teaches students to strategically create and execute a visual content strategy for a brand/organization of the student's choice. Students will go through the process of identifying and selecting an audience, building the brand/organization's social media presence, and creating and executing a visual content strategy that includes different mediums. In the end, students can walk away with a quality portfolio piece.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; COMM130 - Visual Media (3) ; COMM222 - Digital Media Brand Strategy (3)

courses.title: Professional Imaging
courses.description: This professional imaging course focuses on the latest professional techniques to prepare experienced visual communicators for a career, agency, or related visual communication professions. Students will acquire advanced skill in current digital imaging trends and practices. Formative feedback and group critique provide opportunity for professional portfolio growth.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM300 - Digital Imaging (3) ; COMM305 - Vector Graphics (3) ; COMM310 - Creating Online Media (3)

courses.title: Digital Media Content Creation
courses.description: This course gives students a hands-on experience in how to work in, effectively use, and produce content in currently influential new media platforms.  Students will learn how to identify potential market niches, how to analyze their potential, and then how to develop and carry out a plan to produce high-quality public content in multiple venues.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM222 - Digital Media Brand Strategy (3)

courses.title: Digital Media Analytics and Strategy
courses.description: This course gives students hands-on experience in measurement, analysis, and strategy related to digital/social media. Students will learn how to work with industry measurement tools, for example Google Analytics, Facebook Insights, and Data Studio,  a tool that helps turn data into interactive, visual dashboards and reports that inspire smarter business/content decisions. Students will gain experience using these tools to apply strategic, data-driven decision making to improve content creation efforts and maximize marketing outcomes.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM320 - Digital Media Content Creation (3)

courses.title: Public Relations Research
courses.description: This course is an overview of the role of research in public relations. Includes analysis and implementation of research tools, measurement, and methods for gathering and analyzing data, assessment, and evaluation of public relations campaigns. Students will gain experience incorporating the ethical practices and standards for public relations research and presenting intricate data and findings to non-expert audiences. This course will be offered every other semester on a rotating basis with COMM 339 PR Design.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM235 - PR Principles and Writing (3)

courses.title: Public Relations Design
courses.description: Students explore, use, and apply a variety of design principles aimed at the creation of promotional materials. Analysis of public relations goals and how they mold strategic and conceptual design development. Application of Adobe Creative Cloud for the creation of promotional materials across platforms. The course will be offered every other semester on a rotating basis with COMM 335 PR Research.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM130 - Visual Media (3) ; COMM235 - PR Principles and Writing (3)

courses.title: Advanced Media Writing
courses.description: This course teaches journalistic modes of media writing beyond skills taught in COMM 111, including magazine writing, advocacy journalism, and public documents research and writing.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM111 - Writing for Communication Career (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; COMM240 - Newsgathering Principles and Practices (3)

courses.title: Editing Essentials
courses.description: This course teaches principles of improving the quality of language in written stories and scripts, including sentence structure, agreement, case, voice, punctuation, spelling, clarity, conciseness, coherence, accuracy, sensitivity, and style. Both micro- and macro-editing will be considered in this course.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM111 - Writing for Communication Career (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; COMM240 - Newsgathering Principles and Practices (3)

courses.title: Group Dynamics
courses.description: This course analyzes the theory and practice of human communication in a small-group setting focusing on leadership, participation, and evaluation, with emphasis in group norms, roles, cohesion, and conflict.

courses.title: Persuasion
courses.description: This course encourages students to use logos, pathos, and ethos to extend their reach of influence by exploring means of achieving common ground among competing interests in emphasizing the critical thinking skills necessary to understand and communicate about complex, controversial issues in non-confrontational ways either written or oral, and culminates in a team-community-action project.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; COMM102 - Public Speaking (3) ; PEACE101 - Conflict and Peace (3)

courses.title: Video Journalism
courses.description: This course introduces students to the principles and techniques of visual storytelling for multiple methods of  distribution.  Students learn skills in information gathering, interviewing, and writing.  Students use HD video and digital audio equipment to produce a variety of stories primarily for online audiences.

courses.title: Intermediate Moving Image
courses.description: Provides opportunities to study and practice intermediate video production techniques and project management skills within a video production environment. Guides students in combining the operation of field and studio equipment in team-based projects to enhance video production skills and work effectively as collaborating creatives.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM265 - Video and Film Production Essentials (3)

courses.title: Advanced Moving Image 1
courses.description: Students will study and practice advanced video production techniques and higher-level project management skills within a video production environment. Students will combine the operation of field and studio equipment in team-based projects to enhance video production skills and work effectively as collaborating creatives.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM265 - Video and Film Production Essentials (3)

courses.title: Media Business Ownership
courses.description: This course gives students a hands-on experience in brainstorming, planning, creating, and running an independent media content creation business. Students will make a business plan for an independent media content creation company that will include product descriptions, marketing strategies, competitive analysis, and financial information.

courses.title: Scroll Practicum
courses.description: This course is a department-sponsored, hands-on learning experience that includes regular class meeting times. This structured, mentored practicum gives students the opportunity to apply principles learned in their coursework for the Scroll online newspaper and to experience leadership opportunities and responsibilities based upon their competency.

courses.title: Campaigns and Projects
courses.description: This course is a student media-sponsored, hands-on learning experience that includes regular class meeting times. This structured, student-mentored practicum gives students the opportunity to apply principles learned in their coursework to develop skills in an agency environment and direct hands-on project experience. This course runs in conjunction with 397C.

courses.title: Soapbox Practicum
courses.description: This course is a department-sponsored, hands-on learning experience that includes regular class meeting times. This structured, mentored practicum gives students the opportunity to apply principles learned in their coursework Soapbox Agency in a media and agency environment and to experience leadership opportunities and responsibilities based upon their competency.

courses.title: Social Media Practicum
courses.description: This course is a hands-on learning experience creating social media content for a brand. The course focuses on creating quality useful long-form content through research, creative and critical thinking, and group work. Students will have the opportunity to develop their leadership, communication, and content creation skills throughout the course.

courses.title: Community Outreach Practicum
courses.description: This course is a department-sponsored, hands-on learning experience that includes regular class meeting times. This structured, mentored practicum gives students the opportunity to work with VOICE in partnership with local organizations to complete project of value to the community. Research, communication, and outreach strategies are emphasized where students will apply principles learned in their coursework by working on VOICE projects and to experience leadership opportunities and responsibilities based upon their competency.

courses.title: Radio Station Practicum
courses.description: This course is a department-sponsored, hands-on learning experience that includes regular class meeting times. This structured, mentored practicum gives students the opportunity to apply principles learned in their coursework to develop content for the BYU-Idaho radio stations and to experience leadership opportunities and responsibilities based upon their competency.

courses.title: Audio/Visual Production Practicum
courses.description: This course is a department-sponsored, hands-on learning experience that includes regular class meeting times. This structured, mentored practicum gives students the opportunity to apply principles learned in their coursework to develop and create content for BYU-Idaho Audio/Visual Production and to experience leadership opportunities and responsibilities based upon their competency.

courses.title: Visual Emphasis Practicum
courses.description: This course is a department-sponsored, hands-on learning experience that includes regular class meeting times. This structured, mentored practicum gives students the opportunity to apply principles learned in their coursework to develop visual content in a media and agency environment and to experience leadership opportunities and responsibilities based upon their competency.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM300 - Digital Imaging (3) ; COMM305 - Vector Graphics (3) ; COMM310 - Creating Online Media (3)

courses.title: Public Relations Practicum
courses.description: This course explores the theory or phenomenon of events in society as well as management fundamentals.

courses.title: Communication Practicum II
courses.description:
This course is a department-sponsored, hands-on learning experience that includes regular class meeting times. This structured, mentored practicum gives students the opportunity to apply principles learned in their coursework in a media and agency environment and to experience leadership opportunities and responsibilities based upon their competency.

Note: Communication majors may take any combination of 297R, 397R, and 497R practicum courses in any sequence to fulfill their graduation requirements.

courses.title: Digital and Social Media Campaigns
courses.description: Digital and Social Media Campaigns is the capstone course for the Digital Media emphasis in the Department of Communication. Students will be expected to utilize and integrate knowledge, experience, and skills from previous Comm core, module, and Digital and Social Media emphasis courses.  Students will use these skills to plan, execute, and measure the results of and make intelligent adjustments for an integrated, professional-caliber digital/social media strategy and execution for two different brands/organizations.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM320 - Digital Media Content Creation (3) ; COMM322 - Digital Media Analytics and Strategy (3) ; COMM315 - Design for Social Media (3) ; COMM397D - Social Media Practicum (1)

courses.title: Crisis Communication
courses.description: This course will introduce, explore, and focus on key elements of crisis management. Crisis elements will include communication strategies related to prevention, response, and long-term management. Emphasis will be placed on practical application of crisis theory, case-studies, and analysis of a variety of crises in several industries.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM335 - Public Relations Research (3) ; COMM336 - Public Relations Design (3)

courses.title: Public Relation Campaigns
courses.description: This course is a capstone experience designed for students in public relations, pulling together and drawing upon all previous academic and practical learning experiences to create a professional-level communication campaign.  Research, creative conception, public relations and advertising writing, promotional activities, and media planning and strategy are all involved.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM235 - PR Principles and Writing (3) ; COMM335 - Public Relations Research (3)

courses.title: News in the 21st Century
courses.description: This course provides students with deep learning in modern news-gathering trends and techniques such as data journalism.  Students will learn the latest techniques to report and investigate the news. The course will demonstrate competence with creating and disseminating journalism through digital technologies. Students will have an in-depth learning experience of the latest trends in news, including the non-profit, online, hyperlocal, and converged models emerging in the field today. The future of the career - entrepreneurial journalism - is discussed.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM240 - Newsgathering Principles and Practices (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; COMM342 - Editing Essentials (3)

courses.title: Conflict Resolution and Negotiation
courses.description: This course teaches students the theory needed to gain a hands-on experience to resolve conflicts while using principled negotiation in a variety of personal and professional contexts. Topics in this course include conflict resolution strategies, negotiation, third-party intervention, and relevant strategies for effective leadership in the workplace, in interpersonal relationships, and with families.

courses.title: Advanced Visual Media
courses.description: Students in the advanced visual media course explore advanced technology tools to create a variety of self-assigned digital, web, and print projects. Students will create projects which will be presented to the public through the use of social media and a digital portfolio. These advanced projects are designed for immediate application to meet current demands in most business, marketing, advertising, design and communication situations.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM130 - Visual Media (3) ; COMM316 - Professional Imaging (3) ; COMM397H - Visual Emphasis Practicum (1)

courses.title: Advanced Moving Image 2
courses.description: Students will study, practice and apply advanced video production techniques and higher-level project management skills within a video production environment. Students will conceptualize, plan, write, visualize, budget, direct, shoot, edit, and promote fictional and factual video content.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM265 - Video and Film Production Essentials (3) ; COMM365 - Advanced Moving Image 1 (3)

courses.title: Strategic Communication and Social Change
courses.description: This course provides an opportunity for you to acquire and apply skills that align with your values, extend your reach of influence, and position you to be an applicant an employer wants to hire. It will also prepare students to enter professions that depend heavily on strategic communication and critical thinking. It helps students have the ability to think critically, analyze, and articulate issues and communicate complex information to a general audience for informational or persuasive purposes.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; COMM250 - Organizational Principles (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; COMM350 - Group Dynamics (3) ; COMM450 - Conflict Resolution and Negotiation (3)

courses.title: Directed Studies and Projects

courses.title: Communication Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

This course consists of an extended or full-time experience in a professional media or communication organization.  Proposed internship must be approved by designated department faculty member before going to the university internship office for final approval and registration.

courses.title: Communication Senior Project
courses.description: This course is a creation of an approved capstone project or paper to showcase the skills and competencies developed in the communication major. Senior students will work closely with a professional mentor, faculty adviser, and peers to develop a project or research paper that demonstrates the fusion of their undergraduate coursework and experiences.  Projects and papers should be significant and relevant to the student's academic or career objectives.  Students in this course will demonstrate senior-level proficiency in research, visual communication, writing, and presentation skills.  Senior projects will be presented to faculty and peers in an open house fashion.

courses.title: Basic Woodworking
courses.description: This course provides students an introductory experience in woodworking.  At the completion of this course, students will be able to safely use a variety of woodworking tools.  Students will learn designing and estimating skills for small projects.  They will have experience in selecting, cutting, and milling lumber, and will use both hand and power tools in learning proper joining techniques. Students will also select finishing materials and employ correct finishing techniques.  This course will be beneficial to those considering woodworking as a vocation in the construction or cabinetmaking industries as well as those pursuing woodworking as a hobby.

courses.title: Survey of Virtual Design and Construction Management
courses.description: This course helps students choose a career within their program of study. During the semester, Architecture and Construction Management faculty will inform students of the many and varied career paths possible within the professions.  Students will also be introduced to each major's required Professional Development Plan.

courses.title: Framing Systems
courses.description: This course is a study of the tools, materials, codes, procedures, and industry practices used in the construction of structures. Topics include construction drawings, codes, materials, introduction to estimating, introduction to scheduling, site layout, foundations, floors, stairs, walls, and roofs. Classroom discussion and lab experiences help students understand the processes used in residential and light-commercial construction.

courses.title: Furniture Making
courses.description: This course teaches advanced woodworking techniques used in the design and construction of fine furniture. Emphasis will be placed on the design, materials, and joinery techniques utilized in the creation of a vanity. Because of the variable nature of the styles and materials used in the construction of the vanity, the cost for this project will vary with the minimal cost being approximately $100. This course is offered every other semester.

courses.title: Finishing Systems
courses.description: This course will give students a basic understanding of the design, materials, and methods of finishing systems used in the building construction industry. Topics covered include roofing, glazing, cladding and curtain walls, insulation, wall coverings, ceilings, stairs, railings, decks, fences, millwork, cabinets, architectural coatings, and floor coverings. Students construct and apply finishes to a small building during labs.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CONST120 - Framing Systems (3)

courses.title: Construction Safety
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the OSHA standards as they apply to the construction industry. Students will discover that employee safety is critical to the successful completion of any construction project. Discussion topics will include Falls, Electrocution, Struck-by, Caught in/between, Managing Safety & Health, PPE, Fire Safety, Excavations, Cranes, Scaffolds and more.  Special emphasis will be placed on recognizing the most common safety hazards in the construction industry. Student activities include preparing and presenting a safety meeting as part of a group, and researching and writing a Company Safety Manual.

courses.title: Building Systems
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems in a building. The content of this course will help the students understand how these systems operate and how they contribute to personal comfort and productivity.  This brief systems overview will look at the infrastructure that provides the public utility services we need and how we use those utilities in our buildings, including history, design, materials, equipment, fixtures, etc.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CONST120 - Framing Systems (3)

courses.title: Statics and Strength of Materials
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to force systems in static equilibrium and an  elemental understanding of the strengths of material, the relationship between applied loads and the internal forces and deformations induced in the structural element.  Major topics that are covered in the course include forces, moments, couples, free body diagrams, trusses, frames, centroids, moment of inertia, stress, strain, deformation and load, shear, and moment diagrams.

courses.title: Beginning Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap. 

An internship is a cooperative program between BYU-Idaho Design and Construction Management Department and approved Experience Providers (employers). Professional internships correlate actual work experience in the building construction industry with the architecture and construction coursework. Internships approved by the internship coordinator provide students with knowledge of career opportunities and actual work experience in preparation for employment after graduation. The ideal internship would take place during the student's flex semester and be a full time, paid, employment opportunity. The length of time for your internship experience is intended to be equal to a 14 week semester, 40 hours per week or approximately 560 hours. Students should complete this internship course no later than between their Sophomore and Junior years for Construction Management degree seeking students and between Freshman and Sophomore years for those seeking an Associate degree in Architecture.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CONST105 - Survey of Virtual Design and Construction Management (1)

courses.title: Cabinetmaking
courses.description: This course is a study of the materials and methods used in professional cabinetmaking.  Students will study designing, planning, cost estimating, materials, and construction techniques for kitchen, bathroom, and other built-in types of cabinets using both traditional and metric construction methods. This course will also cover the safe setup and operation of professional cabinetmaking equipment. This course is offered every other semester.

courses.title: Construction Estimating
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to introduce the student to the principles of construction cost estimates, including organizing and planning an estimate, developing material and labor databases, preparing accurate quantity takeoffs, and developing an understanding of overhead and profit.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CONST120 - Framing Systems (3) ; VDC170 - Plan Reading (1) ; PW 100T

courses.title: Construction BIM
courses.description: This is an advanced course that will prepare students to use Building Information Modeling (BIM) Technology in the designing, planning, estimating, scheduling, coordination, administration, and management of constructive projects. Topics to be covered include: the building information business model, the BIM coordination process and preparing a coordination plan, using the building model to prepare accurate quantity takeoffs and construction estimates, the development of project schedules and controls from the building model, clash detection and the use of building model in the creation of construction projects, and building information modeling tools in job site administration.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; VDC190 - Building Information Modeling I (3)

courses.title: Field Scheduling
courses.description: This course will introduce students to the concepts of construction planning and scheduling.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; VDC170 - Plan Reading (1)

courses.title: Land Surveying
courses.description: In this course, students will learn the theory and use of instruments dealing with measurements pertaining to plane surveying.  Application of surveying methods of practical problems will be discussed.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; CONST260 - Statics and Strength of Materials (3) ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4)

courses.title: Soils
courses.description: This course is an introduction to soil materials, soil mechanics, and soil testing. In conjunction with the testing methods, the materials presented will provide the basic background for understanding soil behavior and how construction specifications relate to it. The cost and control of excavating, hauling, grading, compacting, lifting and the use of other heavy equipment will be discussed.

courses.title: Construction Materials
courses.description: Construction materials includes information on the basic material properties, construction uses, and installation of modern construction materials. Characteristics and testing procedures of the materials used in construction are discussed:  steel, aggregates, concrete, masonry, asphalt, and wood.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CONST298R - Beginning Internship (1)

courses.title: Project Management
courses.description: Students in this course learn the objectives that define a successful project using varying delivery methods in commercial building construction.  Students will learn how to use the tools the project manager uses to successfully manage the construction of a building project.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; CONST298R - Beginning Internship (1) ; PW100T completion also fulfills the prerequisite

courses.title: Construction Scheduling
courses.description: Students in this course learn the styles and techniques of creating a construction schedule by breaking down the project scope and developing schedule activities, durations, and a network of logical relationships to calculate projected start and finish dates.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; CONST315 - Field Scheduling (3) ; CONST298R - Beginning Internship (1) ; PW100T completion also fulfills the prerequisite

courses.title: Advanced Estimating and Bidding
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to help students prepare to gain the knowledge and skills required to estimate in construction. An in-depth analysis of estimating methods, fundamental skills, the estimator's responsibilities, and computer software applications for construction cost estimates is covered. Evolving estimating methods will also be introduced.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CONST305 - Construction Estimating (3)

courses.title: Construction Law
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to provide an introduction to contract law and the legal requirements and regulations associated with the operation of a construction company and execution of construction projects.

courses.title: Special Problems
courses.description: Students in this course will learn problem solving in a variety of construction and architectural areas. This course may involve special assignments, student competitions, laboratory.

Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

An internship is a cooperative program between BYU-Idaho Design and Construction Department and approved Experience Providers (employers). Advanced level internships correlate actual work experience in the management of people and resources in the construction/architecture industry with the architecture and construction coursework. Internships approved by the internship coordinator provide students with knowledge of career opportunities and actual work experience in preparation for employment after graduation. The length of time for your internship experience is intended to be equal to a 14 week semester, 40 hours per week or approximately 560 hours. Students should complete this internship course no later than between their Junior and Senior years.

courses.title: Capstone: Construction Principles
courses.description: This course is a Capstone to your experience as a DCM major. You will work as a team to demonstrate your ability to design, estimate, schedule, and propose on a project. Throughout the semester, the topics of leadership and management will be explored.

courses.title: Introduction to Computing
courses.description: This is an introductory class into the fields of computer science, software engineering, computer programming, and software development. It is designed to introduce the student to the world of computers and software, and particularly how we use computers and software to build life changing solutions in areas like mobile and web applications, databases, and artificial intelligence. It is also designed to clarify the curriculum at BYU-Idaho so a student can successfully plan a graduation path and educational experience.

courses.title: Introduction to Programming
courses.description: Introduces the fundamentals of programming and the building blocks of programming languages, including variables, decisions, calculations, loops, arrays, and input and output. Guides students in using these tools to solve problems.

courses.title: Programming with Functions
courses.description: Helps students become more organized, efficient, and powerful computer programmers by teaching them to research and call functions written by others; write, call, debug, and test their own functions; and handle errors within functions. Guides students in writing programs with functions to solve problems in many disciplines, including business, physical science, human performance, and humanities.
