courses.title: Freshman Discovery Project (Cybersecurity)
courses.description:
This course is meant to be fun and exciting! Students will create a real project of their choosing that will help them to gain excitement about continuing in one of the computing majors. 

This is a 2-credit course designed to provide freshman students in Computing Degrees at BYU-Idaho with the opportunity to engage in hands-on project development. This course is intended to be taken during the second semester of the freshman year. Students enrolled in CSE199R should have completed or be enrolled concurrently in CSE 111 Programming with Functions or have equivalent programming experience. 

Students will have the freedom to choose and develop a project of their own interest, leveraging the skills and knowledge acquired from previous coursework or personal exploration. The course emphasizes self-directed learning and project management, as students will not be provided with formal learning materials or structured assignments. Instead, they will have the autonomy to define their project scope, set milestones, and implement solutions using appropriate technologies and methodologies.

courses.description: The purpose of CSE 232 is to learn how to build software to meet rigid specifications, how to optimize algorithmic performance, and how to more effectively utilize data structures in real-world applications.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CSE231 - Inheritance Design (2)

courses.title: Software Testing
courses.description: Software Testing is a systematic process of verifying requirements and design elements, features, or standards against the implementation to increase product success. The verification process uses a set of test paths starting from the minor units up to the entire deliverable system using predetermined or live data to build confidence that the product works right (as specified). CSE 270 will explore testing standards, techniques, tools, and cases.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CSE111 - Programming with Functions (2) ; -or- CS124 (last offered 2023) ; -or- CS241 (last offered 2023)

courses.title: Software Lifecycle Models
courses.description: Software Lifecycle Models describes many ways in which software development teams can be organized, how artifacts are generated and utilized, how communication between team members occurs, and how progress is tracked.

courses.title: Discrete Mathematics
courses.description: Introduces the mathematical topics needed to provide a solid theoretical foundation for computer science.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Faculty/Student consultation will determine an area of study/research that will give an advanced student greater appreciation and experience in this field. Terms of enrollment, credit, etc., will be determined by the instructor.

courses.title: Professional Readiness
courses.description: Prepares students to be professionals in their major by completing activities that will provide professional connections, confidence, and employability.

courses.title: Applied Programming
courses.description: Teaches students to work in teams on large projects using new technology on self-defined projects. Simulates real-world programming projects with the aim of producing workable solutions that have potential impact.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CSE210 - Programming with Classes (2) ; -or- CS241 (last offered 2023) ; -or- CS165 (last offered 2023)

courses.title: Mobile Programming
courses.description: This course introduces students to mobile programming using one of two platforms, iOS or Android. Students may choose to create and program for mobile or wearables for either platform.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CSE310 - Applied Programming (3)

courses.title: .NET Software Development
courses.description: Leverages a student's fundamental software development and core web technology background with the Microsoft .NET framework with C# using the Visual Studio Integrated Development Environment. Students will build upon a C# foundation using the ASP.NET framework to design and develop scalable, standards-based websites, applications, and services using contemporary methodologies and established design patterns. Teamwork and programming deliverables will be required.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CSE210 - Programming with Classes (2) ; WDD130 - Web Fundamentals (2)

courses.title: Design Patterns
courses.description: Focuses on understanding and using design patterns as high-level programming constructs. Emphasizes problem-solving and analysis skills.

courses.description: Introduces students to how hardware and software execute multiple tasks simultaneously. Covers programming, strategies, and mechanisms for addressing the complexities and problems that arise in concurrent execution.

courses.description: An introduction to the many tools and services provided by modern operating systems that allow developers to make more performant and feature-rich applications

courses.title: Computer Networks
courses.description: This course is an introduction to how digital devices communicate with each other.  The major focus is how devices communicate using the global Internet.  The course includes network programming assignments.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CSE212 - Programming with Data Structures (2) ; CSE310 - Applied Programming (3) ; -or- CS246 (last offered 2023)

courses.title: Software Engineering Principles
courses.description: Students learn to analyze and make decisions in software projects through all phases of the software development lifecycle, including requirements elicitation, design, testing, verification, and maintenance.

courses.title: Requirements Elicitation
courses.description: Finding the needs of a stakeholder is a non-trivial process. One cannot simply ask them what they need; they often do not know or know how to describe their needs. Requirements engineering is the process of systematically interviewing and observing clients to discover their needs. It also consists of expressing these needs in a non-ambiguous way. This course takes students through every step of this process.

courses.title: Algorithms and Complexity
courses.description: Introduces formal techniques to support the design and analysis of algorithms, focusing on both the underlying mathematical theory and practical considerations of efficiency. Topics include asymptotic complexity bounds, techniques of analysis, and algorithmic strategies. The following will be done with numerous algorithms used in modern computing solutions: Research the algorithm using AI tools to complement required reading and classroom activities; Explain the details of the algorithm methodology and performance; Implement the algorithm in an imperative programming language.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CSE280 - Discrete Mathematics (3) ; CSE212 - Programming with Data Structures (2)

courses.title: Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

Students will gain a greater vision of becoming business professionals and will establish professional career networking links with the business professionals they meet during their internship. Students will write reports and complete self-evaluations.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CSE310 - Applied Programming (3)

courses.title: Product Development Project (Cybersecurity)
courses.description:
This course is meant to be fun and exciting! Students will create a real project of their choosing that will help them to gain excitement about continuing in one of the computing majors.

This is a 2-credit course designed to provide junior students in Computing Degrees at BYU-Idaho with the opportunity to engage in hands-on project development to complete a real product. This course is intended to be taken during the junior year, any time after completing CSE 310.

Students will have the freedom to choose and develop a project of their own interest, leveraging the skills and knowledge acquired from previous coursework or personal exploration. The course emphasizes self-directed learning to create a real-world product. Students will not be provided with formal learning materials or structured assignments. Instead, they will have the autonomy to define their project scope, set milestones, and implement solutions using appropriate technologies and methodologies.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; CSE310 - Applied Programming (3) ; ITM310 - Applied Cloud Computing (3)

courses.title: Product Development Project (Embedded Systems)
courses.description:
This course is meant to be fun and exciting! Students will create a real project of their choosing that will help them to gain excitement about continuing in one of the computing majors.

courses.title: Architectural Design
courses.description: This class enables students to work in very large codebases, describing existing designs and suggesting improvements.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CSE310 - Applied Programming (3) ; CSE331 - Design Patterns (2) ; -or- CS246 (last offered 2023)

courses.title: Machine Learning
courses.description: Introduces machine learning and its use in discovering patterns in data and making predictions. Develops students' familiarity with the overall process and terms of machine learning, including how to communicate with non-technical stakeholders. Introduces a broad set of machine learning algorithms and explains both how they work and how to apply them appropriately.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; DS250 - Data Science Programming (2) ; Take the following course(s): ; CSE310 - Applied Programming (3) ; MATH341 - Linear Algebra (3) ; Take the following course(s): ; CSE111 - Programming with Functions (2) ; DS350 - Data Wrangling and Visualization (3) ; Take the following course(s): ; CSE212 - Programming with Data Structures (2) ; MATH330 - Engineering Statistics (3)

courses.title: Computer Security
courses.description: The purpose of this class is to help each student develop the skills necessary to become a security expert in whatever domain of computer security that is important to their job when they enter the workforce.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CSE310 - Applied Programming (3)

courses.title: Developing AI Systems
courses.description: Prepares students to use AI in industry. Building on previous experience with machine learning modeling, students learn to design and implement end-to-end AI systems. They learn to deploy these systems into working environments and monitor them for iterative improvement.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CSE450 - Machine Learning (3)

courses.title: UX Research
courses.description: Introduces and guides students through one of the most important and difficult processes in digital product development: user research. Provides opportunities for students to conduct user research and user testing at multiple stages of the product development cycle. Teaches best practices for conducting user interviews, analyzing feedback, and compiling research reports that influence the final design of a product. Fosters students' empathy for end users who may have perspectives and backgrounds different from their own.

courses.title: Process Improvement
courses.description: This course introduces the students into field of Process Improvement. The goal here is to help students realize that there is always an opportunity for continuous improvement for an organization and for themselves.  Students will be study multiple methodologies used in industry to systematically analyze and improve processes.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; CSE272 - Software Lifecycle Models (2) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; BUS321 - Organizational Leadership (3) ; -or- ITM380 (last offered 2024)

courses.title: Computational Theory
courses.description: Covers the theory of computation, including finite automata, regular expressions, languages, grammars, Turing machines, computability, complexity, and P, NP, and NP-complete problems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CSE381 - Algorithms and Complexity (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; CSE382 - Patterns and Data Structures (3)

courses.title: Massively Parallel Computation
courses.description: Introduces using functional programming to create massively parallel, distributed computing systems in the cloud. In support of this, students learn the impact of common computational errors found in massively parallel systems and how to avoid them.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CSE382 - Patterns and Data Structures (3)

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Faculty/Student consultation will determine an area of study/research that will give an advanced student greater appreciation and experience in this field. Terms of enrollment, credit, etc., will be determined by the instructor.

courses.title: Internship II
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

Students will gain a greater vision of becoming business professionals and will establish professional career networking links with the business professionals they meet during their internship. Students will write reports and complete self-evaluations.

courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: Provides students with experience in directed individual or group research and study of a computer science topic not covered by the curriculum. Requires students to demonstrate their ability to learn and apply new material by completing a significant project.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CSE310 - Applied Programming (3) ; -or- CS246 (last offered 2023)

courses.title: Senior Project, Part A
courses.description: Provides students with experience in directed individual or group research and study of a computer science topic not covered by the curriculum. Part A of the senior project includes proposal preparation, research, requirements specification, and other activities as specified in the proposal.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CSE310 - Applied Programming (3) ; -or- CS246 (last offered 2023)

courses.title: Senior Project, Part B
courses.description: This course is the completion of the senior project started in CS 499A as specified in the proposal and requirements specification.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CSE499A - Senior Project, Part A (2)

courses.title: Cybersecurity Fundamentals
courses.description: Introduces students to industry-leading frameworks, strategies, tools, and technologies of cybersecurity, including computing devices, networks, the Internet, and information categories.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; CSE110 - Introduction to Programming (2) ; ITM101 - Introduction to Cloud Technologies (2) ; WDD130 - Web Fundamentals (2)

courses.title: Networking
courses.description: Teaches general networking principles to provide an understanding of data communication protocols, transmission systems, media, and software.

courses.title: Systems Security I
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to provide the student with an overview of the field of Cyber Security. Students will be exposed to the spectrum of Security activities, methods, methodologies, and procedures. This course offers a comprehensive guide for anyone wishing to take the CompTIA Security+  Certification Exam. It provides an introduction to the fundamentals of network security, including compliance and operational security; threats and vulnerabilities; application, data, and host security; access control and identity management; and cryptography. The course covers new topics in network security as well, including web application attacks, penetration testing, data loss prevention, cloud computing security and application programming development security.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CYBER201 - Cybersecurity Fundamentals (2) ; CYBER240 - Networking (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ITM112 - Introduction to Linux (2) ; CIT352 - Operating Systems I (3) ; ITM101 - Introduction to Cloud Technologies (2) ; -or- CIT151 (last offered 2023)

courses.title: Network Design I
courses.description: Teaches the principles of network standards and architectures that correspond to the Interconnecting Cisco Networking Devices Part 2 (ICND2) standard. Students learn the configuration and use of networking devices and protocols, including LAN switching technologies, IPv4 and IPv6 routing technologies, WAN technologies, infrastructure services, and infrastructure maintenance.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CYBER240 - Networking (3)

courses.title: Network Design II
courses.description: Focuses on advanced router configuration, Cisco IOS Software management, routing protocol configuration, TCP/IP, and advanced routing protocols such as EIGRP and Frame Relay. Students develop skills in configuring a router, managing Cisco IOS Software, and configuring routing protocols on routers.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CYBER340 - Network Design I (3)

courses.title: Wireless Networking
courses.description: This is an introductory course in Wireless Networking. The course encompasses the design, planning implementation, operation, and troubleshooting of wireless communication.  The material covers a comprehensive overview of technologies, security, and design practices.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CYBER240 - Networking (3)

courses.title: Advanced Scripting
courses.description: Systems programming, automation, and configuration using advanced scripting techniques.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CSE111 - Programming with Functions (2)

courses.title: Security Assessment
courses.description: Covers up-to-date penetration testing and vulnerability assessment skills necessary to assess the resilience of an information system against attacks. Students prepare for the CompTIA Pentest+ certification (or similar) exam. Students have access to an industry-recognized certification as part of their required course materials. They will be required to take either that certification test or an industry-recognized equivalent as part of the course experience.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; CYBER301 - Systems Security I (3) ; ITM112 - Introduction to Linux (2) ; CYBER240 - Networking (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ITM111 - Introduction to Databases (3) ; ITM220 - SQL (3)

courses.title: Security Analysis and Operations
courses.description: Teaches up-to-date job skills used by security analysts, threat hunters, incident responders, and security operations centers. Students prepare for the CompTIA CySA+ certification (or similar) exam. Students have access to an industry-recognized certification as part of their required course materials. They will be required to take either that certification test or an industry-recognized equivalent as part of the course experience.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; CYBER301 - Systems Security I (3) ; ITM112 - Introduction to Linux (2) ; CYBER240 - Networking (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ITM111 - Introduction to Databases (3) ; ITM220 - SQL (3)

courses.title: Identity and Access Management
courses.description: Teaches principles of digital identity, managing access to computing resources, and privacy concerns, and explores authentication and authorization options for on-premises (datacenter) and off-premises (cloud) infrastructures.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; CYBER370 - Security Assessment (3) ; CYBER375 - Security Analysis and Operations (3) ; ITM400 - Cloud Architecture (3)

courses.title: Systems Security II
courses.description: The purpose of this lab based course is to teach students techniques for securing the entire network architecture both internally and externally. Students will learn how to configure and use firewalls and intrusion detection/prevention systems. In addition, students will learn how to harden operating systems and secure remote access.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the followingOption 1: ; Take the following course(s): ; CYBER370 - Security Assessment (3)Option 2: ; Take the following course(s): ; CYBER375 - Security Analysis and Operations (3)Option 3: ; Take the following course(s): ; CYBER301 - Systems Security I (3) ; CYBER240 - Networking (3)

courses.title: Introduction to Dance Major and Professions
courses.description:
This course introduces the student to various aspects of dance through movement and cultural
contexts in order to understand the diverse opportunities and careers in the dance field. It is designed
to work through the BYU-Idaho dance program as a preparation in developing skills necessary to
join the dance community and job market as the student may wish to pursue. Dance 103 introduces
dance vocabulary and basic research and writing skills. Connections are drawn between the
individual, dance, faith and society. Through critical reflection, analysis and application of dance, the
course prepares students as they gain necessary knowledge and skills to become an advocate for
dance.

courses.title: Jazz Dance, Beginning
courses.description: A movement course where beginning levels of rhythms, style, and technique of jazz dancing are introduced to the student, including basic jazz terminology.

courses.title: Tap Dance, Beginning
courses.description: A movement course where the rhythms, styles, and techniques of beginning tap dancing are introduced to the student, including basic tap terminology.

courses.title: Modern Dance, Beginning
courses.description: This course is built as an introduction to modern dance history and technique. Students will be exposed to the art of dance, and articulate an understanding of the elements of dance (time, space, and energy). Students will demonstrate creative problem solving and interpersonal skills through collaborative improvisation and composition experiences.

courses.title: World Dance, Beginning
courses.description: This is an introductory movement course where students will learn selected rhythms, styles and techniques representing numerous international cultures and dance styles. Basic terminology, formations, styles, and steps will provide a general understanding of world dance, its location, and function within the dance world.

courses.title: Clog Dance, Beginning
courses.description: This is an introductory movement course where students will learn selected rhythms, styles, and techniques of clogging.  Basic terminology, elements, and steps will provide a fundamental understanding of the subject matter corresponding to its location and function within the dance world.

courses.title: Social Dance, Beginning
courses.description: This is an introductory-level movement course where students will be exposed to a wide variety of social, recreational, and ballroom dance styles. Basic terminology, positions, formations, skills, and practices will provide a broad understanding of dance as a means of healthy and wholesome socialization and recreation.

courses.title: Social Dance, Beginning
courses.description: This is an introductory-level movement course where students will be exposed to a wide variety of social, recreational, and ballroom dance styles. Basic terminology, positions, formations, skills, and practices will provide a broad understanding of dance as a means of healthy and wholesome socialization and recreation.

courses.title: Ballet, Beginning
courses.description: This course provides introductory background knowledge and experience in ballet technique, including alignment, kinesthetic movement principles, terminology, and ballet history.

courses.title: Jazz Dance Intermediate
courses.description: This is a movement course where intermediate levels of rhythms, style, and technique of jazz dance are explored, including jazz terminology.

courses.title: Tap Dance Technique
courses.description: In this course, students will learn intermediate dance through advanced level terminology, technique, steps and rhythms, in at least three styles of tap dance. Content and movement in the course will challenge students to train their bodies and mind in connection to rhythm and movement.

courses.title: Modern Dance Technique I
courses.description: Students will learn the fundamentals of dance techniques in Modern dance, emphasizing development in body, motion, space, time, and energy awareness. Students will learn key historical figures in the form to deepen understanding of Modern dance as an art form. Acceptance in the course and progression to DA 340R, DA 440R, and DA 443R will be based on successful completion of this course and a competency placement audition.

courses.title: Introduction to Choreographic Devices
courses.description: Through creative play and exploration, students will learn how to manipulate time, space, and energy. Through discussion, questioning, critical thinking, and movement presentations, students will develop their individual artistic voices. This course will employ study, observation, discussion, and movement exploration on a weekly basis.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE240R - Modern Dance Technique I (2)

courses.title: World Dance Technique 1
courses.description: This is a movement course where intermediate/advanced levels of World Dance will be introduced to the student.  Accompanying terminology and background will provide a deep understanding of the subject corresponding to its location and function within the greater dance world.

courses.title: Clog Dance Technique I
courses.description: This is a technique course where intermediate level rhythms, styles, and techniques of clogging will be introduced to the student.  Terminology, stylistic elements, and pattern will provide a broad understanding of the subject.

courses.title: Ballroom Technique I
courses.description: This is a studio course where the technical foundations of Ballroom dancing are taught. At this level, students are expected to gain knowledge and proficiency in basic levels of Latin and Standard Ballroom dance technique through practical experience and theoretical application. It is expected that a student will take this course a minimum of two times before proceeding to the Technique 2 course (DA 380).

courses.title: Ballet Technique I
courses.description: This course will explore ballet through an understanding of kinesthetic awareness.  Developing this conscious attention to the body will allow the dancer to learn the difference between efficient movement and inefficient movement, a principle that can be used not only in dance but also in everyday life.

courses.title: Dance Kinesiology I
courses.description: Introduction to human anatomy and kinesiology consisting of the study of human movement specific to dance, with emphasis on the anatomical principles and the laws of physics as they apply to dance technique and performance.  Structural and neuromuscular analysis including individual analysis of alignment, muscular imbalances, body types, conditioning needs, injury prevention, nutrition, somatics and movement behavior. Specific areas of the body studied will be the spine, torso, pelvis, and femoral joint.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE240R - Modern Dance Technique I (2)

courses.title: Practicum
courses.description: This course gives students practical experience in teaching, assisting and choreographing in a mentored setting.

courses.title: Conditioning for Dancers
courses.description: This course is designed to teach and instill lifelong conditioning practices for dancers. It will teach conditioning principles and exercise, injury prevention methods, and nutritional knowledge specific to the needs of a dancer. This course will implement healthy practices that will ensure long and healthy futures within the field of dance and to prepare the student bodies for the physical demands of the Dance Major.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; DANCE231R - Jazz Dance Intermediate (1) ; DANCE240R - Modern Dance Technique I (2) ; DANCE235R - Tap Dance Technique (1) ; DANCE290R - Ballet Technique I (1) ; DANCE270R - World Dance Technique 1 (1) ; DANCE271R - Clog Dance Technique I (1) ; DANCE280R - Ballroom Technique I (1)

courses.title: Jazz Dance Advanced
courses.description: This is a movement course where advance levels of rhythm, styles, and techniques of jazz are explored, including basic through advanced jazz terminology.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE231R - Jazz Dance Intermediate (1)

courses.title: Tap Technique II
courses.description: This is a studio technique class where advanced level rhythms, styles and techniques of American tap dancing will be taught. Applicable terminology, structures, stylistic elements and patterns will be provided to the student to create a broad understanding of the subject.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE235R - Tap Dance Technique (1)

courses.title: Modern Dance Technique II
courses.description: This course is designed to give the intermediate/advanced dancer practical exercises in dance techniques emphasizing development in elements of dance, kinesthetic awareness, movement principles,  performance, style, vocabulary, and pedagogy in both modern dance and ballet. Methods of kinesiology and dance science will be introduced and explored.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE240R - Modern Dance Technique I (2)

courses.title: Special Topics in Dance
courses.description: This course will provide higher levels of technique and theory  and rotate between the following topics to allow students to tailor the curriculum to their needs. Topics include: Dance Improvisation, Music for Dancers, Advanced Survey Footworks, Advanced and Introductory Ballet and Pointe Work, History of Hip Hop, Research Design for Dance and Specialized movement lens in Ballroom and Jazz Dance. See our webpage at byui.edu/dance for information on which topics will be offered during each semester and more in-depth descriptions of each of those topics.

courses.title: Dance Seminar
courses.description: In this course students will be introduced to subject matter pertaining to the professional field of dance and dance-related artistic and scholarly work. It will introduce numerous theoretical concepts on the topics of dance, dance studies, body, identity, representation, choreography, performance, and more. Additionally, it will provide a platform for exploration of various professional pursuits and practical experience with the planning and preparation for a major dance-based project.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE103 - Introduction to Dance Major and Professions (1)

courses.title: Dance Production and Technology
courses.description: This course will provide students with instruction and mentoring in the use of technology in the creation, preservation and presentation of dance on stage and digital platforms.  Through historical contextualization and hands-on application of course material, the student will develop an appreciation for, understanding of, and skill in the employment of technology used for dance.

courses.title: Philosophy and Technique of Teaching Dance
courses.description: This course is designed to teach the skills necessary to be a successful dance teacher in all genres and for all ages. To impart knowledge and provide opportunities for critical thinking regarding dance and dance teaching, as well as opportunities to acquire and practice course organization and teaching skills. Students will explore in-depth aspects of owning, running, or teaching in a school or studio setting. Complete studio handbooks will be created for individual use, along with developing the skill and personal philosophy to be successful in an educational setting.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; DANCE231R - Jazz Dance Intermediate (1) ; DANCE235R - Tap Dance Technique (1) ; DANCE240R - Modern Dance Technique I (2) ; DANCE270R - World Dance Technique 1 (1) ; DANCE271R - Clog Dance Technique I (1) ; DANCE280R - Ballroom Technique I (1) ; DANCE290R - Ballet Technique I (1)

courses.title: Teaching Techniques of Dance
courses.description: This course focuses on genre-specific instruction, feedback, and curriculum development for skills-acquisition dance teaching. It provides practical experience and implementation of the skills and knowledge presented in the Philosophy of Teaching Dance course (DANCE356), which must be completed before taking this course.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; DANCE331R - Jazz Dance Advanced (1) ; DANCE335R - Tap Technique II (1) ; DANCE340R - Modern Dance Technique II (2) ; DANCE371R - Clog Dance Technique 2 (1) ; DANCE380R - Ballroom Technique II (1) ; DANCE390R - Ballet Technique II (2)

courses.title: Clog Dance Technique 2
courses.description: In this course, students will be introduced to advanced level rhythms, styles, and techniques of clog dancing.  Advanced level terminology, elements, and steps will provide a deep understanding of the subject corresponding to its location and function within the dance world.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE271R - Clog Dance Technique I (1)

courses.title: Ballroom Technique II
courses.description: This is a studio course where intermediate-level Ballroom dancing techniques are taught. At this level, students are expected to expand and build upon a solid foundational knowledge and proficiency in intermediate levels of Latin and Standard Ballroom dance technique through practical experience and theoretical application. It is expected that a student will take this course a minimum of two times before proceeding to the Technique 3 course (DA 480).
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE280R - Ballroom Technique I (1)

courses.title: Ballet Technique II
courses.description: This course explores ballet through an understanding of kinesthetic movement principles. The complete barre with center adagio, petite allegro, and grand allegro are further enhanced by pre-performance study of classical variations. Students will have the opportunity to view video of their class and variation work as a part of the course.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE290R - Ballet Technique I (1)

courses.title: The Art of Yoga and Meditation
courses.description: Through a concentrated study of yoga asanas, mediation techniques, pranayama (breathe control), and philosophical studies, students will engage in questioning, analysis and application as they journey within on a path to the Divine.

courses.title: Research and Creative Practicum
courses.description: This practicum course allows upper division students to learn advanced topics in areas such as Kinesiology, history, and/or personal exploration and development in choreography and teaching methods through guided study.

courses.title: History of Dance
courses.description: This course will guide students through an exploration of dance history and its associated socio-cultural aspects.  Close attention will be paid to the correlation between dance and people, particularly in the ways in which they relate to and influence one another. Great effort will be made to present the material from a variety of perspectives and to demonstrate its symbolic nature. While focusing on the 20th century this course will show how a historical foundation must underlie any venture into a holistic understanding of both popular and artistic movement expressions and events.

courses.title: Senior Capstone Project
courses.description: This course provides credit for an in depth and substantial choreographic or theoretical work that denotes advanced study. This course will require a written document, oral presentation, and/or visual production. Preparation for this course will begin in the DANCE103 and DANCE350 classes in order to help students determine a topic of research. This class will be offered as needed with the understanding that there must be 3 or more students registered for the class any given semester.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE350 - Dance Seminar (3)

courses.title: Modern Dance Technique III
courses.description: This course is designed to encourage students to expand their range of movement capabilities, discovering new possibilities in all planes of motion and spatial orientations. It promotes active participation with movement concepts and Somatic vocabulary. Classes explore fully body contact with the floor, the space and with partners and/or groups of individuals. Each individual will investigate their relationship with space, alignment, efficiency, weight and momentum as well as the effects of gravity, breath and effort. Each individual will realize the potential for artistic and movement discovery in and outside the classroom and will have the opportunity to develop their own movement vocabulary and descriptive language. Individuals will take a Hermeneutic approach to the study of the phenomenon of movement.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE340R - Modern Dance Technique II (2)

courses.title: Choreographic Explorations
courses.description: This course encompasses the study, exploration, implementation, and examination of the dance making process at an advanced level of inquiry, creative thinking, and critical analysis in order to more articulately develop an understanding of movement as an expressive art form.  It is also an opportunity for students to produce a final choreographic project that will incorporate the skills, knowledge, and experience acquired throughout their studies which will be presented in a live performance setting.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE242 - Introduction to Choreographic Devices (2)

courses.title: Advanced Technique and Somatics
courses.description: This course is designed to encourage students to expand their range of movement capabilities by discovering new possibilities in all places of motion and spatial orientation. The course promotes active participation with somatic movement concepts and modern dance vocabulary. Students will study their body movement as it copes with the environment by understanding how total body connectivity is the initiative for movement. Students will learn a kinesthetic understanding of how function effects form. This course will explore full body contact with partners, the floor and the space around them, center work, locomotion, and structured movement combinations. Through developed somatic approaches, students will learn how movements are designed to investigate relationships with space, correct alignment and efficiency, weight and momentum, the effects of gravity, and breath. Students will further their understanding of who they are as an individual and as an artist through daily reinvestment of the familiar and continual drive for the unknown.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE340R - Modern Dance Technique II (2)

courses.title: Step Dancing Technique III
courses.description: This is a studio course where the students will be trained in advanced-professional level rhythms, styles and techniques of various step dancing genres. Professional level skill, terminology, patterning, styling, and steps from Irish and Canadian step dancing, tap dance, and American clogging will provide a diverse understanding of the subject matter corresponding to its location and function within the dance world.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; DANCE335R - Tap Technique II (1) ; DANCE371R - Clog Dance Technique 2 (1)

courses.title: Dance Alliance
courses.description: Dance Alliance is a distinctive dance company representing BYU-Idaho that is dedicated to sharing the gospel through dance and using individual technical strength while engaging in a variety of dance genres.  As students create dance for performances they will be bound by the 13th Article of Faith in music, costumes, and choreography which will be 'virtuous, lovely or of good report or praiseworthy.'  The purpose of dancers and artists is to lift, inspire, and change the hearts of those who experience the performance.  It is this alternative in dance that Dance Alliance will seek out.  Check the Theatre and Dance Department website for audition and tour dates at www.byui.edu/dance.

courses.title: Ballroom Technique III
courses.description: This is a studio course where advanced-level Ballroom dancing techniques are taught. At this level, students are expected to apply and master knowledge and proficiency in advanced levels of Latin and Standard Ballroom dance technique through practical experience and theoretical application. It is expected that a student will take this course a minimum of two times.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE380R - Ballroom Technique II (1)

courses.title: Collegiate Dancers
courses.description: This course promotes recreational dancing, teaching, and performance.  This outreach group will consist of 40 dancers dedicated to sharing several styles of dance. Representing BYU-Idaho, the group will perform for community schools and local organizations in addition to campus events.  The department hopes students will receive a quality experience that will allow them to share dance in their communities as well as prepare for other performing opportunities.  These students will be invited to strengthen their testimonies of the restored gospel in addition to developing their skill, performance, teaching, and team work abilities. Check the Theatre and Dance Department website for audition dates at www.byui.edu/dance.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 course from the following range: DANCE 200 - 499

courses.title: Ballet Technique III
courses.description: This advanced level course is designed to study and practice classical ballet technique through kinesthetic awareness. Students will practice barre work, center adagio, petite allegro, and grand allegro with a focus on technique, performance quality, musicality, and artistry. Emphasis will be placed on technical clarity and strength through extended movement combinations as well as choreography. Acceptance in the course will be based on successful completion of DA390-Ballet Technique II and a competency placement.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE390R - Ballet Technique II (2)

courses.title: Dance Kinesiology II
courses.description: Advanced exploration of human anatomy and kinesiology consisting of the study of human movement specific to dance, with emphasis on the anatomical principles and the laws of physics as they apply to dance technique and performance.  Structural and neuromuscular analysis including individual analysis of alignment, muscular imbalances, body types, conditioning needs, injury prevention, nutrition, somatics and movement behavior.  Specific areas of the body studied will be the knee, ankle, lower leg, shoulder, and arm.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; DANCE295 - Dance Kinesiology I (3)

courses.title: Applications of Laban/Bartenieff Movement Analysis
courses.description: This is a project-based course in which we learn to use the language of movement to clarify our pedagogical voice and enhance our compositional abilities. The course emphasizes body awareness and developmental human movement patterning. It explores patterns of Total Body Connectivity and how these basic neurophysiological patterns underlie and support all human movement. It teaches Bartenieff Fundamentals and Laban Movement Analysis as a teaching and compositional lens. It makes application to all genres of dance, sport, theatre, somatics, performance, composition, and psychology.

courses.title: Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

The purpose of the internship is to provide real-world experience linked with information and learning from courses taken at the university.  The internship should aid the student in decisions about future careers in the dance world.

courses.title: Data Intuition and Insight
courses.description: Introduces students to using data to make decisions and communicate meaning through visualization. Covers the underlying data summaries used in data visualizations, including mean, standard deviation, and percentiles.

courses.title: Data Science Programming
courses.description: Builds on the general programming principles of the prerequisite course and teaches students to write programs for data science applications. Focuses on leveraging preexisting libraries to accomplish data retrieval, preparation, prediction, and analysis tasks.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CSE110 - Introduction to Programming (2) ; PH135 - Introduction to Scientific Computing in Physics (2) ; CSE111 - Programming with Functions (2) ; -or- CS101 (last offered 2023) ; -or- CS165 (last offered 2023) ; -or- CS241 (last offered 2023)

courses.title: Special Topics in Data Science
courses.description:
The content of this course will be determined by the department and the instructor, based on student needs and interest. 
Students will study an area of data science not otherwise covered in the data science curriculum.

courses.title: Data Wrangling and Visualization
courses.description: Applies data-driven programming to handle, format, and visualize messy and complex data. Teaches students to implement data handling techniques and the grammar of graphics process to visualize complex data.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the followingOption 1: ; Take the following course(s): ; MATH325 - Intermediate Statistics (3)Option 2: ; Take the following course(s): ; CSE111 - Programming with Functions (2) ; DS250 - Data Science Programming (2)

courses.title: Big Data Programming and Analytics
courses.description: Develops big data analytics skills using R, Python, and SQL with the current industry tools for big data programming and analytics.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; DS250 - Data Science Programming (2)AND ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CSE450 - Machine Learning (3) ; DS350 - Data Wrangling and Visualization (3) ; ITM327 - Data Warehousing (3)

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Data Science
courses.description: The content of this course will be determined by the department and the instructor, based on student need and interest. Students will study and extend their understanding in an area of Data Science not otherwise covered in the Data Science curriculum. As part of this course, students will demonstrate discipleship by helping one another succeed in this class.

courses.title: Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

This course consists of practical experience working in a data science intensive industry.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; DS250 - Data Science Programming (2) ; DS350 - Data Wrangling and Visualization (3)

courses.title: Senior Project in Data Science
courses.description: This course supports the professional goals of the student. Under the guidance of a faculty member, the student will engage in a focused learning experience that applies data science principles. The student could possibly work in partnership with other students. The student will present their work publicly.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; DS250 - Data Science Programming (2) ; DS350 - Data Wrangling and Visualization (3)

courses.title: Introduction to Electrical and Computer Engineering
courses.description: Introduces students to the fields of electrical and computer engineering and to the use of electrical and computational circuits and systems to design and build life-changing devices such as cell phones, computers, the electrical grid, and robots. Uses introductory programming techniques to enable students to build basic but interesting projects.

courses.title: Computer Systems
courses.description: Explains how computers work, from charge on a computer chip to pixels on a device and everything in between. Provides a high-level overview of all these parts to develop a conceptual understanding of how everything fits together without getting bogged down in details.

courses.title: Electric Circuit Analysis I
courses.description: Introduces students to circuit analysis for electrical and computer engineering. Covers current, voltage, power, basic circuit laws and theorems, transient analysis, and AC steady-state analysis. Includes laboratory exercises.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4)AND ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECEN100 - Introduction to Electrical and Computer Engineering (2) ; -or- ECEN101 (last offered 2025)

courses.title: Fundamentals of Digital Systems
courses.description: Explores the fundamentals of digital systems, including number systems, truth tables, Boolean algebra, Karnaugh maps, combinational logic circuits (multiplexers, decoders, and adders), sequential logic circuits (flip-flops, counters, and shift registers), and state machine design and analysis. Students must design and build a project that uses sequential logic. A student presentation is required.
courses.corequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; CSE121C - C Language (1) ; ECEN100 - Introduction to Electrical and Computer Engineering (2) ; Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; CSE111 - Programming with Functions (2)

courses.title: Electric Circuit Analysis II
courses.description: Studies the analysis and design of DC and AC circuits. Covers transient analysis using differential equations. Includes laboratory exercises.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECEN150 - Electric Circuit Analysis I (3)

courses.title: Microprocessor Based-System Design
courses.description: Covers the architecture, applications, programming, and interfacing of a microcontroller. Students learn to develop device drivers and design systems with input/output. In addition, students learn how to prepare for an internship. Laboratory exercises are included.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CSE121C - C Language (1) ; ECEN100 - Introduction to Electrical and Computer Engineering (2)AND ; Take the following course(s): ; ECEN240 - Fundamentals of Digital Systems (3) ; CSE111 - Programming with Functions (2)

courses.title: Electronic Circuit Fabrication and Evaluation Lab
courses.description: Teaches students to use Electronic Design Automation (EDA) software to create the needed documents to fabricate Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs). Students create parts in a component library, circuit schematics, PCB layouts, and apply Design Rule Checking. The needed files will be generated, and orders place to fabricate the designed PCBs. Students apply soldering techniques to assemble the boards after they are fabricated and troubleshoot any problems identified. Students use standard lab equipment to evaluate the performance of the assembled PCBs.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ECEN250 - Electric Circuit Analysis II (3)

courses.title: Introduction to Electrical Power and Rotating Machines
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the elements and basic concepts of power systems and electric machinery. The course includes a survey of the methods and tools used to study the generation and delivery of electric power. The course introduces the concepts of electric generation and the flow of power. Lab activities provide a hands-on learning experience related to the topics covered in the course.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECEN250 - Electric Circuit Analysis II (3)

courses.title: Computer Architecture
courses.description: Computer system and processor architecture including instruction sets, memory hierarchy, pipelining, I/O, program performance optimization, and heterogeneous computing.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; CSE212 - Programming with Data Structures (2) ; ECEN260 - Microprocessor Based-System Design (3)

courses.title: Digital Systems Design
courses.description: Studies the hierarchical design of digital systems, circuit synthesis, and simulation using the Verilog hardware description language. Circuit implementation field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) will also be explored. A technical report and presentation is required. Laboratory exercises are included.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECEN240 - Fundamentals of Digital Systems (3) ; -or- ECEN160L (last offered 2023)

courses.title: Electronic Devices and Circuits
courses.description: Semiconductor devices, such as transistors, have revolutionized our world, and continue to do so. Attractive career opportunities await those who choose to become proficient in the understanding and use of modern electronic semiconductor devices. This course provides an introduction to semiconductor devices, starting off with pn junction diodes followed by an investigation and analysis of some of the many useful applications of semiconductor diodes used in modern electronic circuits. Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJTs) and Metal-Oxide Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors (MOSFETs) are examined. Laboratory exercises are also included.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECEN250 - Electric Circuit Analysis II (3)

courses.title: VLSI System Design
courses.description: Introduces VLSI design, with a focus on CMOS, the dominant technology used in modern VLSI design. Covers n- and p-channel MOS transistors, digital and analog CMOS circuitry, an overview of CMOS processing technology, layout and design rules, simulation and testing, and VLSI design tools and methodologies.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECEN350 - Electronic Devices and Circuits (3)

courses.title: Embedded Systems
courses.description: Covers the design and implementation of embedded-system solutions for real-time responsive problems. Covers microcontrollers, I/O protocols, and real-world interfacing with digital/analog systems. Detailed concepts include RTOS programming, operation of schedulers and multitasking, various serial communication techniques, ADC and DAC operation and requirements, and DMA use.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECEN260 - Microprocessor Based-System Design (3)

courses.title: Signals and Systems
courses.description: The main goal of this course is to develop the theory of classical signals and systems analysis for both continuous- and discrete-time cases. Topics include signal and system properties, linear time-invariant systems, stability analysis, sampling of continuous-time signals, the z-transform, the discrete Fourier transform, time- and frequency-domain representations of discrete-time signals and systems, and introductory concepts in stochastic signals and systems. The course also introduces statistical inference applications through the use of the Kalman filter for maximum likelihood parameter estimation and state estimation.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECEN250 - Electric Circuit Analysis II (3)

courses.title: Electromagnetics
courses.description: Electromagnetics is foundational material to electrical engineers, providing the theoretical framework for capacitors, inductors, electric motors, generators, transmission lines, antennas, EM wave propagation, etc. While electromagnetics is math intensive, the goal of this class is to explore several different electromagnetic applications along with striving for a conceptual understanding of the basic principles. Laboratory exercises are also included.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECEN250 - Electric Circuit Analysis II (3) ; MATH316 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra (4)

courses.title: Professional Career Preparation
courses.description: Serves as one of three courses comprising the alternate internship requirement. Guides students in establishing professional mentor relationships and preparing for successful employment. Covers resumes, networking, interviewing, and engineering ethics.

courses.title: Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

Full-time employment as an electrical engineering intern or a computer engineering intern for one semester or more.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECEN260 - Microprocessor Based-System Design (3) ; ECEN250 - Electric Circuit Analysis II (3)

courses.title: Power Systems Analysis
courses.description: Develops students' understanding of power system operation and control, power system economics, power quality, and power system reliability. Covers methods for analyzing and protecting against symmetrical and unsymmetrical faults, evaluating transient event stability and power flow, and long-distance power transmission modeling. Includes laboratory activities that provide hands-on learning experiences related to the topics covered.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECEN311 - Introduction to Electrical Power and Rotating Machines (3)

courses.title: RF Circuits
courses.description: Introduces RF circuits and the basics of key RF components, including high-frequency transistors, filters, mixers, oscillators, and phase-locked loops. Introduces students to laboratory test equipment, network analysis, and the fundamentals of transmission lines. Develops students' understanding of basic high-frequency test equipment. Includes laboratory experiments.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECEN350 - Electronic Devices and Circuits (3)

courses.title: Signal and Power Integrity
courses.description: This course is an introduction to signal and power integrity.  It addresses the problems encountered and corresponding practical solutions when designing interconnects for high speed electronic circuits with frequencies over about 100 MHz or rise times shorter than about 1 ns.  This course also studies how to correctly design power distribution networks on circuit boards to keep the voltage across the chip pads constant, minimize ground bounce, and minimize EMI problems.  Laboratories provide experience using advance simulation software to analyze signal and power integrity issues, designing high speed printed circuit boards, and using measurement equipment to validate these issues in hardware.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECEN250 - Electric Circuit Analysis II (3)

courses.title: Semiconductor Device Engineering
courses.description: Introduces semiconductor device physics, fabrication, and engineering, with a primary focus on CMOS technology. Covers the fundamental physics of PN diode and MOSFET transistor operation and the fabrication steps for a basic CMOS process. Briefly reviews future device trends and provides essential background for engineers who use transistors in their careers.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECEN350 - Electronic Devices and Circuits (3)

courses.title: Advanced Embedded Systems
courses.description: Provides students with deeper insight into system integration and the structure and functionality of system software for embedded systems. Examines the challenges of real-time system development, including PID controllers, advanced real-time operating systems, and hardware connectivity.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECEN361 - Embedded Systems (3)

courses.title: Feedback Control of Dynamic Systems
courses.description: Dynamic modeling, dynamic response, and analysis and design of feedback control.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECEN250 - Electric Circuit Analysis II (3) ; ME305 - Mechatronics (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH316 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra (4) ; MATH341 - Linear Algebra (3)

courses.title: Digital Signal Processing
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the flourishing field of digital signal processing (DSP), which focuses on the enhancement and analysis of a myriad of signals, the Fourier and Laplace transform along with the foundational DSP topics of sampling, aliasing, Analog-to-Digital Conversion, Digital-to-Analog Conversion, the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), the z-transform, and digital filtering. Laboratory exercises are included.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECEN250 - Electric Circuit Analysis II (3)

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Covers current topics in computer and electrical engineering.

courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: Develops a culminating design experience based on skills learned in advanced technical courses.  Students work in teams to plan, design, test, and demonstrate a major project.  Instruction on leadership is presented.  Instructor consent is required as well as completion of either ECEN 398R Internship or ECEN 397 Professional Career Preparation.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECEN398R - Internship (1) ; ECEN397 - Professional Career Preparation (1)

courses.title: Economic Principles and Problems-Micro
courses.description: This introductory course in microeconomics studies the behavior of individual economic agents such as consumers and businesses in a market economy.  Analytical tools are used to study the consumption and production decisions in an economy under perfect and imperfect market conditions.

courses.title: Economic Principles and Problems-Macro
courses.description: This introductory course in macroeconomics studies the national economy as a whole and its interaction with the global economy.  Measurement of economic health and the use of fiscal and monetary policies to address unemployment, inflation, and growth are analyzed.

courses.title: Professional Exploration and Orientation
courses.description: Provides students majoring in Economics, Financial Economics, or Agricultural Economics with an introduction to potential careers and continuing professional development. Students survey occupational opportunities in their program of study. They will be introduced to networking opportunities and career marketing, dealing with a personal career search. In addition, students develop study skills and refine their course planning and preparation to enhance their university experience and career preparation.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3)

courses.title: Quantitative Methods
courses.description: This course will teach the fundamentals of comparative statics, differential calculus, and integral calculus with a focus on economics applications. This will prepare students for upper-division coursework in economics and provide a foundation for graduate-level studies.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; ACT 27 or SAT 620 or 2016 SAT 640 or ALEKS 85 ; Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH109 - Precalculus (5) ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; ECON201 - Professional Exploration and Orientation (1) ; AGBUS100 - Agriculture Orientation (1)

courses.title: Financial Analytics
courses.description: Develops students' ability to integrate electronic spreadsheets into the identification, analysis, and solution of economic and financial problems. Provides a conceptual and practical understanding of spreadsheets and equips students with the skills needed to engage in economic and financial modeling. Provides significant experience using the Bloomberg information system, which offers access to news and analytics as well as financial, economic, accounting, and legal data.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ACCTG210 - Principles of Accounting I (3) ; AGBUS201 - Agricultural Financial Accounting (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CIT110 - Introduction to Excel (3) ; BA215 - Spreadsheet Analysis for Business (3)

courses.title: Statistics for Economists
courses.description: Introduces many of the quantitative tools used by economists. It serves as an essential prerequisite for Economics 388 and many 400-level economics courses. Covers probability theory, mathematical statistics, linear algebra, data set creation and manipulation, and STATA software.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; ACT 27 or SAT 620 or 2016 SAT 640 or ALEKS 85 ; Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH109 - Precalculus (5) ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3)

courses.title: Beginning Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap. 

For information on how to register for an internship see the BYU-Idaho internships webpage. This course is designed for students working full or part-time in economics-related employment to gain introductory experience in the work force and to begin applying economics principles in a real-world environment. Students must complete an application and approval through the College of Business and Communication Career Services, contract with their employer to work for college credits, and work a minimum of just under 13 hours per week for a minimum of seven weeks (90 hours minimum for 1 credit). Other requirements include writing reports, submitting self and supervisor evaluations, and adhering to BYU-Idaho standards and policies.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3)

courses.title: Managerial Economics
courses.description: Enhances understanding of how microeconomic analysis can be applied to modern business decision-making.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON215 - Quantitative Methods (4) ; MATH108X - Math for the Real World (3) ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; MATH109 - Precalculus (5) ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3) ; MATH221A - Business Statistics (3) ; MATH221B - Biostatistics (3) ; MATH221C - Social Science Statistics (3)

courses.title: Economic Thought and History
courses.description: This course explores the development and application of major economic doctrines from classical through contemporary economics.  Contributions of selected writers and schools of thought are analyzed with emphasis on how these theories are used in our day.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3) ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3)

courses.title: Money and Banking
courses.description: Studies financial markets and the banking sector and how these markets affect the general economy. Covers four areas: money and bond markets in conjunction with interest rate theory; banking and the theory of rational expectations; the operations and performance of financial institutions, including issues of asymmetric information; and the development of monetary policy and the structure of the Federal Reserve.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3)

courses.title: Investment Analysis
courses.description: Teaches students current investment practices in combination with advanced economic theory. Compares and contrasts methods for evaluating investment choices. Students build investment models based on current market conditions. Covers efficient diversification techniques, the Capital Asset Pricing Model, and portfolio performance evaluation to provide the advanced understanding needed for careers in the financial services sector.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECON255 - Financial Analytics (3)

courses.title: Environmental and Natural Resource Economics
courses.description: Applies economic analysis to various natural resource and environmental issues, including the use of renewable and nonrenewable resources, sustainable development, quality of life, and the environmental impacts of specific industrial and consumption activities, such as solid waste disposal and air and water pollution. Covers methods for measuring natural resource and environmental values, cost-benefit analysis, the design and implementation of government policies, and the environmental effects of human economic activity.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3)

courses.title: International Economics
courses.description: Introduces international trade and finance. Examines international institutions, policies, and issues.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3)

courses.title: Behavioral Economics
courses.description: Examines how empirical evidence of human decision-making can contradict economics' assumption that individuals act rationally. Introduces behavioral economics as a means of adjusting economic assumptions to capture predictable patterns of irrational behavior without discounting the contributions economics has made to understanding human behavior. Discusses procrastination, risky behavior, altruism, and other elements of predictably irrational behavior and applies them to various subfields of economics.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3)

courses.title: Ethics in Financial Management
courses.description:
Explores the unique challenges of ethics and morality in the finance setting. There are many potential pitfalls that employees and companies can fall prey to that are not originally obvious. This course will help students to become as "wise as serpents and harmless as doves" (Matt. 10:16). They will gain specific knowledge about ethical behavior in finance and apply gospel principles to various financial scenarios. Students will also be able to analyze financial scenarios for the incentives involved by all parties. This will give students the tools to avoid traps and pitfalls found at all levels in the finance setting and demonstrate to fellow employees the importance of being a disciple of Jesus Christ and acting with morality (as well as ethics) in all areas of our lives.
 
 "Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves. Be ye therefore wise as serpents and harmless as doves (Matthew 10:16, KJV)."
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3) ; ECON255 - Financial Analytics (3)

courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomics
courses.description: This course introduces the fundamentals of microeconomic theory including: Consumer theory, producer theory, partial equilibrium analysis, and general equilibrium analysis.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON215 - Quantitative Methods (4) ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4)

courses.title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
courses.description: Macroeconomics is the study of national and global economies—their growth, fluctuations, and the policy tools that influence them. In this intermediate course, we build upon foundational principles by delving into mathematical models and computational tools that help analyze complex economic phenomena.  The course utilizes a textbook to guide the theoretical exploration, alongside practical applications using Python. By the end of the semester, students should have not only a deeper understanding of macroeconomic behavior but also stronger quantitative and communication skills—both vital in professional settings.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3) ; Take the following course(s): ; CSE110 - Introduction to Programming (2) ; CSE111 - Programming with Functions (2) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON215 - Quantitative Methods (4) ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4)

courses.title: Introduction to Econometrics
courses.description: Examines econometrics as the branch of economics that formulates statistical methodology to estimate, predict, and test economic relationships. Develops students' ability to critically evaluate econometric models and conduct basic empirical economic research.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON278 - Statistics for Economists (3) ; MATH325 - Intermediate Statistics (3)

courses.title: Special Projects
courses.description: This arranged course allows students to undertake a special project or further research in the field of economics. The student is responsible to find an instructor who agrees to act as a faculty supervisor.  It is expected that the student will outline carefully the proposed research/study for the supervisor's approval. Then with the instructor, the student determines the objectives, outcomes, assessments, timelines, meeting times, and credit hours for the project.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3)

courses.title: Professional Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

Apply the principles and skills learned in the classroom to on-the-job practices and procedures for economists. Through on-the-job experience, gain a greater vision of what it means to be an economics professional.  Establish professional career habits and hone economic analytical skills.
