courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ECON201 - Professional Exploration and Orientation (1)AND ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; BA215 - Spreadsheet Analysis for Business (3) ; BUS115 - Applied Spreadsheets and Analysis (3) ; CIT110 - Introduction to Excel (3) ; ECON255 - Financial Analytics (3)

courses.title: Investment Banking and Private Equity
courses.description: Focuses on capital markets, investment banking, and the rise of private equity, including venture capital, hedge funds, and private equity buyout funds. Examines how current and historical events reshape capital markets and highlights the basic analytics of debt and equity underwriting, venture capital funding, initial public offerings, leveraged buyouts, and mergers and acquisitions. Covers the financial tools, techniques, and best practices used in buyouts by financial buyers and acquisitions by strategic buyers, along with strategic, organizational, and general management issues faced by alternative asset managers. Explores how different players in capital markets find, evaluate, and analyze opportunities; structure deals and affect value creation and value division; add value after transaction completion; and realize objectives such as enhanced market position or a profitable exit. Includes two projects and one team project that provide deeper exposure to analytic techniques and dealmaking skills related to the course.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; FIN301 - Financial Management (3) ; ECON255 - Financial Analytics (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; FIN411 - Advanced Financial Modeling (3) ; ACCTG433 - Advanced Spreadsheet Application (3)

courses.title: Law and Economics
courses.description: This advanced course examines how economic principles explain and inform legal rules and institutions. The course begins with property rights theory, exploring how different rights allocations and enforcement mechanisms affect economic efficiency. Building on this foundation, students analyze contract law through an economic lens. The course concludes with antitrust analysis, where students apply their understanding of property rights and contracts to evaluate market power, competitive effects, and merger policy. Throughout the course, students engage with theoretical models, empirical evidence, and case studies.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3)

courses.title: Financial Economics
courses.description: The central concern of this course is about methods firms use to make financial decisions and economic tools used to make those decisions.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON355 - Investment Analysis (3) ; ACCTG302 - Intermediate Financial Accounting II (3)

courses.title: Labor Economics
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the field of contemporary labor economics as we explore the interactions between firms and workers in the macro economy.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ECON151 - Economic Principles and Problems-Macro (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; AGBUS210 - Agricultural Economics (3) ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3)

courses.title: Industrial Organization
courses.description: The course introduces students to the economics of imperfect competition.  Topics covered include the theory of the firm, market structure, and various aspects of firm strategy such as pricing, advertising, product differentiation, and innovation. Related questions of public policy will also be addressed.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON215 - Quantitative Methods (4) ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4)

courses.title: Senior Capstone
courses.description: This course is designed to be a culminating experience for seniors who explore topics of interest and apply analysis tools developed in their course of study. Students will analyze case studies, take the major fields test, and take further steps to prepare to enter the workforce.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ECON388 - Introduction to Econometrics (3)

courses.title: Principles and Practices of Early Intervention
courses.description: In this course students will be introduced to the field of Early Intervention focusing on supporting families with a child (ren), ages 6 to 17 months. The principles and practices involved include, but are not limited to, a focused look at typical and atypical development of infants, current research into early intervention practices, shared insights from families and professionals in the field, and real case study experiences. Evaluating, planning, and delivering developmentally appropriate, evidence-based coaching for families with infants ages 6 to 17 months will be studied and implemented.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; CHILD210 - Child Development (3) ; CHILD300 - Infant and Toddler Development (3)

courses.title: Early Childhood Curriculum and Fundamentals for Toddlers
courses.description: Theorists, principles, and practices related to the field of early childhood will be examined. Evaluating, planning, and delivering developmentally appropriate, evidence-based curriculum for diverse populations of toddlers and their families will be studied. Including but not limited to toddlers with and without disabilities, toddlers who are considered at risk for a delay, and/or toddlers who are learning English as a second language. The developmental standards (e.g., Early Learning Guidelines, etc.) related to supporting child growth will be introduced. Activity planning skills will be taught and fostered with a focus on domain specific content (e.g., cognitive, communication, social/emotional, motor, adaptive behavior, and aesthetic) and toddler appropriate curricula areas (e.g., Art, math, science, movement, literacy etc.) The course will address licensing standards including completing required Infant/Adult CPR and First Aid trainings, TB testing, and state determined background checks. These must be successfully completed before applying for ECSE 350L Toddler Experience. Finally, this class should be taken the semester before enrolling in ECSE 350B Early Childhood Curriculum & Guidance for Toddlers and the ECSE 350L Toddler Experience.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ECSE341 - Principles and Practices of Early Intervention (2) ; -or- ECSE340 (last offered 2022)

courses.title: Experience with Toddlers
courses.description: Students will utilize assessment, collaboration, and developmental knowledge to design and implement developmentally appropriate activities for toddlers, including those with special needs, through play-based experiences. They will emphasize music, movement, self-help (e.g., snack), language/literacy, creative arts, dramatic play, fine motor, gross motor, sensory exploration, blocks, cognition, and outdoor play. Additionally, they'll learn to implement various interventions supporting children across developmental domains. The course will also cover building relationships and collaborating with families and professionals in early childhood education. Emphasis will be placed on ethical and safety practices in relationships with children and families. In the lab, students will collaborate with families, conduct assessments, monitor progress, and document growth based on individualized plans, family concerns, and child interests.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECSE350A - Early Childhood Curriculum and Fundamentals for Toddlers (2)

courses.title: Early Childhood Curriculum and Fundamentals for Preschool
courses.description: The principles and practices involved in evaluating, planning, and delivering developmentally appropriate, evidence-based curriculum for children in preschool, both with and without disabilities, are studied. The developmental and academic standards (e.g., Early Learning Guidelines, Common Core, etc.) related to curriculum will be introduced. Lesson/activity planning skills will be taught and fostered. Domain specific content will be reviewed for the developmental (e.g., cognitive, communication, social/emotional, motor, and adaptive behavior) and preschool curricular domains (e.g., literacy,  language, affective, Cognitive (including math and science), aesthetics (including music and art),  and physical). The course will address licensing standards including CPR, First Aid, and background checks.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECSE350A - Early Childhood Curriculum and Fundamentals for Toddlers (2)

courses.title: Early Childhood: Teaching Preschool Children
courses.description: Student teachers will design developmentally appropriate lesson plans. The student-teacher candidates will participate in practical hands-on experience working with and developing relationships with preschool-aged children both with and without special needs. In this practicum, child-focused planning will be developed through informal assessments of the child’s needs and interests, referencing their Individualized Education Plans (IEP) when applicable. This course will provide opportunities to carry out child-focused plans and prepare the student-teachers to use core principles, develop appropriate practices, teach preschool curriculum, and implement principles of child guidance. Student teachers will be expected to apply knowledge learned from the seminar associated with this course in their practicum.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ECSE360A - Early Childhood Curriculum and Fundamentals for Preschool (2)

courses.title: Family and Community Relationships
courses.description: This course will give teacher candidates a perspective on providing family-focused services with an emphasis on families who have a child with special needs (birth through adulthood). Important issues to be discussed will be on empowering parents, strengthening family and professional partnerships, and inter-agency collaboration. Teacher candidates will develop a family resource plan. They will have practical experience writing an Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP), and researching, accessing, and linking families with community resources.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR200 - Teaching as a Profession (2)

courses.title: Strategies for Early Childhood Special Education
courses.description: In this course, students will research and apply evidence-based practices related to universal interventions, behavior management, child guidance, and teaching strategies for young children with and without special needs. Students will learn to use theories of direct instruction and collaborate on team interventions. This process will be evidenced as the student works with a case study child and family assessing present levels, implementing the IFSP/IEP process, putting into practice strategies to support identified child goals, and monitoring child responsiveness and progress.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; SPED424 - Assessment and Evaluation (4)

courses.title: Technology for the 21st Century Classroom
courses.description: The focus of this course is to enhance teacher-candidate competence and confidence in fostering learners' use of technology to enhance learning, increase collaboration in a global and digital society, and develop digital citizenship.

courses.title: Motivation and Management
courses.description: This course is intended for all education majors, those with education clusters, and those wanting to improve the management of children in an ecclesiastical or home setting.  It is designed to provide models of discipline practices where agency and respect are fostered and to help bridge the gap between theory and practice through exploration of management and motivation theories, practices, and teaching strategies.  Strategies learned, help in the creation and building of cooperative and inclusive classroom environments where all students are invited to actively participate.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR200 - Teaching as a Profession (2) ; ED202 (last offered 2021) ; SPED200 (last offered 2021)

courses.title: Early Field Practicum
courses.description: The Early Field Experience course follows an introduction to the Framework for Teaching (Danielson), providing experience in a public elementary school setting. Teacher candidates work twice a week in a classroom of elementary-aged students under the supervision of a mentor teacher and attend a weekly seminar on campus throughout the semester. Teacher candidates will implement lesson plans provided by and/or approved by their mentor teachers and regularly reflect on the effectiveness of their work. Lessons are observed multiple times throughout the semester culminating in a formal, formative performance evaluation at the end of the semester conducted by the course instructor.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR325 - Instructional Methods and Technology (3)

courses.title: Elementary Education Motivation and Classroom Leadership
courses.description:
At the end of this course, teacher candidates will understand that all classroom interactions must be genuinely respectful, warm, caring, and sensitive in order to follow the example of the Savior, the Master Teacher. Candidates will know the components of an environment that is permeated by the Spirit
and, as a result, encourage all members of the community to incorporate high standards of learning for themselves and others. Teacher candidates will also understand their role and responsibility in implementing consistent classroom routines, procedures, and transitions to support the development of a productive learning environment. Finally, candidates will know how to develop clear, consistent standards of conduct that encourage appropriate behavior and understand the need for applying those standards with love and patience to help students to effectively govern themselves.

courses.title: Foundations of Literacy Development & Reading Disabilities
courses.description: This course addresses the critical components and theories of literacy (and language) development and provides an introduction to the nature and needs of students with reading disabilities, including dyslexia. The course focuses on scientifically based research on the effects of learning disabilities, including dyslexia, on learning to read and write. The course addresses the historical development of the field of literacy, relevant laws and policies, and the impact on students with learning disabilities, including dyslexia.

courses.title: Elementary Art Methods
courses.description: This course provides K-12 pre-service teachers instructional experience in the visual arts.  Emphasis is placed on the elements and principles of design, integration of the visual arts throughout the curriculum and instructional strategies aligned with the National Art Standards.
courses.prerequisiteText: ED 202 (last offered 2021)

courses.title: Idaho Comprehensive Literacy #2
courses.description: This course is the second in a series of literacy courses, based on the science of reading, that focuses on the Language Comprehension strand of Scarborough's Reading Rope. Students learn how to assess reading fluency, vocabulary, and comprehension, analyze data to guide instructional decision-making, and design instruction to support literacy development for all learners, including English learners and students with reading disabilities such as dyslexia. Students learn to apply textual structure knowledge to promote reading development and support comprehension of children’s literature, content subjects, and disciplinary text. This course also teaches students to identify the characteristics of struggling readers, including dyslexia, and apply appropriate accommodations and adaptations according to laws related to learning disabilities.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR365 - Idaho Comprehensive Literacy #1 (3)

courses.title: Elementary Literacy Practicum
courses.description: The literacy practicum provides ELED, ECSE, and SPED majors opportunities to apply knowledge of literacy development, reading fluency, vocabulary acquisition, comprehension, literacy assessments, and instruction in an authentic learning environment. Teacher candidates make instructional decisions based on the evaluation of literacy assessment data then design lessons centered on learner needs and deliver literacy instruction to elementary-age children. Teacher candidates build expertise in lesson planning and delivery, classroom management, collaboration skills, and professionalism.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ED245 - Early Field Practicum (2) ; ED345 - Idaho Comprehensive Literacy #2 (3)

courses.title: Middle School Practicum
courses.description: This competency-based field experience is designed to apply understanding of learning and teaching in an authentic setting. Students will be working with elementary and middle school age children in public school classrooms or field placements. Through observation, mentoring, planning, and implementation, students will receive teacher-guided instruction to continue building expertise in lesson planning, classroom management, teaching strategies, and professionalism.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR310 - Educational Psychology and Human Development (3) ; EDCOR365 - Idaho Comprehensive Literacy #1 (3)

courses.title: ELED PE, Art, and Music Methods
courses.description: Teacher candidates learn a process to develop and strengthen their creativity to enhance the creativity of the students they teach. Teacher candidates learn how to apply a creativity model to design instruction that integrates human wellness and the arts (P.E., health, music, and art) with content area standards to support learners' cognitive development, communication, and inquiry skills. Teacher candidates contribute to personal, and overall wellness by creating and implementing personalized health and wellness goals.

courses.title: Language and the Brain
courses.description: This course addresses brain function as it relates to language and reading development and variations in visual memory, auditory memory, attention, language function, and auditory processing among students with and without reading disabilities.  The course will also address the neurobiological origins of dyslexia and its effects on language and literacy development, including the role of attention, executive functioning, memory, and processing speed in reading and writing development.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR365 - Idaho Comprehensive Literacy #1 (3)

courses.title: Advanced Phonics
courses.description: This course builds on foundational literacy concepts learned in Idaho Comprehensive Literacy Standard 1 to provide students with a deep understanding of the structures and subsystems of language (phonological awareness, phonics, orthography, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics) and the interrelationship of these literacy elements. Students learn components of instruction necessary to teach the structures of language that lead to fluent reading, reading comprehension, and effective writing. Students also learn to analyze reading and writing errors then plan explicit instruction within a structured literacy framework.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR365 - Idaho Comprehensive Literacy #1 (3)

courses.title: Elementary Math Pedagogy
courses.description: The course will introduce teacher candidates to math pedagogical concepts. Teacher candidates will explore skills and ways of thinking about mathematics and generalize for application within the classroom. By using math manipulatives, the teacher candidate learns the in-depth progression of children's mathematical learning that informs the conceptual understanding of operational algorithms. How to plan for, accommodate, and remediate students' progressions in mathematical understanding will be an additional focus.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR325 - Instructional Methods and Technology (3) ; MATH205 - Mathematical Reasoning for Teachers 1 (3)

courses.title: STEM Methods
courses.description: In this course, we begin to bridge the gap between teaching subjects in isolation and allowing children to see how all things work together. STEM education is all about authentic integration between science, technology, engineering, and math. Teacher candidates will learn and apply essential STEM pedagogical principles to create a scientific inquiry lesson plan that includes standard alignment for all STEM disciplines. Teacher candidates incorporate scientific inquiry, innovative technologies, the engineering design cycle, and data collection and analysis in lesson planning. Participants will also use experiential learning and historical perspectives to develop the ability to make standards-based connections between each STEM discipline.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; SCIED259 - Integrated Science (4)

courses.title: Independent Readings and Projects
courses.description: This course is designed as an independent study program, with content and objectives determined by the student and a faculty member.

courses.title: Elementary Social Studies Methods
courses.description: This course provides K-8 teacher candidates with instructional strategies aligned with the National Council for the Social Studies and Idaho Standards. The ten themes and major concepts of social studies will be emphasized and explored in the construction of an integrated social studies unit of instruction. Perspectives, biases, and sensitivity issues related to diversity, with a focus on American Indians, will be discussed and studied.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ED345 - Idaho Comprehensive Literacy #2 (3) ; HIST115 - History and Civics for Elementary Education (2)

courses.title: Assessment and Evaluation in Education
courses.description: Relying on sound principles of assessment and evaluation in education, this class will give teacher candidates the philosophical foundation and basic tools to create and evaluate assessments that contribute to student learning.  The course will emphasize using assessment as a tool for learning by integrating characteristics of effective assessment and digital tools to help teachers and students evaluate data to make instructional decisions that enhance learning.

courses.title: Elementary Senior Practicum
courses.description: This course is designed to give teacher candidates practical experience in contributing to positive learning environments; designing curriculum, including differentiated unit and lesson planning; developing the dispositions of a professional educator with an emphasis on collaboration;  while working in an elementary school classroom two full days (or their equivalent) in a public school and participating in a weekly seminar.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ED346E - Elementary Literacy Practicum (2)

courses.title: Literacy Assessment and Intervention Methods
courses.description: This course covers effective assessment and intervention principles and practices for a wide variety of students, including those with dyslexia and other reading disabilities. Students will learn how to identify, develop, administer, and interpret various literacy assessments. Students will also learn how to design and implement evidence-based literacy interventions based on assessment data, including explicit, systematic, and multimodal instruction of word identification, decoding, comprehension, writing, and vocabulary strategies. Students will explore the methods and routines of comprehensive literacy intervention programs for multiple levels of literacy acquisition in children (K-12) and adults.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ED345 - Idaho Comprehensive Literacy #2 (3)

courses.title: Practicum in Assessment and Intervention
courses.description: This practicum provides teacher candidates with hands-on experience working one-on-one with students with reading difficulties, including dyslexia. Candidates will apply their knowledge of assessment and intervention by administering literacy assessments, interpreting results, and designing individualized, evidence-based reading interventions. Through explicit instruction, ongoing progress monitoring, and reflection, candidates will refine their ability to implement effective literacy strategies and adjust interventions based on student needs. Additionally, candidates will collaborate with educators to communicate student progress and support learning goals. Performance will be evaluated using the Danielson Framework for Teaching to ensure high-quality instruction and professional growth. This course is not offered in the Spring.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ED454 - Literacy Assessment and Intervention Methods (3)

courses.title: Literacy in the Content Areas
courses.description: In Literacy in the Content Areas, teacher candidates develop an understanding of language and literacy as it applies to teaching content in secondary schools with a focus on English learners and students who struggle with reading and writing. The course emphasizes incorporating reading and writing in the content areas and evidence-based instructional strategies to support all students' literacy development. Teacher candidates develop an understanding of struggling readers and writers, including students with dyslexia, learn how reading and writing difficulties vary in presentation and degree, and federal and state laws pertaining to students with learning disabilities. The course focuses on how reading, writing, and oral language skills are developed and used in discipline-specific curricula, including adaptations to support English learners and struggling readers and writers. Young adult literature is integrated throughout the course.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ED345 - Idaho Comprehensive Literacy #2 (3)

courses.title: Teaching as a Profession
courses.description: Serves as a cornerstone of the Educational Core for all teacher preparation programs. Prepares future teachers to understand the roles and responsibilities of professional teachers, recognize the dispositions and character traits of successful educators, and develop a personal educational philosophy through broadened perspectives and enlightened discernment. Includes a thoughtful study of gospel-themed teaching principles; an introduction to educational philosophies and theories; an overview of the four Domains of Teaching based on current educational research; and a review of relevant historical events and perspectives. Guides serious teacher candidates through a reflective process culminating in an individual statement of personal philosophy that articulates doctrines and principles guiding personalized behavior and decision-making. Although the course focuses on preparing and developing professional teachers, it presents teaching and learning as eternal principles applicable in ourselves, homes, church, and classrooms. Encourages all to increase in wisdom and follow the Savior while striving to become master teachers.

courses.title: Educational Psychology and Human Development
courses.description: Relying heavily on social science, cognitive neuroscience, and the study of Christ as a master teacher, this course is designed to explore child and adolescent development, to identify principles that promote understanding and guide the creation and implementation of purposeful and meaningful learning experiences, and to identify teaching strategies that promote thoughtfulness in both the affective and cognitive domains.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR200 - Teaching as a Profession (2)

courses.title: Assessment Methods and Analysis
courses.description: Examines the purpose, significance, and implementation of assessments in K-12 education. Analyzes the role of assessments in evaluating student learning, monitoring progress, and guiding instructional decisions. Emphasizes differentiating assessments for diverse learners, integrating digital tools and platforms to enhance assessment practices, and analyzing assessment data to extract meaningful insights, inform instruction, differentiate teaching approaches, and support student growth.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR200 - Teaching as a Profession (2)

courses.title: Instructional Methods and Technology
courses.description: Guides teacher candidates in learning and practicing key components of effective instruction used by successful educators, including evidence-based teaching methods, instructional strategies, lesson planning, and instructional technology to engage students in learning.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR200 - Teaching as a Profession (2)

courses.title: Diverse and Exceptional Students
courses.description: Covers the basics of diversity and special education issues with which a typical P-12 teacher will be expected to be familiar. Teacher candidates learn culturally responsive practices and how to employ essential teaching strategies based on students' exceptional needs, abilities, language, and background. Diverse and exceptional students include a varied population that will be spoken of generally, as well as the specific populations of English Learners, students with varying abilities, racially diverse populations, culturally diverse students including those from American Indian populations, etc. Teacher candidates also become familiar with laws and policies governing a teacher's engagement with diverse and exceptional students in the public schools.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR200 - Teaching as a Profession (2)

courses.title: Literacy Foundations
courses.description: Prepares future secondary education teachers to support literacy development among middle- and high-school-age students. Develops understanding of linguistic and neurological literacy development and the distinguishing characteristics of dyslexia and struggling readers and writers. Examines federal and state laws pertaining to learning disabilities specific to literacy acquisition and instruction. Students learn evidence-based instructional practices to support literacy development within their content areas. Prepares Secondary Education majors to take the Idaho Comprehensive Literacy Assessment Standard 5.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR200 - Teaching as a Profession (2)

courses.title: Idaho Comprehensive Literacy #1
courses.description: This is the first in a series of courses, based on the science of reading, to prepare future teachers to successfully guide children to acquire early literacy skills.  This course equips learners with professional-level knowledge of linguistic and neurological literacy development by focusing on the Word Recognition category of Scarborough’s Reading Rope.  Students learn structured literacy instructional practices to support the literacy development of all learners, including English Learners and those with reading disabilities, such as dyslexia.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR200 - Teaching as a Profession (2)

courses.title: Content Area Reading and Writing
courses.description: Prepares teacher candidates with principles, tools, and strategies to foster content literacy across disciplines. Students learn evidence-based instructional practices for teaching reading comprehension, vocabulary acquisition, and writing skills necessary for content and disciplinary reading and writing. This course meets the Idaho literacy requirements for educators teaching at a secondary level. Students will take the Idaho Literacy Standard 2 and 4 exams in this course.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR325 - Instructional Methods and Technology (3)

courses.title: Language Arts Methods
courses.description: In the Language Arts Methods course, students learn how to engage all students in the writing process based on the science of reading. This course teaches students to evaluate various types of writing and use assessment information to provide personalized feedback and support to students with diverse learning profiles. Students learn evidence-based structured literacy practices for teaching developmental spelling and handwriting, written expression, content area writing, conventions, and research skills. Students also learn instructional methods to help all learners develop their writing skills in various formats, including written, visual, digital, and oral communication. Additionally, the course explores the characteristics of struggling writers, such as English learners and students with dyslexia and dysgraphia, and how to adapt instruction to meet their needs.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ED345 - Idaho Comprehensive Literacy #2 (3)

courses.title: Management and Professional Ethics
courses.description: Provides instruction concurrent with student teaching and introduces teacher candidates to the qualities of a positive classroom environment and strategies for establishing routines and procedures to increase instructional time. Presents strategies and frameworks for working with students who exhibit difficult behaviors. Guides teacher candidates in applying learned strategies in the student teaching classroom. Introduces professional standards and the Idaho Code of Ethics to prepare candidates for professional participation in the teaching field.

courses.title: Student Teaching
courses.description: Student Teaching is the culminating experience, the capstone of the academic and professional training of a pre-service teacher. A twelve-week, daily practicum is completed in the public school classroom. A one-hour weekly seminar will serve as the forum in which student teachers can address challenges and concerns while sharing experiences, expertise, and successes. This seminar will also connect to management and student discipline topics coordinated with the ED 450 management course taken concurrently with student teaching. There are a vast number of education students that BYU-Idaho is trying to serve. Because of this, be aware of the following: 1. There is a STRONG probability that your student-teaching placement will be at a distant site.  (Salt Lake City, UT, Ogden, UT; Melissa, TX; Caldwell, ID) 2. Distant-site placements are limited to certain locations that have been organized for BYU-Idaho students. 3. There will be a disruption in your regular routine in order to participate, and you will need personal transportation.

courses.title: Language Assistance for English Language Learners
courses.description: Emphasizes skills that will enable each ESL student to improve his or her English language ability in order to succeed in the college classroom. The course allows students to customize their learning outcomes based on identified needs in the following areas, writing, speaking, vocabulary, and study strategies. Students may register for a .5 - 2.0 credit. The class may be repeated for a maximum of 6.0 credits. The Learning Outcomes for this course are individualized by the students and based on the number of credits the student registers for.

courses.title: English International Language Listening
courses.description:
This course is designed to allow nonnative English speakers with a listening proficiency at or above the Advanced Low-level on the ACTFL scale to receive credit for developing this skill level.  Students are required to demonstrate Advanced Low listening proficiency by passing a certification exam recognized by the BYU-Idaho Department of Languages and International Studies.

This course is available to international online degree-seeking students who speak English as a second or international language.

courses.title: English International Language Speaking
courses.description:
This course is designed to allow nonnative English speakers with a speaking proficiency at or above the Advanced Low-level on the ACTFL scale to receive credit for developing this skill level.  Students are required to demonstrate Advanced Low speaking proficiency by passing a certification exam recognized by the BYU-Idaho Department of Languages and International Studies.
This course is available to international online degree-seeking students who speak English as a second or international language.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EIL170 - English International Language Listening (4)

courses.title: English International Language Reading
courses.description:
This course is designed to allow nonnative English speakers with a reading proficiency at or above the Advanced Low-level on the ACTFL scale to receive credit for developing this skill level. Students are required to demonstrate Advanced Low reading proficiency by passing a certification exam recognized by the BYU-Idaho Department of Languages and International Studies.

This course is available to international online degree-seeking students who speak English as a second or international language.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EIL171 - English International Language Speaking (4)

courses.title: English International Language Writing
courses.description:
This course is designed to allow nonnative English speakers with a writing proficiency at or above the Advanced Low-level on the ACTFL scale to receive credit for developing this skill level. Students are required to demonstrate Advanced-Low writing proficiency by passing a certification exam recognized by the BYU-Idaho Department of Languages and International Studies.

This course is available to international online degree-seeking students who speak English as a second or international language.

courses.title: Reading Comprehension
courses.description: The primary focus of the elective course is understanding, practicing, and applying reading skills, strategies, and college-level vocabulary. The outcomes for this course are based on ensuring that a student is prepared to participate in college-level reading.

courses.title: Basic Writing
courses.description: Teaches basic writing conventions, including the writing process, sentence basics, grammar, punctuation, paragraph and essay development, critical thinking, and the rhetorical situation.  It is recommended for individuals with ACT English score of 17 or below (or a commensurate SAT score).

courses.title: College Reading
courses.description: In this elective course students will develop and apply reading skills for improved textbook comprehension in the arts and sciences.

courses.title: English Language Development - Oral
courses.description: This course focuses on the improvement of English skills for non-native speakers. Oral communication will be emphasized.

courses.title: English Language Development - Writing
courses.description: This course focuses on the improvement of English writing skills for non-native speakers, emphasizes written communication, and prepares students for ENG 150.

courses.title: Writing and Reasoning Foundations
courses.description: Introduces academic inquiry and writing, laying the foundation for further academic and professional development. Students learn to think and read critically and practice the writing process, including invention, research, summary, synthesis and analysis, revision, and editing. Students work on several major writing assignments, including a research project in which they gather information from a range of valid sources, demonstrating they can analyze and use that information purposefully, following appropriate documentation.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the followingOption 1 ; Complete 1 of the following ; ACT English score of at least 17 ; SAT English score of at least 400 ; SATR Writing score of at least 23 ; SATR Reading/Writing score of at least 390 ; TOEFL of at least 80 OR TOEFL score of at least 4.0 for 2026 and later. ; IELTS of at least 6.5Option 2 ; ENG 106 with a grade of C or higherOption 3 ; ENG 106L with a grade of B or higherOption 4 ; ENG 109 with a grade of B or higherOption 5 ; The Write Class exam with a placement of ENG 150 or higherOption 6 ; The Basic Writing exam with a score of 80 or higher

courses.title: Writing and Reasoning Foundations with Support
courses.description: Prepares students to learn and apply basic and advanced writing skills. Students learn to think and read critically and practice the writing process, including invention, research, summary, synthesis and analysis, revision, and editing. Students work on several major writing assignments, including a research project in which they will gather information from a range of valid sources, demonstrating the ability to analyze and use information purposefully, following appropriate documentation. This course fulfills the requirements for English 150 but offers additional instruction and support.

courses.title: Introduction to Literature
courses.description: Introduces literary genres, including the short story, novel, poetry, and drama. Emphasizes skilled reading, analysis, and appreciation of significant examples of literature.

courses.title: Great Books of the World
courses.description: In ENG 217, you will find meaning in the Great Books of the World as you learn to read, appreciate, interpret, and critically analyze books across historical and cultural contexts. Discover the relevance of storytelling as you explore significant themes related to the human condition, engage with life’s profound questions, gain empathy for experiences different from your own, and evaluate for yourself what it means to “seek ye out of the best books words of wisdom” (Doctrine and Covenants 88:118). The course includes reading books of lasting impact, synthesizing and evaluating interpretations, and supporting individual analysis through essays. This course is for students of any major.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: Creative Writing
courses.description: This introductory course focuses on the creation of original works of poetry, drama, fiction, and creative non-fiction.

courses.title: English Education Early Field Practicum
courses.description: Designed under the principles of implicit instruction or exploratory learning, the goal of this course is to help English Education majors explore the profession and gain early experiences in public school teaching through guided inquiry, structured observation, and limited teaching.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; EDCOR200 - Teaching as a Profession (2)

courses.title: Fundamentals of Literary Interpretation
courses.description: Introduces literary genres such as fiction, poetry, drama, and literary theory to students in English, English Education, Humanities, and Interdisciplinary Studies. Prepares students for success in future English classes because they gain the tools to read and analyze literature. Teaches students how to analyze specific details from literary works and then use that analysis to make and support effective written arguments. Students also learn how to use a variety of different theoretical lenses to find new avenues for analyzing and understanding literature. These reading, analysis, and critical thinking skills prepare students for a variety of disciplines or jobs.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: Rhetoric, Design, and Professionalization
courses.description: This course focuses on written and visual rhetoric, using multiple technologies to deliver and enhance a variety of texts aimed at various audiences.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3) ; COMM111 - Writing for Communication Career (3)

courses.title: Special Projects
courses.description: This course is an arranged course that requires Department Chair approval.

courses.title: Advanced Writing and Research
courses.description: Students learn how to reason carefully and express ideas clearly as they respond to a variety of rhetorical situations. Students develop these competencies as they learn to recognize strong arguments, uncover assumptions, evaluate evidence, recognize rhetorical patterns, and infer ideas from data. To apply these skills, students conduct advanced academic research and write in genres that they will use as students, employees, and disciples of Christ such as reports, essays, professional communications, and others.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: Advanced Research and Literary Analysis
courses.description: This course emphasizes academic writing on literature, including close reading, textual analysis, and researched argument.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; ENG251 - Fundamentals of Literary Interpretation (3)

courses.title: Technical Writing and Communication
courses.description: This course prepares students to produce technical and professional documents for a variety of fields.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3) ; COMM111 - Writing for Communication Career (3)

courses.title: Advanced Creative Writing
courses.description: This course focuses on the creation of original writing in a single genre: fiction, poetry, drama, film, or creative non-fiction.  Students may repeat this course for credits and should see schedule for specific offerings.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG218 - Creative Writing (3)

courses.title: Technology for Professional Writers
courses.description: This course introduces students to and provides students with practical experience with industry-standard professional writing tools (e.g., page-design and image-manipulation software and web technologies).
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Introduction to Linguistics and Language Acquisition
courses.description: This course introduces students to linguistics, or the study of language and its structure. Students will learn about phonetics, semantics, syntax, morphemes, pragmatics, as well as the social, cultural, and psychological aspects of language (i.e. sociolinguistics). Students will apply this knowledge to the study of primary and secondary language acquisition and to other professional contexts (professional writing, computer science, cybersecurity, etc.).
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3) ; ENG150P - Writing and Reasoning Foundations with Support (4)

courses.title: Language Theory: Grammar and Usage
courses.description: This course introduces the study of the English language with an emphasis on grammar, usage, semantics, and copyediting.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3) ; COMM111 - Writing for Communication Career (3)

courses.title: Editing
courses.description: Through service-learning-style opportunities, students will develop expertise in comprehensive editing, copy editing, and proofreading.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ENG325 - Language Theory: Grammar and Usage (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; COMM111 - Writing for Communication Career (3) ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: History of English Language
courses.description: This course introduces the study of the English language with a focus on history, influence, nomenclature, and semiotics.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Rhetoric
courses.description: Fundamentals of Rhetoric introduces the study of rhetoric including history, theory, vocabulary, and application. In this course, students will learn to recognize that rhetoric is a dynamic force for shaping discourse communities, ideologies, and nations. This will allow students to better evaluate and articulate arguments as they begin and continue their careers. Students will analyze rhetorical situations and strategies and then apply these concepts in their own writing.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: Writing Instruction Methods
courses.description: The goal of this course is to help English Education majors and minors explore the writing and language components of the language arts curriculum, adopt principles of effective English instruction, and utilize a variety of formal and informal assessments.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR200 - Teaching as a Profession (2) ; EDCOR325 - Instructional Methods and Technology (3)

courses.title: Writing Instruction Methods Lab
courses.description: The goal of this course is to help English Education majors and minors explore the writing and language components of the language arts curriculum, adopt principles of effective English instruction, and utilize a variety of formal and informal assessments.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR200 - Teaching as a Profession (2) ; EDCOR325 - Instructional Methods and Technology (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ENG329 - Writing Instruction Methods (3)

courses.title: British Literature-Medieval and Renaissance
courses.description: This course examines works and authors of the Medieval and Renaissance periods from Beowulf to Milton and the influence of historical events, philosophical ideas, and literary trends.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ENG314 - Advanced Research and Literary Analysis (3)

courses.title: British Literature-Restoration to Romanticism
courses.description: This course examines works and authors of the Restoration, 18th Century, and Romantic periods from Dryden to Keats and the influence of historical events, philosophical ideas, and literary trends.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ENG314 - Advanced Research and Literary Analysis (3)

courses.title: British Literature-Victorian and Modern
courses.description: This course examines works and authors of the Victorian and Modern periods from Carlyle to Eliot and the influence of historical events, philosophical ideas, and literary trends.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ENG314 - Advanced Research and Literary Analysis (3)

courses.title: American Literature - Colonial and Romantic
courses.description: This course examines works and authors of the U.S. Colonial and Romantic periods from Bradstreet to Dickinson and the influence of historical events, philosophical ideas, and literary trends.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ENG314 - Advanced Research and Literary Analysis (3)

courses.title: American Literature - Realism and Modernism
courses.description: This course examines works and authors of the Realism and Modern periods from Twain to O'Connor and the influence of historical events, philosophical ideas, and literary trends on the works and authors.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ENG314 - Advanced Research and Literary Analysis (3)

courses.title: British and American Literature, 1965 to the present
courses.description: This course examines contemporary British and American works and authors from 1965 to the present and the influence of historical events, philosophical ideas, and literary trends.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ENG314 - Advanced Research and Literary Analysis (3)

courses.title: Themes in Literature
courses.description: This course traces an important theme (nature, fantasy, archetypal quest) as expressed in various literary genres and through historical periods. (See schedule for specific course theme.)
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: Fiction
courses.description: This course explores the development and characteristics of short fiction and/or the novel.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ENG314 - Advanced Research and Literary Analysis (3)

courses.title: Poetry
courses.description: This course introduces major poets and analyzes significant poetry, indicating cultural and artistic relationships to other art forms.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ENG314 - Advanced Research and Literary Analysis (3)

courses.title: Drama
courses.description: This course explores literary study of plays, encompassing their historical, critical, and social contexts.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; ENG314 - Advanced Research and Literary Analysis (3) ; TA115 - Introduction to Theatre (3)

courses.title: Literary Non-fiction
courses.description: This course involves extensive reading, writing, and study of creative non-fiction works by major authors.  (Includes memoir, personal essay, nature, travel, and literary journalism.)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ENG314 - Advanced Research and Literary Analysis (3)

courses.title: Children's Literature
courses.description: This course introduces students to the spectrum of children's literature, past and present.

courses.title: Young Adult Literature
courses.description: This course focuses on evaluating and promoting young adult literature. Designated sections will also help students learn to teach young adult literature in public schools.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: US Multicultural and World Literature
courses.description: This course is a survey of US multicultural and world literature written in or translated into English from across various cultural, national, and linguistic boundaries. Students will be exposed to artistic expression and diverse perspectives from at least 4 different cultures or countries, focusing on literature from the 19th-21st centuries. Elements to aid in this study may include history, religion, tradition, mythology, folklore, politics, belief systems, language and dialect, family structures, etc. of the cultures or countries. This course will help students appreciate, understand, and learn from different perspectives and cultures from God's children from all around the world and help students become more conscientious global citizens able to interact with cultures different from their own.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: Major Authors
courses.description: This course focuses on the life and works of one major writer or the life and works of a few related authors.  (See schedule for specific offerings.)
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: Shakespeare
courses.description: This course focuses on the works of Shakespeare and the culture of Elizabethan England.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: Practicum in Applied English Studies
courses.description:
This is an experiential course designed for students looking to bridge the gap between academic study and real-world application. Students develop the ability to translate and narrate their English studies skills and experiences to current and future professional opportunities. 
This course is for students who are (or will be during the semester) participating in an approved English-related professional experience: These include English-relevant campus jobs, English-relevant volunteer or client-based work, the BYU-Idaho English Scholars Program, the BYUI English Study Abroad Program, or an extended and self-initiated English-relevant professional project. 

Emphasis is placed on learning and applying to their professional experience core employability competencies, such as establishing expectations, cultivating key relationships, contributing effectively to teamwork, embracing diversity, giving and receiving feedback, and managing projects efficiently. These skills are invaluable for both current job-seekers and future career opportunities.

Additionally, students gain practical experience in creating compelling job application materials. This includes crafting an updated resume, drafting persuasive cover letters, refining elevator pitches, and honing interview skills – all tailored to effectively communicate their unique experiences and skills to potential employers.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3) ; COMM111 - Writing for Communication Career (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ENG252 - Rhetoric, Design, and Professionalization (3) ; COMM130 - Visual Media (3)

courses.title: Practicum in Teaching College English
courses.description: This course gives students a foundation in composition theory and pedagogy with a specific focus on how these theories/practices are applied in GE writing classes in universities and dual enrollment writing classes in secondary education.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG314 - Advanced Research and Literary Analysis (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3) ; ENG325 - Language Theory: Grammar and Usage (3) ; ENG328 - Fundamentals of Rhetoric (3)

courses.title: English Internship
courses.description: This course offers students credit as they apply their English studies in a practical, professional environment through a structured internship. Students gain hands-on experience, develop industry-relevant skills, and integrate academic learning with real-world application. Students are encouraged to arrange their own internships. The English Department is also available to guide students to opportunities. Students can register for up to six credits total (one credit equals 70 hours of internship work). This class is repeatable up to six credits. Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges but do incur an administrative fee equivalent to one credit hour’s tuition. Internship credits are not included in the 12-credit fulltime student minimum.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ENG252 - Rhetoric, Design, and Professionalization (3) ; ENG316 - Technical Writing and Communication (3)

courses.title: Genres of Professional Writing
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth look at the fields of professional writing and technical communication. Students will learn of the theories that shape this discipline and gain a broader understanding of the professional writing field.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG328 - Fundamentals of Rhetoric (3)

courses.title: Creative Writing and Publishing
courses.description: This course focuses on the creation of advanced writing in fiction, poetry, drama, film, or creative non-fiction and familiarizes students with the marketplace for creative work.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ENG218 - Creative Writing (3) ; ENG318R - Advanced Creative Writing (3)

courses.title: Teaching English in Secondary Schools
courses.description: This course comprehensively prepares English Education majors for the secondary English language arts classroom where they are charged with the responsibility to teach ALL English Language Arts skills: reading, writing, listening, speaking, viewing, and language study. In this senior level practicum course, students learn how to adopt principles of effective planning and preparation, management of the learning environment, instruction, and assessment.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG329 - Writing Instruction Methods (3) ; ENG329L - Writing Instruction Methods Lab (1) ; EDCOR325 - Instructional Methods and Technology (3)

courses.title: Teaching English in Secondary Schools Lab
courses.description: This practicum lab course comprehensively prepares English Education majors for the secondary English language arts classroom where they are charged with the responsibility to teach ALL English Language Arts skills: reading, writing, listening, speaking, viewing, and language study. In this senior level practicum course, students learn how to adopt principles of effective planning and preparation, management of the learning environment, instruction, and assessment.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG329 - Writing Instruction Methods (3) ; ENG329L - Writing Instruction Methods Lab (1) ; EDCOR325 - Instructional Methods and Technology (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ENG430 - Teaching English in Secondary Schools (3)

courses.title: Studies in Literary Theory
courses.description: This course surveys predominant critical theories for literary study and interpretation.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG251 - Fundamentals of Literary Interpretation (3) ; ENG314 - Advanced Research and Literary Analysis (3)

courses.title: Themes in Rhetoric
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth look at a particular area in the academic discipline of Rhetoric. Each semester, this course will focus on a particular rhetorical theme or area of study. In the past, these have included sports rhetoric, visual rhetoric, political rhetoric, digital rhetoric, and rhetoric and musicology. Students should contact professors to identify specific themes for each semester. Students will apply these theories as they compose rhetorical analysis and research essays.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG328 - Fundamentals of Rhetoric (3)

courses.title: Advanced Professional Writing
courses.description: In this course students will develop expertise in professional writing, comprehensive editing, copy editing, proofreading, document production, and design. Students will gain practical experience through service learning opportunities.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG321 - Technology for Professional Writers (3) ; ENG326 - Editing (3)

courses.title: Senior Writing Seminar
courses.description: This course provides a capstone experience for English Majors. In depth reading, discussion, and careful analysis of consequential literary works are at the heart of this senior level course. In-class presentations of student research are required. English 495 culminates in a significant research paper representing each student's best work as a critical thinker and interpreter of literature.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG251 - Fundamentals of Literary Interpretation (3) ; ENG314 - Advanced Research and Literary Analysis (3) ; ENG325 - Language Theory: Grammar and Usage (3)

courses.title: Aerobic Fitness
courses.description: Students will participate in group exercise classes in a social environment developing their fitness through energizing cardio and resistance workouts choreographed to music. This course would be an excellent introduction to group fitness for those who plan to take ESS 204.

courses.title: Water Aerobics
courses.description: This fitness course is for students who would like to participate in a non-weight-bearing, cardio-conditioning class. Students will use the resistance of the water to improve their cardio-respiratory system, muscular strength, endurance, flexibility, and body composition with a low and minimal impact on joints and muscles. They will learn water aerobic skills and will be required to teach what they have learned to classmates for specific class activities.

courses.title: Introduction to Lifetime Sports and Holistic Wellness
courses.description: This course explores the intersection of physical activity, social development, and spiritual well-being through participation in various lifetime sports. Through practical engagement and reflective exercises, students will gain a deeper understanding of how lifelong physical activity contributes to holistic wellness. Additionally, students will develop biographical sketches of their peers and demonstrate proficiency in the rules of different lifetime sports.

courses.title: Exercise Science Orientation
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to introduce students to the movement sciences, explore careers in the movement sciences, identify the typical skills found among those graduates that are successful in related business, identify future courses that will foster knowledge and skills in specific areas, identify acceptance criteria for professional health programs, and identify exit routes for those less likely to be admitted into professional health programs.

courses.title: Military Physical Fitness
courses.description: This is a military style fitness program open to all students.

courses.title: Archery
courses.description: In this course students will demonstrate proficiency with compound and recurve bows as well as identify differences between styles and makes of bows. Students will demonstrate knowledge of proper form and how to improve shooting technique and each will understand basic mechanics of the bow along with proper maintenance of equipment, including bows and arrows. This knowledge will allow them to continue the sport outside of class.

courses.title: Body Weight Management
courses.description: This course is designed to teach students a comprehensive approach to weight loss. While anyone is welcome in the course, the format will be of greatest benefit to individuals trying to lose weight. Each day, students will engage in a variety of physical activities including running, calisthenics, resistance training, and other exercise. Students enrolled in the class must be able to exercise. As part of the curriculum, students will have an outside-of-class exercise requirement. Students will also be taught the principles of healthy eating and how to calculate caloric requirements, as well as develop comprehensive programs for themselves as part of class requirements. The course meets the fitness class requirement for exercise physiology majors.

courses.title: Swimming Beginning
courses.description: This course is a fitness course and is designed for beginners or non-swimmers.  Instruction will be given in the five basic strokes, and basic.  Students will learn water safety skills such as treading water, floating,  and safety in/around pools and open bodies of water.  Students will become efficient enough for a 15 minute non-stop swim and will be able to describe how the pursuit and maintenance of physical fitness enhances the vibrancy of an individual's spirit and fosters communication with the Holy Ghost. Students will apply concepts from physiology, kinesiology, and nutrition to develop personal exercise routines.

courses.title: Swimming Intermediate
courses.description: This course is designed for students with some swimming ability. Students will learn the fundamentals of swimming, including six different strokes, water polo, snorkeling, diving, and competitive skills. A 12-minute swim test will be administered for distance at the beginning and the end of the semester to show improvement. Students will describe how the pursuit and maintenance of physical fitness enhances the vibrancy of an individual's spirit and fosters communication with the Holy Ghost. They will apply concepts from physiology, kinesiology, and nutrition to develop personal exercise routines.

courses.title: Weight Training
courses.description: This course is designed to teach the basics of resistance training. Instruction will include how to safely perform traditional resistance exercises. Students will also learn how to apply the training principles of overload, progression, periodization, and the basics of program design. Specific assignments will assess a student's ability to design a basic individualized program based on principles taught in class. Students will train with weight equipment each day and a portion of the grade is based on participation. This class meets the fitness class requirement for Exercise Physiology majors.

courses.title: Aerobic Fitness Techniques
courses.description: Students will learn to lead group exercise classes including HIIT, circuit, cycling, dance fitness, step, cardio kickboxing, and group resistance training.  Participants will teach 10 sessions to classmates and receive feedback on their teaching.  Upon successful completion of this course, students will be prepared for a national group fitness instructor certification, specifically the Primary Group Fitness Instructor Certification from the Athletics and Fitness Association of America (AFAA). This course makes students strong candidates to teach group fitness for the BYU-Idaho Campus Recreation Program.

courses.title: Intramurals
courses.description: This course covers the history, philosophy, administration, and leadership of a campus Intramural Program.  Students will be required to work lab hours in the rec Sports (Intramural) Activities Program and learn how to administer to injuries, misconducts, and day-to-day operations such as games management, scheduling, score keeping, and event/tournament management.  Students will also play every sport to learn rules, proper field/court set up, and scenario training.

courses.title: Sports Officiating: Indoor Sports
courses.description:
This course provides a comprehensive exploration of the principles and practices of sports officiating. It may include various indoor sports such as water polo, volleyball, basketball, etc. Designed for students interested in developing a deep understanding of officiating techniques, rules interpretation, and decision-making skills, this course combines theoretical knowledge with practical experience.
 
Note: Students are required to complete 20 hours of practicum experience supporting campus recreation sports.

courses.title: Sports Officiating: Outdoor Sports
courses.description:
This course provides a comprehensive exploration of the principles and practices of sports officiating. It may include various outdoor sports such as football, soccer, lacrosse, softball, etc. Designed for students interested in developing a deep understanding of officiating techniques, rules interpretation, and decision-making skills, this course combines theoretical knowledge with practical experience.
 
Note: Students are required to complete 20 hours of practicum experience supporting campus recreation sports.

courses.title: Lifeguarding
courses.description: This course includes American Red Cross certifications for pool lifeguards, CPR for the professional Rescuer, AED, First Aid, and Oxygen administration.   Students will correctly demonstrate and performing CPR, First Aid, use of an Automated External Defibrillator (AED), and Oxygen Administration.  Each will identify, match, and recall the knowledge and ethical obligation they should incorporate into the status of an American Red Cross Lifeguard.

courses.title: Water Safety Instructor
courses.description: Students will produce and deliver three 15-minute lessons covering aquatic knowledge and skill sessions demonstrating and performing skills such as swimming strokes, diving, and basic water safety which they will be required to teach as Red Cross instructors.  Students will also identify, match, and recall the knowledge and ethical obligation they should incorporate into a position as an instructor.

courses.title: Professional Experience Seminar
courses.description: In this course students will demonstrate leadership skills and an ability to cooperate with others by applying concepts from upper-division coursework to manage risk, lead activities, and teach course-specific skills and concepts.  The outcomes for each situation will vary based on the objective. While some students will act in the role of a grader, others will learn to teach classmates in labs.

courses.title: Health and Wellness Coaching
courses.description: This course teaches students how nutrition, fitness, lifestyle behaviors, and other factors impact disease processes, performance, quality of life, goal achievement, and weight management efforts. Students will demonstrate competence in their skills to administer selected health and fitness assessment protocols and properly interpret the result. They will design effective and appropriate nutrition, fitness, and weight management intervention programs and strategies for an individual client.  They will recognize and present their perceived strengths and weaknesses in the area of mentor-client interaction and group teamwork toward program implementation and serve the campus community by administering the assessment protocols and designing intervention programs through the university's Wellness Center.

courses.title: Fundamentals in Coaching and Sports Psychology
courses.description: This course will have students analyze and study the mind and movement as it applies to the psychological principles of activity in sports and activity while exposing students to principles and practices of effective coaching. The course will include coaching philosophy, sport psychology, motivational technique, and an examination of different coaching styles.

courses.title: Sports Medicine
courses.description: This course is designed for health professional students, i.e. athletic trainers, coaches, health and physical educators, physical therapists, EMT's and premedical students as an introduction to sports medicine professional development and responsibilities, injury prevention and risk management, and injury management.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; BIO264L - Human Anatomy and Physiology I Lab (1) ; BIO264 - Human Anatomy and Physiology I (3) ; BIO460 - Human Anatomy with Lab (4)

courses.title: Sports Medicine Lab
courses.description: In this course injury prevention, examination, and treatment techniques will be presented, i.e. taping/bracing, tests and measures, and use of therapeutic modalities.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ESS349 - Sports Medicine (3)

courses.title: Athletic Training Clinical Experience
courses.description: This course may be repeated for a maximum total of 3 credits with no more than 1 credit per semester.  Thirty contact hours are required for each credit.  The contact hours per week are to be arranged with an instructor.  This course will cover the practical application and clinical experience in health skills and use of therapeutic modalities.  A maximum of 3 credits will apply toward graduation.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ESS349L - Sports Medicine Lab (1)

courses.title: Lifeguard Instructor
courses.description: In this course, students will prepare and teach three 20-minute lessons that cover an array of skills and life-guarding knowledge. They will also set up and run an out-of-class practice session for students in the Lifeguard Training course. The practice session must be a minimum of one hour in length. They will also identify, match, and recall the knowledge and ethical obligations they should incorporate into a position as an instructor. Lifeguard certification is required before enrolling in this class.

courses.title: Aquatics Management
courses.description: This course will provide students with the basic knowledge and skills to manage an aquatic facility. Coursework will include such topics as pool chemistry, filtration, health codes, lifeguard selection, injury prevention, and risk management. Segments on water activities and programs including water aerobics, competitive swimming, and snorkeling will be explored.

courses.title: Exercise Physiology
courses.description: This course teaches a branch of physiology that deals with the functioning of the human body during exercise and movement. Students will gain an in-depth understanding of energy metabolism, muscle function, cardiovascular function, respiration, hormonal control, and neurophysiology during rest and in response to acute and chronic exercise. In addition, these concepts will be applied to environmental conditions, age, and gender and used to explain concepts and trends in exercise and human performance.

courses.title: Exercise Physiology Lab
courses.description: This course introduces some of the fundamental laboratory techniques used for the field of Exercise Physiology including metabolic function, lactate testing, oxygen consumption, and measurement of work and power, among other topics.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; BIO460 - Human Anatomy with Lab (4) ; Take the following course(s): ; BIO264 - Human Anatomy and Physiology I (3) ; BIO264L - Human Anatomy and Physiology I Lab (1)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ESS375 - Exercise Physiology (3)

courses.title: Foundations in Exercise Oncology
courses.description: Cancer is the second leading cause of death in the United States but there are over 18 million cancer survivors in the United states. Many of these cancer survivors face numerous challenges such as losing muscle mass, strength, and experiencing anxiety, depression and fatigue. Exercise has been shown to be a powerful tool to help ameliorate many of these challenges and is becoming recognized as a needed resource for this population. In this course we will talk about what cancer is, how exercise impacts it and how you can safely create an exercise program for people who are going through cancer treatments or are survivors of cancer. By the end of the course, you will be ready to take the Exercise Oncology Instructor Certification exam through Maple Tree Cancer Alliance.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ESS375 - Exercise Physiology (3)

courses.title: Strength Training Theory and Application
courses.description: This course has specific application for individuals pursuing personal training, strength, and conditioning, or coaching careers. Aspiring physical therapists may benefit from this course as well. Students will learn the theories and methods of anaerobic conditioning with specific emphasis on resistance training and apply these concepts as they develop programs for males and females.
