courses.description: This course is a project-based class that introduces the spatial concepts and theory of GIS (Geographic Information Systems), building on skills developed in GIS 150. Students use industry-standard GIS software (ArcGIS Pro) to apply location analytics and solve spatial problems in diverse disciplines. Students are prepared for intermediate-level GIS internships and to apply GIS in varied fields and careers. This course is part of the GIS certificate and minor.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; GIS150 - Spatial Thinking (1)

courses.title: UAS-Based Mapping
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the collection and processing of low-altitude aerial imagery using small unmanned aircraft systems (sUAS), commonly known as drones. Topics include aerial mission planning, sUAS flight operations best practices, and aerial image interpretation and analysis using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) software. sUAS regulations (14 CFR Part 107) and safety practices are emphasized with the aim of enabling students to pass the FAA Remote Pilot Certificate examination.

courses.title: Web and Mobile GIS
courses.description: This course introduces students to online GIS (Geographic Information Systems) and mobile data collection using industry-standard GIS apps. Students use GPS enabled devices (such as a phone) to gather point, line, and polygon field data. Students post-publish maps and download field-collected data to generate professional maps and dashboards. The course reinforces concepts learned in introductory GIS and shows how desktop, mobile, and web GIS are linked. Prior understanding of GIS is required.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; GIS250 - Spatial Analysis (3) ; GEOL 340 (last offered 2022) ; GEOG 230 (last offered 2022)

courses.title: Remote Sensing
courses.description: This course introduces students to basic theory, history, and practical applications of remote sensing technology. Topics include aerial image interpretation, resolution, sensor types, georegistration, vegetation indices, and image classification. Students will use Geographic Information Systems software packages to analyze and interpret aerial image data.

courses.title: Applied GIS for Social Sciences
courses.description: This course is a project-based class in which students broaden their skills and gain practical experience in GIS (Geographic Information Science) related to their discipline. Students will use industry software and will also acquire and use GIS freeware. In GIS II for Social Sciences, the emphasis is on social science applications of GIS, network analysis, geostatistics, parcel mapping, urban planning, suitability studies, modeling workflows, and the Python-GIS interface. Students complete an independent spatial analysis-based project. This course is intended for majors in political science, international studies, economics, business, and other social science disciplines.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; GIS250 - Spatial Analysis (3) ; -or- GEOL 340 (last offered 2022) ; -or- GEOG 230 (last offered 2022)

courses.title: Applied GIS for STEM
courses.description: This course is a project-based class in which students broaden their skills and gain practical experience in GIS (Geographic Information Science). Students use both industry-standard software and GIS freeware. In GIS II for STEM the emphasis is on machine learning, watershed analysis, geostatistics, infrastructure networks, Lidar, suitability studies, workflow modeling, and the Python-GIS interface. Students complete an independent spatial analysis-based project.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; GIS250 - Spatial Analysis (3) ; -or- GEOL 340 (last offered 2022)

courses.title: GIS Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

This course consists of practical experience working in GIS. After identifying a possible internship, get approval from the department internship coordinator and then sign up for the internship through the university Career Navigator website. Students who are unable to identify an internship opportunity are encouraged to complete a capstone research project (GEOL490r) under a geology or geography faculty mentor.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; GIS250 - Spatial Analysis (3)

courses.title: Ancient Greek I
courses.description: An introduction to Classical and New Testament Greek.

courses.title: Ancient Greek II
courses.description: Second semester Classical and New Testament Greek.  Includes readings from the Greek New Testament and an introduction to scholarly resources for New Testament study.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; GREEK101 - Ancient Greek I (4)

courses.title: Ancient Greek 3
courses.description: Completion of Classical and New Testament Greek grammar. Includes readings from the New Testament and classical Greek texts.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; GREEK102 - Ancient Greek II (4)

courses.title: Readings in Ancient Greek
courses.description: Readings in the Ancient Greek.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; GREEK201 - Ancient Greek 3 (4)

courses.title: Career and Self Discovery
courses.description: Students will take an active approach to self-discovery by learning about tools and resources that help connect their identity and purpose to future possibilities in the world of work. They will broaden awareness of their talents, gifts, and eternal identity through guided self-reflection, weekly journaling activities, and career assessments. Weekly readings will illustrate how to find passion, purpose, place, and calling. Students will explore labor market data (job demand, starting salary, benefits, associated skills, and educational requirements) and engage in informational interviewing to increase knowledge about specific careers and industries in an area of interest.

courses.title: Strategies for Academic Success
courses.description:
This course may not be taken as a student's only enrolled course. 

This course allows students to create academic success goals for a semester and implement a plan of action utilizing various strategies and campus resources to accomplish the goals under the direction and supervision of the instructor. This course includes class time and tutoring time.

courses.title: Time Management and Concentration
courses.description: This online 1.0 credit course is taught on the block (six weeks) so that students can quickly apply the strategies learned to their studies. Students can expect the course to require approximately 4-5 hours of their time per week. In this course, students will learn how to realize their goals through the use of semester, weekly, and daily charts and schedules wherein priorities are set and carried out. Students will learn how to schedule study times for maximum efficiency and will learn strategies for overcoming procrastination. To improve their concentration, students will assess their physiological preparation for learning, become more attuned to their learning style preferences, identify personal internal and external distractions, and apply strategies for overcoming these. Finally, students will learn how good concentration can enhance their ability to retain information learned.

courses.title: Note Taking and Textbook Study
courses.description: This online 1.0 credit course is taught on the block (six weeks) so that students can quickly apply the strategies learned to their studies.  Students can expect the course to require approximately 4-5 hours of their time per week. In this course, students will not only learn note-taking and textbook reading strategies but will also be given assignments to apply what they are learning to their other classes. The skills learned in this course can bless students academically, as well as in their professional and personal life as they perform readings and take notes. The ability to implement these skills will help students to identify the most important ideas that they read or are exposed to.

courses.title: Critical Thinking and Test-Taking Skills
courses.description: This six-week, online, 1.0 credit course is taught on the block (six weeks) so that students can quickly apply the strategies learned to their studies.  Students can expect the course to require approximately 4-5 hours of their time per week. In this course, students will not only learn critical thinking and test-taking strategies but will also be given assignments to apply what they are learning to their other classes. Like any skill learned, without application, there will likely be little retention or change. The activities of the course are not intended as "busywork" but as an opportunity to implement what they learn and to evaluate what strategies will work best for them. The skills that students learn in this course can bless them as a student, as well as in their professional and personal life as they learn to think critically and prepare effectively for the exams of life.

courses.title: Technology Basics
courses.description: This course will have mid-week and weekly assignments, a final project, and an end-of-class final. The weekly assignments and final project will determine your class score.

courses.title: Student Instructor Training
courses.description: This course is designed to assist student instructors in developing teaching skills. This course provides pedagogical skills as well as content knowledge training to promote student instructor success.

courses.title: Tutor Training: Reading
courses.description: Tutor training to meet student needs and national certification. Training in establishing rapport, assessing needs, teaching study habits, and helping students accept responsibility.

courses.title: Tutor Training: Writing
courses.description: Tutor training to meet student needs and national certification. Training in establishing rapport, assessing needs, teaching study habits, and helping students accept responsibility.

courses.title: Tutor Training: Math
courses.description: Math Tutor training in fundamental education principles and tutoring techniques as well as certification in basic math courses.  Training in establishing rapport, assessing needs, teaching study habits, and helping students accept responsibility.

courses.title: Tutor Training: Study Skills
courses.description: Tutor training to meet student needs and national certification. Training in establishing rapport, assessing needs, teaching study habits, helping students accept responsibility.

courses.title: Instructor Mentor Training
courses.description: This course is designed to assist instructor mentors in developing and strengthening discipleship and leadership qualities. This course incorporates leadership effectiveness at three levels: individual, team, and organization.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; GS108A - Student Instructor Training (1)

courses.title: Realize Vision
courses.description: BYU-Idaho is founded upon true principles that are fundamental to the gospel of Jesus Christ.  In this course you will be introduced to these inspiring principles which will significantly enhance your learning and experience at BYU-Idaho.  The student will also come to understand the prophetic vision and mission given to BYU-Idaho and its students and how to realize those blessings in their own lives. Additionally, this course provides students entering the online degree program the opportunity to learn of the resources available to them through BYU-Idaho and gain the skills and understanding necessary to successfully complete the program. This includes working one-on-one with an academic advisor to create a Graduation Plan that fits with their academic goals.

courses.title: Career Development
courses.description: In this course, students develop resources, professional connections and essential employability skills to obtain or improve employment in a field related to their university certificate. Students will network and apply for job opportunities in their industry. The life-long skills gained in this course are valuable for both active and future job seekers.
courses.corequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; ART235 - Graphic Design (3) ; AUTO332 - Engine Management Systems (2) ; BUS210 - Small Business Creation (3) ; BUS375 - Business Law (3) ; ITM327 - Data Warehousing (3) ; COMM150 - Interpersonal Theory and Practice (3) ; COMM310 - Creating Online Media (3) ; CONST315 - Field Scheduling (3) ; CONST391 - Construction Scheduling (3) ; CSE210 - Programming with Classes (2) ; CSE212 - Programming with Data Structures (2) ; ECON150 - Economic Principles and Problems-Micro (3) ; FCS340 - Money Management (3) ; FHGEN242 - Introduction to Evidence Analysis (3) ; ME272 - Mechanical CADD and GD&T (3) ; MKT353 - Web Business Creation (3) ; OSH450 - Environmental Sanitation and Water Quality Management (3) ; PSYCH111 - General Psychology (3) ; PUBH320 - Human Diseases (3) ; EDCOR340 - Diverse and Exceptional Students (3) ; WDD230 - Web Frontend Development I (3) ; WDD231 - Web Frontend Development I (2) ; -or- AGBUS 197R (last offered 2025) -or- CS 246 (last offered in 2023) -or- HTMBC 340 (last offered 2025) -or- SMMBC160 (last offered 2025)

courses.title: Decision Making and Leadership
courses.description: Students and instructors in this course use case studies to explore principles of decision-making and disciple leadership.

courses.title: Professional Projects
courses.description: This course helps students apply the concepts and skills they have learned in their coursework to a professional project.  During the first week of the course, students identify an appropriate 50-hour project they can use for the course.  Projects fit into one of three areas:  work-related projects, service and volunteer projects, or personal professional development projects. In addition to completing the 50-hour project, students complete tasks and assignments that help promote professional development and career readiness.

courses.title: Exploring Careers in Health Services
courses.description: Many people interested in the Health Professions have a strong desire to help others. This course will introduce you to the many health professions available to you as you consider a career in the Health Field. This course will cover the avenues to careers such as Nursing, Medicine, Public Health, Allied health careers, Occupational Health, Healthcare Administration and so much more. This is a survey course and will discuss how to achieve a solid career in the Healthcare industry.

courses.title: Medical Terminology
courses.description: This is an introduction course into the language of medicine.

courses.title: Introduction to Healthcare Administration
courses.description: In this course students will learn the history, structure, and function of the United States healthcare system. Throughout the course, students will also learn about organizational governance, basic management principles, the nation's physician workforce, healthcare industry regulation, health insurance, and healthcare reform. Lastly, students will work in teams to present on current healthcare issues and discover job opportunities within the healthcare industry.

courses.title: Healthcare Law and Ethics
courses.description: This course introduces students to the major legislation and laws pertaining to healthcare in the United States. Employment laws and ethical issues in healthcare are also discussed.

courses.title: Managing Healthcare Provider Organizations
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce students to the specific issues and body of knowledge pertaining to healthcare quality and safety, volume growth, marketing, and exceptional financial performance. Emphasis is placed on improving processes and systems that will enhance the quality of patient care in healthcare provider organizations. Students will also collaborate on several cases studies and display presentation skills throughout the course.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HCA285 - Introduction to Healthcare Administration (3)

courses.title: Healthcare Systems
courses.description: This course teaches students how to better organize the delivery of healthcare.  Students will learn the major types of morbidity associated with the organs and systems of the human body, as well as the physicians, medical devices, and procedures utilized to treat and rehabilitate patients.  Students will also learn methods and tools that can be used to improve the coordination of healthcare over the full cycle of care.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HCA285 - Introduction to Healthcare Administration (3)

courses.title: Healthcare Strategy
courses.description: This course teaches students how to effectively develop a strategy and guide an organization through the steps of a strategic planning process.  Additionally, students will learn how to create a solid cultural foundation upon which to build a strategy, including increasing their own level of emotional intelligence and understanding of how to create high-performing teams.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HCA285 - Introduction to Healthcare Administration (3)

courses.title: Healthcare Insurance Industry
courses.description: This course identifies third-party reimbursement and payment methodologies, including, but not limited to, differentiating between Medicare and Medicaid, managed care, and self-insuring. Students will analyze the business office functions that facilitate a healthcare organization to maximize reimbursement and to negotiate and administrate contracts with healthcare insurance companies. It prepares students to purchase healthcare insurance for their families and employees, as well as to critically assess current healthcare insurance issues and legislation.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HCA285 - Introduction to Healthcare Administration (3)

courses.title: Healthcare Finance
courses.description: This course focuses on the financial accounting, managerial accounting, and finance management functions specific to healthcare provider organizations in the United States. Emphasis is placed on reimbursement by healthcare insurance companies and public programs, as well as on the tax implications of for-profit and not-for-profit healthcare providers. This class requires prerequisite accounting and finance courses.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; HCA285 - Introduction to Healthcare Administration (3) ; FIN301 - Financial Management (3)AND ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ACCTG210 - Principles of Accounting I (3) ; -OR- ACCTG180 (last offered 2025)

courses.title: Healthcare Operations
courses.description: This healthcare operations course is designed to prepare students to be contributing, value-added members of quality departments and teams within healthcare provider organizations. To this end, the course deepens students' understanding of principles of operational effectiveness and efficiency and applies this deeper understanding to the provision of healthcare services. Students will learn and apply methods of continuous process improvement to enhance quality of care and patient safety. These methods will prepare the students to improve healthcare delivery processes by reducing delays, eliminating errors and waste, increasing capacity, and managing variability. Students will also learn and apply data measuring and analyzing skills. The successful completion of the course will provide students the opportunity to earn a Lean Six Sigma Healthcare Yellow Belt Certification. Costs for the Lean Six Sigma portion of the course (Approximately $150) will be billed through the BYU-Idaho Bookstore.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HCA285 - Introduction to Healthcare Administration (3) ; HCA340 - Managing Healthcare Provider Organizations (3) ; SCM361 - Operations Management (3)

courses.title: Healthcare Administration Capstone
courses.description: This course allows students to deepen their understanding of material taught in prior healthcare administration and business courses by applying such in case studies. Students, working collaboratively, will enhance their leadership and analytical skills. Considered the "culminating experience" of the Healthcare Administration program, students will integrate academic coursework and practical experiences to develop skills which will allow them to transition from the academic environment to the competitive healthcare marketplace.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HCA285 - Introduction to Healthcare Administration (3) ; HCA290 - Healthcare Law and Ethics (2) ; HCA340 - Managing Healthcare Provider Organizations (3) ; HCA360 - Healthcare Systems (3) ; HCA380 - Healthcare Strategy (3) ; HCA395 - Healthcare Insurance Industry (3)

courses.title: Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

HCA 498R is the internship required for all Healthcare Administration students. Internships must be completed in healthcare provider organizations and must be administrative in nature. Patient care will not be approved. Students must complete HCA 285 and HCA 340 before registering for and completing HCA 498R. However, students are encouraged to complete as many HCA courses as possible before completing their required internship. Additionally, students are encouraged to limit the number of other classes/credits take during the internship semester.

courses.title: Biblical Hebrew I
courses.description: This course covers Genesis through Deuteronomy. The focus of the course is for students to achieve a knowledge of Biblical Hebrew vocabulary and Biblical Hebrew grammar sufficient to be able to translate using Hebrew text and lexicon. Students will learn how to pronounce and read the Hebrew text out loud. Much of the time in this course centers on translating a few important chapters, but the course will also include a review and survey from Genesis to Deuteronomy.

courses.title: Biblical Hebrew II
courses.description: This course covers Joshua through Malachi. This course emphasizes and adds to the skills acquired in the HEB 101. The focus of the course is for students to enhance and augment their knowledge and expertise from HEB 101. This course also adds Biblical Hebrew poetry in the translations. Much of the time in this course centers on translating a few important chapters, but this course will also include a review and survey from Joshua to Malachi.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HEB101 - Biblical Hebrew I (3)

courses.title: History Skills and Careers
courses.description: This course provides students an introduction to BYU-Idaho's history program, the nature of historical study, and careers in history and related fields. It will also introduce students to key skills for succeeding as history students.

courses.title: History and Civics for Elementary Education
courses.description: This survey course deepens understanding of history, civic, and economic content rooted in curriculum taught in elementary schools. The course is focused on major concepts and ideas found in K-8 social studies standards and teacher qualification exams.

courses.title: U.S. History to 1877
courses.description: This is an introductory survey of American history from the pre-Columbian era to 1877.

courses.title: U.S. History Since 1877
courses.description: This is an introductory survey of American history from 1877 to the present.

courses.title: World History to 1500
courses.description: A broad survey course of the history of world civilizations from their beginnings to AD 1500.

courses.title: Modern World History
courses.description: This course will focus on the development and interactions of the major world civilizations (both Western and non-Western) from the Columbian Exchange to the present.

courses.title: Introduction to Secondary Methods
courses.description: This course is an introduction to methods of effective teaching for secondary education majors.

courses.title: Middle School Practicum
courses.description: This competency-based field experience is designed to apply an understanding of learning and teaching in an authentic setting. Students will be working with middle school age children consistent with each students' content specific area of emphasis/minor. Through observation, practice, and reflection, teacher candidates will continue developing expertise in instructional planning, enhancing learning environments, instructional pedagogy and delivery, and professionalism. Mentor teachers and faculty supervisors will provide regular feedback to candidates through multiple formative evaluations.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; EDCOR200 - Teaching as a Profession (2) ; EDCOR310 - Educational Psychology and Human Development (3) ; EDCOR365 - Idaho Comprehensive Literacy #1 (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST115 - History and Civics for Elementary Education (2) ; HIST120 - U.S. History to 1877 (3) ; HIST201 - World History to 1500 (3)

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: This course allows students to engage in specific historical topics through directed readings, special projects, or work study.

courses.title: Writing and Research in History
courses.description: This course covers the nature and philosophy of history with emphasis on developing the research and writing skills needed in historical study.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HIST104 - History Skills and Careers (1)

courses.title: Ancient Greece and Rome
courses.description: In this course students will survey Greek or Roman History with one or two cultural/literary topics that will be covered in more detail.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Medieval History
courses.description: In this course students will survey the history of the Middle Ages with a focused study on selected topics.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Renaissance and Reformation
courses.description: This course will cover the major influences and accomplishments of the Renaissance and Reformation, especially evolution of thought.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Early Modern European History
courses.description: This course is an introductory survey of early modern European history, from the fifteenth century to the late eighteenth century. Organized chronologically and thematically, it examines developments from the invention of the printing press to the eve of the French Revolution. Major themes will be studies of the Renaissance, Protestant and Catholic Reformations, the Scientific Revolution, global effects of European exploration and expansion and the rise of Absolutism, culminating with a study of Enlightenment ideologies.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Modern European History
courses.description: This course covers Europe from 1750 to the present with a particular emphasis on its intellectual and industrial leadership in the world as well as the perils of nationalism and the promise of European integration.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: The Trojan War
courses.description: This course explores some of the methods used to uncover the historical reality of the legendary Trojan War in the Bronze Age.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: The Golden Age of Athens
courses.description: This course examines the fifth century BC in Athens particularly through its cultural output.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Roman Imperialism
courses.description: This course explores the question of how a republic acquired an empire and covers the events and historiography of the rise of the Roman Empire.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Augustus and the Roman Empire
courses.description: This course examines the collapse of the Roman Republic and the creation of the Roman Empire under the Emperor Augustus.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Anglo-Saxon England
courses.description: This course examines the political, economic, social, and cultural development of Anglo-Saxon society from its beginnings in the fifth century until the Norman Conquest of 1066.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: The Crusades
courses.description: This course focuses on the causes and effects of the armed Christian pilgrimages to the Near East beginning in the eleventh century with a consideration of related movements in places like Spain and Livonia.  Consideration of issues such as just war theory, religious violence, and colonialism will also be included.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: The Byzantine Empire
courses.description: This course explores the history and culture of the Byzantine Empire from about 300-1453.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: The Medieval Papacy
courses.description: This course explores the history of the institution of the papacy and the lives and ideas of many of its leaders.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: The Hundred Years War
courses.description: This course explores the history of the conflict known as the Hundred Years War and its political, military, and economic impact on both England and France.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: The Holocaust
courses.description: This course is an in-depth study of the Holocaust in mid-twentieth-century Europe and its ramifications.  Students will research primary accounts from perpetrators, bystanders, rescuers, victims, and resisters.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3) ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3)

courses.title: Middle East: Muhammad to 1800
courses.description: The course covers the Middle East, Southwest Asia, and North Africa from the 6th century through the 18th century AD.  The history, culture, religion, economics, and politics of the region will be examined.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Modern Middle East
courses.description: The course covers the Middle East, Southwest Asia, and North Africa, focusing on the 19th and 20th centuries.  The history, culture, religion, economics, conflicts, and politics of the region will be examined.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: The Islamic World
courses.description: This course explores Islam as a global phenomenon in its historical, geographical, and sectarian contexts. Specific lessons introduce students to Islamism and fundamentalism, as well as theories of Islamic government, Islamic economics, and Islamic banking.

courses.title: History of East Asia
courses.description: This course introduces the history of China, Japan, India and neighboring countries, stressing the period since European colonial expansion.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: South Asia
courses.description: This introduces the history of South Asia from the Indus River Civilization to the modern period. The history, culture, and religion of the region will be considered as well as the influence it exerted in other areas of Asia and the West.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Africa since 1400
courses.description: This course covers the major trends in African history from the advent of Europeans in Africa in the mid-1400s.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Colonial Latin American History
courses.description: This course is an in-depth study of Latin America from pre-Columbian era to the Independence of new nations in Latin America (ca. 1830).  Students will analyze primary documents from various indigenous and Spanish sources and examine how new societies develop.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3) ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3)

courses.title: Modern Latin American History
courses.description: This course is an in-depth study of Latin America from post-Independence (ca. 1830) to the present. Students will analyze primary documents from various sources and examine how these new nations developed.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: The American West
courses.description: This course covers the exploration and development of the western United States from 1800 to the present with emphasis on cultural interaction and the mythic imagery of the west.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Early American History to 1800
courses.description: This course covers the exploration and development of the western United States from 1800 to the present with emphasis on cultural interaction and the mythic imagery of the west.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Civil War and Reconstruction
courses.description: This course explores the origins of the American Civil War, examines the major campaigns, investigates reconstruction, and evaluates the legacy of this era.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: U.S. Industrial Age 1870-1945
courses.description: This course investigates of the rise of modern political, social, and economic structures and values in America from 1877-1918.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: United States History Since 1945
courses.description: This course explores the United States as a superpower from the Cold War to the present with a particular emphasis on social, political, economic and cultural changes preceding and succeeding the Vietnam War.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: U.S. Constitutional History and Law
courses.description: This course explores the foundations of constitutionalism, the development of the federal system, the principles of judicial review, nationalism and sectionalism, commerce, due process, equal protection, and civil rights.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: The History of Film in America
courses.description: This course will explore film in America in three senses: first, the film industry itself as a major part of the totality of American history, second, individual films as historical artifacts that give insight into the eras that produced them, and third, films as agents of historical change that transform the public that embraces them.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: U.S. Women's History
courses.description: This course covers all major topics related to U.S. Women's History, waves of feminism, and the conceptual and theoretical controversies over the place of women.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Special Topics in History
courses.description: Explores a unique and specialized topic in history as determined by the instructor.

courses.title: History of Peace
courses.description: This course explores the religious, philosophical, and political histories of efforts to overcome violence and establish peace, both culturally, and structurally. It traces the development of various concepts of peace in eras from ancient to modern and in cultures and geographies from across the globe.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3) ; PEACE101 - Conflict and Peace (3)

courses.title: Environmental History of Protected Landscapes
courses.description: This course examines the history of the relationship between humans and the environment by focusing on the development of national parks, nature reserves, and other protected landscape systems.  After discussing foundations of environmental history, the concept of publicly protected areas is studied from its genesis and evolution in the United States to its diffusion around the world.  Selected international case studies focus on the applicability of the U.S. developed model to diverse physical and cultural environments.  International perspectives, policies, and institutions are then considered.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: Public History
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the ideas and methods of public history with an emphasis on the practical application of research, writing, and critical thinking skills in the public sector at venues such as museums, state and national parks, archives, the media, etc.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3)

courses.title: History of Religions
courses.description: This course will provide an overview of the development of the discipline of History of Religions, its primary concerns, theories and methodologies, and practical application in the study of a particular religious tradition within its historical context.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3) ; POLSC200 - Research Methods (3) ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3) ; PEACE101 - Conflict and Peace (3)

courses.title: Secondary Methods
courses.description: A final, pre-student teaching course for secondary education majors and minors in the social sciences that will provide some instruction in writing objectives, reading strategies, writing assessments, writing lesson plans, and using various instructional methods in actual teaching experiences.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HIST206 - Introduction to Secondary Methods (3)

courses.title: Senior Thesis
courses.description: A capstone course for senior students in which they produce a significant scholarly research report on a topic of their choice, subject to the approval of the course instructor.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HIST300 - Writing and Research in History (3)

courses.title: History Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

An internship is a cooperative program between the BYU-Idaho Department of History, Geography, and Political Science and an approved organization.  Professional internships correlate actual work experience with course work, provide students with knowledge of career opportunities, and give students work experience in preparation for employment after graduation.  Ideas for internships are developed by the student in consultation with the department internship coordinator.

courses.title: Introductory Plant Identification
courses.description: This course teaches the identification, landscape value, and cultural requirements of annuals, perennials,  ground covers, ornamental grasses, deciduous, and evergreen trees.

courses.title: Introduction to Landscape Architecture and Design
courses.description: This is an exploratory course for all majors who may be interested in landscape architecture and design as a career. A prerequisite course for higher-level landscape design and construction courses. The course introduces and applies the fundamentals of landscape design as it pertains to private residential scaled projects. The history, theory, graphics, and design process of landscape architecture are covered. Students will learn the elements and principles of design, spatial composition, and graphic representation relevant to landscape architecture and design.

courses.title: Floral Design
courses.description: Students will take a beginning look at the world of floral design. Course instruction focuses on the principles and elements of design as applied to floral art. The student will also learn about proper care and handling of fresh flowers, and how they are harvested and distributed around the world. Students will learn to identify the most popular flowers in the floral industry. Students will participate in hands-on floral design in weekly labs.

courses.title: Landscape Digital Media
courses.description: This entry-level course introduces students to technical software and digital programs common in the landscape design profession. Digital programs include AutoCAD, Adobe Photoshop, Adobe InDesign, Sketchup, and Lumion. A prerequisite course for higher-level landscape design and construction courses.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HORT230 - Introduction to Landscape Architecture and Design (3)

courses.title: Practicum in Landscape Management
courses.description: As part of a landscape maintenance crew, students will learn practical, hands-on techniques, maintaining local church properties to industry standards. Crews will be operated by One Grounds Management.

courses.title: Practicum in Floral Design
courses.description: This course provides hands-on training and instruction in retail floristry to prepare students for internships and employment in the floral industry. Emphasis will be placed on practicing floral skills and techniques, floral nomenclature and floral merchandising. Practicum students will also have the opportunity to help design flowers for campus events such as weekly devotionals, and graduation.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HORT235 - Floral Design (3)

courses.title: Practicum in Plant shop
courses.description: This course applies business practices as it pertains to managing a retail garden center and plant boutique business operation. The course involves supervised practical experience in developing skills in plant sales, marketing, advertising, production, maintenance, and management.

courses.title: Introduction to Arboriculture
courses.description: Arboriculture is the cultivation of trees and shrubs especially for ornamental purposes. In this course students will have the opportunity to explore the world of trees and how to care for them. Students will be provided with the skills for basic tree management through lecture and hands-on lab experiences.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; APS122 - Introduction to Plant Science (3) ; APS220 - Horticultural Soils (3)

courses.title: Landscape Management
courses.description: This is a hands-on course in which students will manage landscape spaces, including opportunities to work in the Thomas E. Ricks Gardens on campus. Students will learn about proper landscape management practices relating to both the biotic and abiotic worlds. A field trip is required.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; APS122 - Introduction to Plant Science (3)

courses.title: Plant Propagation
courses.description: This course provides a fundamental working knowledge and implementation of commercial plant propagation. Principles include plant and seed physiology, environmental influences, sexual propagation (seed germination and production), and asexual propagation (cuttings, grafting, budding, layering, and micropropagation).
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; APS122 - Introduction to Plant Science (3) ; BIO180 - Introduction to Biology I (3) ; BIO208 - Introduction to Plant Biology (4)

courses.title: Woody Plant Identification
courses.description: This course provides an understanding of the use of woody plants in the exterior environment for home and commercial landscaping. Students learn plant identification, growth characteristics, usage, care, and design values as they pertain to the woody plant horticulture industry. Focus is on trees, shrubs, and groundcovers, and being able to apply these skill sets. Students may have the opportunity to travel and study plants in the landscape industry.

courses.title: Native Plant Identification
courses.description: This course provides the basic skills to identify native plants of the Intermountain West. Students will also learn useful characteristics (e.g., edible, medicinal, and drought-tolerant plants) and how plants interact in natural ecosystems to conserve natural resources and sustain animal life.

courses.title: Interiorscaping
courses.description: This course provides an understanding and use of plants in interior environments from home decor (plant parenting) to commercial interiorscaping businesses. Students learn the names, behaviors, and characteristics of plants that are typically used indoors, which are indigenous to tropical climates. They also learn how to help them acclimatize and survive where the light, soil, water, and nutrients are adjusted to sustainably maintain their health and beauty in conditions less than ideal for their optimum growth. Students will also learn and apply design principles using these plants in interior spaces.

courses.title: Wedding and Event Planning
courses.description: This course is for students who are interested in becoming event planners, or who are interested in learning how to plan and implement creative and exciting events. Event planning can be a fulfilling career and this course enables students to learn the leadership, teamwork, and organization skills involved in the dynamic world of event planning.  Students will be involved in hands-on preparation for class events, and will also participate in class projects that teach beginning wedding and event planning skills.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HORT235 - Floral Design (3)

courses.title: Greenhouse Operations
courses.description: In greenhouse operations, students will learn about greenhouse construction, environmental control, pest control, and plant culture including the production of greenhouse floral crops.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HORT320 - Plant Propagation (3)

courses.title: Advanced Wedding and Event Planning
courses.description: This course provides students the opportunity to expand their knowledge of the wedding and event planning world, as they work together to plan a large department event that promotes the art of floral design. Students will have the opportunity to see their vision come to fruition as they develop, plan, and create an event from scratch. This course is repeatable so that students may increase their responsibility through multiple opportunities to stage an event by participating more than once during their tenure on the campus. Students will also have the opportunity to dive deeper into the event planning world through class projects and assignments.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HORT235 - Floral Design (3) ; HORT328 - Wedding and Event Planning (2)

courses.title: Landscape Competition
courses.description: This course is for students selected to participate in the annual National Collegiate Landscape Competition (NCLC) event. The course is designed to assist students with their transition to the world of work and participate in a skills-based landscape competition. Actively participate in a world-class career fair. This course requires travel to and from the event as a part of the course.

courses.title: Horticulture Business and Bidding
courses.description: This course teaches students general business practices as they pertain to Horticulture including estimating, bidding, and contracting procedures. Students will learn the importance of implementing an estimating strategy covering three principal concepts including producing the product, general conditions, and overhead markups. The course introduces budget development including operating budgets and a five-step forecasting process. Students will learn and apply equations of the estimating system for equipment, materials, labor, and overhead recovery.

courses.title: Floriculture Applications
courses.description: Students will travel to an international conference held in California to review and study the floriculture industry, its leaders, and the interactions of these businesses on a global scale. This course focuses on the current developments of businesses in the floriculture industry including research, production, and marketing.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HORT320 - Plant Propagation (3)

courses.title: Advanced Landscape Design
courses.description: This is an advanced landscape design course building upon experience gained from the prerequisite course, HORT 230 - Introduction to Landscape Design. The course explores spatial composition, planting design, material selection, sustainability, and water-wise landscaping in a broader range and expanded complexity of site and context. Students will be exposed to and use computer-aided drafting programs common in the landscape industry.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HORT230 - Introduction to Landscape Architecture and Design (3)

courses.title: Advanced Floral Design
courses.description: Students will enhance their floral skills as they focus on more advanced skills and designs associated with the retail floral world including, funerals, holidays, and everyday designs. Students will learn styles from the history of floral design, and practice using the Elements and Principles of Design to create beautiful, well-made designs. Weekly hands-on labs will allow students to practice their basic skills and move onto more difficult territory, such as speed and efficiency. Students will dive deeper into the business side of owning and running a retail flower shop and focus on pricing, ordering, holiday inventory, and marketing.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HORT235 - Floral Design (3)

courses.title: Floral Design Capstone
courses.description: This course is designed to be the capstone for the student’s floral design education. In this course, the student will explore contemporary floral design. This course is also designed to assist the student in recognizing how design styles and culture nurture human society, and how it influences the way we use floral materials. We will explore floral design competitions, certifications, and industry partners. This course will push students to expand their knowledge about floral design styles, skills, and creativity. It will help the student identify what kind of floral designer they have become.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HORT435 - Advanced Floral Design (2)

courses.title: Bridal Couture Floral Design
courses.description: This class is the perfect opportunity to learn bridal floral design and advance to a professional level of design.  The student will learn techniques to create several different styles of bridal bouquets, produce large and small-scale designs for weddings and events, and the pricing strategies to create a successful wedding flower business. The student will learn how to consult with brides about flowers and prices in a professional manner. This course is repeatable so that students can have the opportunity to have more hands-on practice if they choose to repeat the course.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HORT235 - Floral Design (3)

courses.title: Landscape Construction Documentation
courses.description: Students will learn the landscape construction process including construction documentation and opportunities for hands-on construction. Students will learn basic components of and produce landscape layout and materials plans, grading and drainage plans, landscape lighting plans, irrigation diagrams, planting plans, and an assortment of construction details. The course covers design and construction techniques for materials and structures including: paving, retaining walls, steps, lumber structures, lumber decking, planting design, water features, swimming pools, landscape lighting and utilities, etc.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HORT430 - Advanced Landscape Design (3)

courses.title: Nursery Management
courses.description: This course focuses on the development, organization, infrastructure, and operations of a production nursery. The course will cover production principles, practices, and strategies for wholesale and retail marketing of nursery crops. Students will travel to the regional nursery production conference held in Boise. The course will concentrate on the development of these skills as it applies to the production and marketing of nursery crops.

courses.title: Cut Flower Crops
courses.description: This course develops the knowledge and skills needed to operate a commercial specialty cut flower business. It includes the development, propagation, scheduling, harvesting, and marketing of specialty cut flowers and business operations.

courses.title: Potted Plants
courses.description: This course teaches students about commercial production, harvesting, marketing, and scheduling of bedding plants and potted commercial crops.

courses.title: Edible Landscaping
courses.description: This course teaches the principles and elements of designing an edible landscape for the home environment.  It includes vegetable and fruit culture, production, and design principles as it apply to creating a residential edible foodscape, food forest, and potager.

courses.title: University Events Florals
courses.description:
Being a part of the floral industry is an exciting and fast-paced environment. This class will help give students real-life experience in planning and executing the requests from BYU-Idaho and their event coordinators. 
The purpose of this course is to give students opportunities to fulfill the requests that the University has, and for the students to find enjoyment and fulfillment in meeting those requests.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HORT235 - Floral Design (3)

courses.title: Introduction to Kinesiology and Biomechanics
courses.description: In this course students will effectively communicate with and teach one another using correct anatomical and directional terminology.  They will analyze and identify physical activity movements from a kinesiological and biomechanical basis.  Students will explain the guidelines and demonstrate the basic skills of muscle stretching and strengthening, correctly demonstrate between normal and pathological posture and gait pattern, and then apply appropriate corrective interventions to selected anatomical deviations.

courses.title: Applied Kinesiology and Assessment
courses.description: This is an interactive course designed to provide students who are interested in PT, OT, chiropractic, AT, or PA with a profound understanding and application of advanced kinesiological principles and orthopedic musculoskeletal assessment techniques. It focuses on advancing students' knowledge and skills in kinesiology, emphasizing the application of hands-on orthopedic musculoskeletal assessment techniques and developing a caring clinical presence consistent with that of a disciple of Jesus Christ. Through a comprehensive exploration of manual muscle testing, joint special tests, and assessments related to sensation, reflexes, balance, coordination, posture, and gait, students gain the tools to progress musculoskeletal rehabilitation safely and effectively. This is a course that will advance students in their preparation for graduate school and help them stand out as an applicant who possesses such advanced skills and knowledge at an undergraduate level.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the followingOption 1: ; Take the following course(s): ; BIO264 - Human Anatomy and Physiology I (3) ; HRHP359 - Introduction to Kinesiology and Biomechanics (3)Option 2: ; Take the following course(s): ; BIO460 - Human Anatomy with Lab (4)

courses.title: Biomechanics of Sport and Exercise
courses.description: This course is designed to foster a profound understanding of how physical laws intricately shape human motion in our daily lives. Throughout this exploration, we will delve into key topics, including qualitative biomechanics, linear and angular kinematics, linear and angular kinetics, and injury and tissue mechanics. These principles will be actively applied to general activities such as walking, running, and jumping, and real-world scenarios, encompassing exercise techniques, physical training, injury prevention, and physical rehabilitation.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; HRHP359 - Introduction to Kinesiology and Biomechanics (3)

courses.title: Discovery and Discernment Through the Arts
courses.description: Introduces students to the basic elements of creation in theatre, the visual arts, music, literature, and film. The course also presents principles of interpretation to find meaning in the arts and promotes discovery of that which is "virtuous, lovely, good report or praiseworthy" in the humanities.

courses.title: Searching for Meaning in the Ancient World
courses.description: Written on the Temple of Apollo at Delphi was the maxim "know thyself." Through examination of ancient myth, literature, art, philosophy, and history, students will study and apply principles from the great cultures of the ancient and medieval worlds to their own life circumstances. Within the heroic journey construct, from the Call to Adventure through the Mastering of Two Worlds, emphasis will be placed on helping the individual to know oneself in relation to their personal past and future potential.

courses.title: Searching for Meaning in the Modern World
courses.description: Introduced to the wider world, the heroine of Shakespeare's THE TEMPEST exclaims, "O brave new world." Her father says, " 'tis new to thee." We are influenced by family, friends and rivals and also by those who have gone before. Poets, musicians, painters, and authors have shaped us, whether we know it or not. As McCullough explains, "We walk around everyday, everyone of us, quoting Shakespeare, Cervantes, Pope. We don't know it, but we are, all the time. We think this is our way of speaking. It isn't our way of speaking - it's what we have been given. The laws we live by, the freedoms we enjoy, the institutions that we take for granted...are all the work of other people who went before us." Through examination of modern literature, art, philosophy, and history, students will study significant people and cultures and apply principles learned to their unique life circumstances.

courses.title: Modern Arts and Propaganda
courses.description:
This course will focus on the use of propaganda, art, and other forms of persuasion starting with the Modern Era (approximately post-1860) and continuing to the present. Students will experience this topic through various social issues and cultural influences from around the world, including the visual, performing, and literary arts. This course emphasizes the development of aesthetic judgment and critical thinking.
Note: Students cannot receive credit for more than one of the following courses: FDHUM 214, FDCA 204 and FDHUM 103. (FDCA 204 and FDHUM 103 are no longer offered.)

courses.title: Global Humanities
courses.description: An interdisciplinary survey of the significant intellectual and artistic achievements of global cultures (e.g., Africa, Asia, and Latin America) through selected works of literature, philosophy, visual art, music, and cinema, as well as a comparative examination of their values and aesthetics with those of European and United States cultural expression.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3) ; -or- HUM305 (last offered 2023)

courses.title: Junior Seminar in the Humanities
courses.description: A junior-level seminar in Humanities focused on a single theme or topic, explored across multiple art forms. The course will help refine individual student's research, oral presentation, writing and critical thinking skills, while deepening their understanding of the chosen topic.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; HUM201 - Searching for Meaning in the Ancient World (3) ; HUM202 - Searching for Meaning in the Modern World (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3) ; -or- HUM305 (last offered 2023)

courses.title: Travel Studies
courses.description: This course emphasizes self-guided study and one-on-one interaction with faculty members.  Students and teachers work together to create a viable research study plan focusing on a specific topic related to the Humanities department European Travel Study itinerary.  This course aims to provide exposure to and develop a deeper understanding of a specific aspect of the Humanities in western culture (religion, literature, art, and/or architecture) through extensive on-site experience, coupled with pre- and post-trip research.

courses.title: Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

 An internship is a cooperative program between the BYU-Idaho Department of Humanities & Philosophy and an approved organization. Professional internships are intended to connect students' coursework with real-life work experience. Likewise, internships provide students with knowledge of career opportunities, in addition to preparation for employment after graduation. The student, in consultation with the department Internship Coordinator, develops potential ideas for internships.

courses.title: Introduction to Interdisciplinary Studies
courses.description: This course explores interdisciplinary studies and how to succeed in a world that values diverse perspectives in learning, work, service, and leadership. Students will learn about innovation and how to tackle complex problems by integrating different viewpoints. Additionally, students will start their professional journey by connecting with the university's career planning services and earning BYU–Idaho Career Center Certification(s).

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: This course covers current topics in Interdisciplinary Studies.

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Innovation
courses.description: This course helps students deepen their understanding of interdisciplinary studies.  During the course, students will review the traits and skills that lead to interdisciplinarity.  They also learn how to recognize and think critically about disciplinary perspectives and insights.  Students then learn how to use interdisciplinary integrations and understanding to address complex issues.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; IDS101 - Introduction to Interdisciplinary Studies (1)

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

The internship should reflect the interdisciplinary nature of the student's degree. Admission to the class is by application to the Internship Office. Applications are available through I-Plan. Students must obtain an internship and be enrolled in the course within the first three weeks of the semester; complete reports and evaluations; and work a minimum of 100 hours with a minimum of ten hours per credit hour each week for a minimum of 7 weeks. 

Content and Topics: All Interdisciplinary Studies students must obtain and complete an internship.  Ideally, the internship will be employment experience based on the academic areas incorporated into the interdisciplinary degree and the career goals of the student.
