courses.title: Interdisciplinary Capstone
courses.description:
Students will create an approved capstone project or paper to showcase the skills and competencies developed in their interdisciplinary major. Senior students will work closely with a professional mentor, faculty advisor, and/or peers to develop a project or research paper that demonstrates the fusion of their undergraduate coursework and experiences. Projects and papers should be significant and relevant to the student's academic or career objectives. Students in this course will demonstrate senior-level proficiency in research, visual communication, writing, and presentation skills.

Content and Topics: The capstone project is the culminating experience of the Interdisciplinary Studies Degree.  Students will propose, complete and present a project that is academically and professionally meaningful based upon their areas of study and career goals.

courses.title: Introduction to International Studies
courses.description: This course provides potential International Studies majors an opportunity to survey five separate areas of emphasis within international studies, the academic demands of the major, and possible career and post-baccalaureate options arising from this major.

courses.title: Cultural Paradigms
courses.description: The course will deal with examining and contrasting cross-cultural data from across the globe.

courses.title: East Asia Culture
courses.description: The history, governments, culture, religion, society, and current events of East Asian countries including, but not limited to, China, Japan, Korea, Mongolia, and Taiwan.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: Russian Culture
courses.description: This course is an introduction to Russian culture, literature, art, music, and history, taught in English.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: Eastern Europe Culture
courses.description: The history, governments, culture, religions, society, and current events of Eastern European countries including, but not limited to, Ukraine, the Balkans, the Baltic States, Poland, Hungary, Romania, Albania, and other former communist states.

courses.title: Western Europe Culture
courses.description: The history, governments, culture, religion, society, and current events of Western European countries including, but not limited to, Great Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Switzerland, Spain, Portugal, and Scandinavia.

courses.title: Chinese Culture
courses.description: This course consists of an examination of Chinese culture from ancient to modern times.  Topics vary, but may include: geography, history, politics, family, social issues, religion, language, literature, philosophy, and current issues.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: Southeast Asia Culture
courses.description: The history, governments, culture, religion, society, and current events of Southeast  Asian countries including, but not limited to, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Vietnam, Indonesia, Singapore, and Philippines.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ENG150 - Writing and Reasoning Foundations (3)

courses.title: Middle Eastern Culture
courses.description: This course looks at the history, governments, culture, religion, society and current events of Middle Eastern countries including, but not limited to, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Iran, Israel, Syria, Jordan, Egypt, and Kuwait.

courses.title: African Culture
courses.description: This course evaluates the "whys" and "hows" of modern Africa from historical, geographical, political, and economic perspectives of select African cultures.

courses.title: Latin American Culture
courses.description: This course looks at the history, governments, culture, religion, society, and current events of Latin America including, but not limited to, Mexico, Guatemala, Panama, Brazil, Argentina, Venezuela, Chile, and Colombia.

courses.title: Internship in International Studies
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

This internship is a cooperative program between the BYU-Idaho International Studies program and an approved organization. Professional internships correlate actual work experience with course work, provide students with knowledge of career opportunities, and give students work experience in preparation for employment or graduate school upon graduation. The student, in consultation with the program's internship coordinator, develops ideas for internships.

courses.title: International Studies Experience
courses.description: This course is required for students not completing INTST 398R (Internship in International Studies).  The student, in consultation with the International Studies internship coordinator, selects a foreign study experience related to language and area focus.  Students are required to purchase emergency medical insurance through BYU-Idaho.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; INTST300 - Cultural Paradigms (3)

courses.title: Independent Study International Studies
courses.description: This course consists of independent projects monitored through periodic conferences and assessments by the instructor.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; INTST300 - Cultural Paradigms (3)

courses.title: Capstone in International Studies
courses.description: This course consists of a seminar in International Studies for students in their senior year devoted to current topics and global affairs as determined by the instructor.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; INTST300 - Cultural Paradigms (3)

courses.title: International Study Pre-departure
courses.description: Required for all students participating in Semester Abroad Programs. The course must be completed prior to international departure. Covers discipleship and diplomacy, health and safety, culture acquisition, etc.

courses.title: Introduction to Cloud Technologies
courses.description: This course introduces current technologies and their impact on business operations and products. It is intended for anyone who wishes to understand how businesses leverage technology to solve real world problems.

courses.title: Introduction to Databases
courses.description: Covers the basic elements of database management systems. The course introduces students to the concepts of logical and physical relationships in a data model and the concepts of inner and outer joins. Students will use a computer-aided software engineering (CASE) tool to design, create, and query a database.

courses.title: Introduction to Linux
courses.description: Describes the Linux operating system and exposes students to the most common distributions of Linux. The course teaches how to log in and explore before explaining the file system, manipulating files, and how to use the Linux Command Line Interface (CLI) or shell. The course also teaches how to work with file permissions, security updates, processes, and shell scripting.

courses.title: SQL
courses.description: Focuses on learning how to write Structured Query Language (SQL) to interact with databases for various data retrieval and reporting needs. Students create tables, constraints, indexes, and views; insert, update, delete, and query data. SQL activities examine how to write cross joins, inner joins, outer joins, common table expressions (CTEs), subqueries, and composite queries that use set operators. SQL statements explore built-in database functions, data fabrication, hierarchical queries, pivot operations, and conditional logic.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CSE110 - Introduction to Programming (2) ; ITM111 - Introduction to Databases (3) ; -or- CIT160 (last offered 2023)

courses.title: Portfolio Service Project
courses.description:
The purpose of this experience is to actively pursue the mission of BYU-Idaho; "develop disciples of Jesus Christ" (University Mission Statement), and service plays an important role in this process. Students will seek to put into practice the skills and knowledge gained through their initial course of study (e.g. 100 and 200 level courses). Students are asked to find and engage in volunteer service that focuses on benefiting others.

Please be aware that service work is considered outward facing. As the sponsoring organization for this course, the service provided should not benefit BYU-Idaho as this detracts from the service orientation. Also the service should not benefit BYU-Idaho when a comparable paid job exists (e.g. TA, web designer, programmer, tech support, student support, market researcher, SOC analyst, tutor, etc.) as it could potentially create a violation of the Fair Labor Standards Act.

courses.title: Introductory Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap. 

This course is designed as a CIT sophomore-level capstone experience where a student applies the skills previously learned in computer information technology/information systems in a real-world environment.

courses.title: Cloud Foundations
courses.description: This course introduces virtual cloud computing concepts and the building block services of Amazon Web Services (AWS). Organizations leverage cloud computing services to have on-demand delivery of IT resources. Students will learn how to evaluate the requirements of an organization and understand when AWS services benefit in providing value for IT solutions.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ITM101 - Introduction to Cloud Technologies (2) ; ITM112 - Introduction to Linux (2) ; CSE111 - Programming with Functions (2) ; DS250 - Data Science Programming (2) ; BA315 - Business Analytics (3)

courses.title: Applied Cloud Computing
courses.description: Allows students to take their cumulative knowledge and apply it to several real-world applications using a cloud computing platform. Students define project requirements, pitch their ideas, and ultimately build the solutions.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ITM300 - Cloud Foundations (3)AND ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; WDD131 - Dynamic Web Fundamentals (2) ; CSE111 - Programming with Functions (2)

courses.title: Database Administration
courses.description: Serves students interested in database deployment and management, including the DevOps strategy of infrastructure as code. Students learn how to manage databases for an organization by keeping them secure, portable, scalable, and recoverable.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ITM111 - Introduction to Databases (3) ; ITM220 - SQL (3)

courses.title: Data Warehousing
courses.description: This course offers a comprehensive exploration of data engineering, focusing on the development of data-driven applications using Python and SQL. Students will engage in designing and implementing data warehouses, integrating API-driven data ingestion, and developing front-end applications for database interaction and visualization. Emphasis is placed on practical skills in data modeling, ELT processes, and full-stack application development, preparing students for real-world data engineering roles.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ITM111 - Introduction to Databases (3) ; ITM220 - SQL (3)

courses.title: Cloud Data Engineering
courses.description:
Provides an in-depth exploration of data engineering concepts, focusing on the design, implementation, and optimization of scalable data pipelines. Students gain hands-on experience with modern data engineering tools and cloud-based technologies, learning to efficiently process, store, and manage large datasets. Students will learn how to extract, transform, and load (ETL) data efficiently, work with both structured and unstructured datasets, and implement modern data architectures.
Key topics include data pipeline architecture, ETL/ELT workflows, distributed data processing, and the integration of cloud computing platforms. The course also covers essential principles of data governance, security, and compliance, ensuring students understand best practices for maintaining data integrity and privacy in real-world applications. Students will develop the skills needed to build and maintain robust data infrastructure and systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ITM220 - SQL (3) ; CSE110 - Introduction to Programming (2)

courses.title: DevOps
courses.description:
DevOps is the key to building, deploying, and maintaining reliable applications efficiently in today's fast-paced software landscape. This course gives students a hands-on, practical foundation in DevOps principles, focusing on automation, collaboration, and continuous improvement in modern software development.

Students will gain proficiency in Git for version control, master branching strategies and code reviews, and understand its crucial role in agile development and MVP delivery. A major focus of the course is designing and implementing Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, which enable teams to deliver high-quality software faster and confidently deploy applications into production-ready environments.

Students learn the practical skills and foundational knowledge necessary to implement DevOps best practices in real-world environments, improving software development efficiency, maintainability, and operational reliability.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CSE210 - Programming with Classes (2) ; WDD131 - Dynamic Web Fundamentals (2)AND ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; WDD230 - Web Frontend Development I (3) ; WDD231 - Web Frontend Development I (2) ; CYBER360 - Advanced Scripting (3) ; CSE310 - Applied Programming (3) ; CSE212 - Programming with Data Structures (2) ; ITM310 - Applied Cloud Computing (3)

This course is designed to be a capstone experience where a student applies the skills they have learned in information systems in a real-world environment.

courses.title: Introductory Special Topics
courses.description: Introduces the latest advancements in information technology. The course is taught only when arranged by a faculty member and approved by the department chair, and may be used to allow students to do research or special projects.

courses.title: Cloud Architecture
courses.description: Covers the fundamentals of building Information Technology infrastructure in the Cloud. The course teaches students how to optimize the use of the Cloud by understanding managed cloud services and how they fit into cloud-based solutions.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ITM300 - Cloud Foundations (3)

courses.title: Cloud Development
courses.description:
This course provides a hands-on, practical approach to cloud-native application development, focusing on automation, observability, security, and scalable deployment strategies. Students will gain direct experience in designing, building, and securing applications in cloud environments using industry-leading tools and frameworks.

The course covers key topics such as API development, event-driven architectures, and NoSQL databases, equipping students with the skills to build modern cloud applications. Additionally, students will examine incident response, disaster recovery, and real-time monitoring to ensure system reliability and performance in production environments.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ITM350 - DevOps (3)

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: This is a special topics course to address the latest advancements in information technology.

courses.title: Advanced Grammar in Languages
courses.description: Focuses on the structure of the English language in significant detail so that students gain a deeper understanding of how it works. The material is presented in a way that invites students to ponder how various aspects of English compare with those of a second language. Application of this knowledge allows students to evaluate and address language deficiencies, identify resources useful in furthering language learning, and follow a program of lifelong language learning.

courses.title: Civilization and Culture
courses.description: This course is an exploration of the culture and civilization of the student's foreign language and country (other than the languages already taught at BYU-Idaho). It is also designed to give an overview of cultures and civilizations throughout the world.

courses.title: Language and Literary Traditions
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the study of literature and literary works in the student's foreign language (other than the languages already taught at BYU-Idaho).  It is also designed to give an overview of literature throughout the world.

courses.title: Latin I
courses.description: An introduction to Latin. Beginners and students with less than one year of high school Latin should register for this class.  Vocabulary building, grammar, reading, and basic composition.

courses.title: Latin II
courses.description: Reading Latin prose writers and study of Roman culture. Continuation of Latin 101, second semester.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; LATIN101 - Latin I (4)

courses.title: Latin Reading and Comprehension
courses.description: Latin Reading and Comprehension

courses.title: Research Skills
courses.description: This is an introductory course for anyone who wants to improve their ability to research and analyze information more efficiently. Students learn to define a research issue and evaluate information sources. Emphasis is placed on available library services and navigating library resources, including research databases. This course is open to students of all majors and will be particularly beneficial to anyone wanting to improve their research and information finding skills.

courses.title: Arithmetic
courses.description: A study of arithmetic and applications using arithmetic.  This course is only for those needing a review of elementary school arithmetic including signed numbers, fractions, decimals, and percents.

courses.title: Beginning Algebra
courses.description: The arithmetic of integers and rational numbers as well as an introduction to algebra will be studied.  This course is recommended for those needing basic algebra before taking progressively higher math courses.

courses.title: Intermediate Algebra
courses.description: This course will cover the fundamental operations of algebra, properties of exponents, solving linear, fractional, radical and quadratic equations, graphing linear, and quadratic functions.  Math 101 may not be taken for credit if MATH 110X (FDMAT 110) has been completed with a grade of "B" or higher.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; ACT Math score of at least 18 ; -or- SAT math score of at least 430/ Post 2016, 470 ; -or- ALEKS test score of at least 38 ; -or- MATH 100B with a grade of C or higher ; -or- Math 108Y with a grade of C or higher ; -or- Math Path score of at least 40

courses.title: Math for the Real World
courses.description: This course prepares students to understand, analyze, and solve real-life problems that require quantitative reasoning. Topics include the meaning of probabilities, how to read, critique, and apply statistical information found in news reports, public policy debates, consumer reports, and other daily life and professional situations; the use of mathematical models in describing, understanding, and making predictions about real world phenomena; and the mathematics of budgeting, loans, and investments. Topics will be illustrated by examples and applications from daily life and natural phenomena. Math for the Real World is to inspire students to act wisely when faced with quantitative challenges in collegiate coursework, employment, and daily living.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Math Path score of at least 30 ; -or- ACT math score of at least 18 ; -or- SAT math score of at least 430/post 2016, 470 ; -or- ALEKS test score of at least 38 ; -or- MATH 100B with a grade of C- or higher ; -or- MATH 100G with a grade of C- or higher ; -or- MATH 100L with a grade of C- or higher ; -or- MATH 101 with a grade of C- or higher ; -or- successful completion of PathwayConnect.

courses.title: Math for the Real World with Support
courses.description: This course prepares students with the necessary algebra skills relating to simplifying expressions, solving equations, graphing lines and working with spreadsheets to be able to take the General Education Quantitative Reasoning course. It also includes the content of the Quantiative Reasoning Course: It course prepares students to understand, analyze, and solve real-life problems that require quantitative reasoning. Topics include the meaning of probabilities, how to read, critique, and apply statistical information found in news reports, public policy debates, consumer reports, and other daily life and professional situations; the use of mathematical models in describing, understanding, and making predictions about real world phenomena; and the mathematics of budgeting, loans, and investments. Topics will be illustrated by examples and applications from daily life and natural phenomena.  Math for the Real World with Support is designed to inspire students to act wisely when faced with quantitative challenges in collegiate coursework, employment, and daily living. It can be taken by students who are placed into Math 100B.
courses.prerequisiteText: Math Path score of at least 10

courses.title: Precalculus
courses.description: This course includes a combination of College Algebra and Trigonometry. It is intended to prepare students for Calculus or other math and science courses.  Elementary analysis of functions having discrete or connected domains, methods of solving equations, and systems of equations and matrices will be explored.  Triangle relationships, graphs of periodic functions, trigonometric identities, inverse trigonometric functions, and applications of trigonometry will also be covered.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; MATH101 - Intermediate Algebra (4) ; ACT 23 or SAT 540 (Post 2016, 570) or ALEKS 55

courses.title: College Algebra
courses.description:
This course includes the study of elementary analysis of functions having discrete or connected domains. Methods of solving equations. Systems of equations and matrices. Strong connections to real world applications of functions and matrices will be made. Students who will take Calculus are strongly encouraged to take Math 109 instead of Math 110X.
ALEKS information can be found here: http://www.byui.edu/mathematics/aleks
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; MATH 101 with a grade of C- or higher. ; ACT Math score with a 23 or higher ; SAT Math score with 540 or higher ; New SAT Math score (2016 & Later) with a 570 or higher ; ALEKS preparation course score with a 53 or higher

courses.title: Trigonometry
courses.description: Examines the six trigonometric functions and their inverses. Covers measuring triangles, vectors, graphs, and solving equations. Emphasizes applications of trigonometry throughout the course.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH101 - Intermediate Algebra (4) ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3) ; ACT Math score of at least 23, or an SAT Math score of at least 540 (Post 2016, 570) , or an ALEKS score of at least 53

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: Covers limits, continuity, derivatives, integrals, and transcendental functions, including their properties and applications.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the followingOption 1: ; Take the following course(s): ; MATH109 - Precalculus (5)Option 2: ; Take the following course(s): ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3) ; MATH111 - Trigonometry (2)Option 3: ; ACT 27Option 4: ; SAT 620Option 5: ; 2016 SAT 640Option 6: ; ALEKS 85

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.description: Investigates the properties and techniques of integration, infinite sequences and series, polar coordinates, conic sections, and parametric curves in this follow-up basic calculus course. Includes graphical, analytical, numerical, and verbal representations of these calculus concepts and their relationships.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4)

courses.title: Applied Calculus for Data Analysis
courses.description: The three topic pillars of this course are functions, derivatives, and integrals. We will work on broadening and deepening our understanding of functions as tools of mathematics and as models. We will focus on a derivative as defined by its role in the local approximation of a curve and use derivatives in optimization. We will focus on integrals as a way to compute probabilities and will explore the connection between the probability density function (pdf) and cumulative distribution function (cdf) for a continuous random variable. We will fit models to data visually, by maximizing log likelihood functions, and by using a method of moments. We will rely on software (R and Mathematica) to help us with our calculations in this course.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Complete 1 of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH109 - Precalculus (5) ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3) ; MATH101 - Intermediate Algebra (4) ; ACT 23 or SAT 540 or 2016 SAT 570 or ALEKS 55 ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CHEM105 - General Chemistry I (3) ; DS250 - Data Science Programming (2) ; DS350 - Data Wrangling and Visualization (3) ; -or- CS124 (last offered 2023)

courses.title: Tutoring Mathematics
courses.description:
This course gives math education majors an early practicum experience working with secondary-level students. We hope that participants will discover whether or not they really want to pursue a secondary education degree. During this practicum experience, participants will tutor secondary students, discuss and use "best" practices in tutoring, improve their presentation skills, and prepare for the Praxis Exam requirement. 

Students will visit local schools for 2 hours each week between the hours of 8:30 am and 3:30 pm outside of the weekly class meeting. Travel time and school schedules need to be considered in the students' planning for these visits. Students are responsible for arranging their transportation.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3) ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4)

courses.title: Introduction to the Mathematical Sciences
courses.description: This course is designed to help students gain a deeper understanding of professional opportunities available within the Mathematical Sciences. Students will develop an effective personal educational plan; begin preparing for internships and employment; begin building a project portfolio to share with employers, and discover individual aptitudes and interests.

courses.title: Mathematical Reasoning for Teachers 1
courses.description: This course is designed to help you develop a deeper understanding of essential mathematics topics that you will teach. These topics include whole numbers, operation, and rational numbers. Other goals are to help you improve your ability to reason mathematically, develop greater number sense, represent and communicate mathematical ideas, and solve mathematics problems.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; MATH119 - Applied Calculus for Data Analysis (4) ; MATH108X - Math for the Real World (3) ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3) ; MATH221A - Business Statistics (3) ; MATH221B - Biostatistics (3) ; MATH221C - Social Science Statistics (3) ; MATH221D - Introductory Statistics with R (3)

courses.title: Mathematical Reasoning for Teachers 2
courses.description: This course is designed to help you develop a deeper understanding of essential mathematics topics that you will teach. These topics include Euclidean shapes, their properties, and relationships. Other topics include proportional reasoning, measurement concepts, measurement conversions, concepts of area, area formulas, and volume. Other goals are to help you improve your ability to reason mathematically, communicate mathematical ideas, and solve mathematics problems.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; MATH119 - Applied Calculus for Data Analysis (4) ; MATH108X - Math for the Real World (3) ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3) ; MATH221A - Business Statistics (3) ; MATH221B - Biostatistics (3) ; MATH221C - Social Science Statistics (3) ; MATH221D - Introductory Statistics with R (3)

courses.title: Multivariable and Vector Calculus
courses.description: This course includes the study of vectors, vector geometry, quadric surfaces, alternative coordinate systems, vector-valued functions, partial derivatives, gradient, optimization, multiple integration, vector fields, integral theorems of vector calculus, and applications will be studied. Math 214 and 215 cannot both be taken for credit.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH113 - Calculus II (3)

courses.title: Teaching Calculus
courses.description: This course is for math education majors. Students will deepen their understanding of calculus concepts by learning techniques for teaching limits, derivatives, and integrals to secondary students that develop conceptual understanding.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; MATH214 - Multivariable and Vector Calculus (3)

courses.title: Multivariable Calculus
courses.description: In this course students will study polar coordinates, parametric curves, vectors, vector geometry, vector-valued functions, partial derivatives, gradient, optimization, multiple integration, vector fields, and operations on scalar and vector fields. Emphasis will be on methods and applications. Math 215 and Math 214 cannot both be taken for credit.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4)

courses.title: Business Statistics
courses.description: In this course business students will study graphical representation of data, measure of center and spread, elementary probability, sampling distributions, correlation and regression, statistical inference involving means, proportions, and contingency tables.

courses.description: In this course students will study graphical representations of data, measures of center and spread, elementary probability, sampling distributions, correlations and regression, statistical inference involving means, proportions, and contingency tables, odds ratio and relative risk.
