courses.title: Introductory Statistics with R
courses.description:
In this course, students will study graphical representation of data, measures of center and spread, elementary probability, sampling distributions, correlation and regression, statistical inference involving means, proportions, and contingency tables. Students will learn to use R/RStudio to import a data set, use and create script files, perform statistical tests, and export figures. 

Generally, students in programs that have a strong research component should take this course. Check the requirements of your program to see which statistics course is specified for your major.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH101 - Intermediate Algebra (4) ; MATH108X - Math for the Real World (3) ; MATH109 - Precalculus (5) ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3) ; MATH111 - Trigonometry (2) ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; MATH113 - Calculus II (3) ; MATH119 - Applied Calculus for Data Analysis (4) ; Complete 1 of the following ACT Math score with a 23 or higher SAT Math score with 540 or higher New SAT Math score (2016 & Later) with a 570 or higher ALEKS preparation course score with a 53 or higher Math 11* with a grade of C- or higher(Any course that begins with Math 11).

courses.title: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra
courses.description: This course introduces and explores some of the major concepts of matrix analysis, vector spaces, and linear transformations through solving significant real world problems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; MATH119 - Applied Calculus for Data Analysis (4) ; ECON215 - Quantitative Methods (4)

courses.title: Mathematical Connections for Teachers
courses.description: Designed for future teachers to build understanding of the connections between the mathematics course they are currently taking and the mathematics they will be teaching. Course content will focus on: (1) Developing a personal philosophy of mathematics including its learning and teaching. (2) Understanding mathematics teaching standards. And (3) Building content knowledge involved in the development of algebraic thinking.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; MATH190 - Tutoring Mathematics (1)

courses.title: Problem Solving
courses.description: Investigate problem solving techniques and approaches using real world and common core assessment problems. Experience best practices for teaching problem solving in a secondary level classroom.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH275 - Mathematical Connections for Teachers (3)

courses.title: Fundamentals of Mathematical Modeling
courses.description: This course introduces the mathematical modeling process and explores modeling using regression, discrete dynamical systems, and differential equations.  It is intended for secondary mathematics education majors.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH241 - Fundamentals of Linear Algebra (2) ; MATH113 - Calculus II (3)

courses.title: Modeling with Probability
courses.description: This course introduces the process of modeling real world phenomena with mathematical constructs.  Specific examples from probability and discrete event simulation are explored.  A field trip where students can see these models in real life is included.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH241 - Fundamentals of Linear Algebra (2) ; MATH341 - Linear Algebra (3) ; MATH316 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra (4)

courses.title: Financial Mathematics for Actuaries
courses.description: This course will provide an understanding of the fundamental concepts of financial mathematics, and how those concepts are applied in calculating present and accumulated values for various streams of cash flows as a basis for future use in: reserving, valuation, pricing, asset/liability management, investment income, capital budgeting and valuing contingent cash flows.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; MATH113 - Calculus II (3) ; MATH214 - Multivariable and Vector Calculus (3) ; MATH215 - Multivariable Calculus (4) ; MATH316 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra (4)

courses.title: Special Topics in Mathematics
courses.description:
The content of this course will be determined by the department and the instructor, based on student needs and interest. 
Students will study an area of mathematics not otherwise covered in the mathematics curriculum.

courses.title: Introduction to Analysis
courses.description: This course develops mathematical communication skills. Topics include mathematical proof, set theory, mathematical induction, logical reasoning, elementary number theory, and properties of relations and functions.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH113 - Calculus II (3) ; MATH316 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra (4)

courses.title: Differential Equations with Linear Algebra
courses.description: This course will explore matrices, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, first and second order ordinary differential equations, power series and Fourier series methods, Laplace transforms, and systems of linear ordinary differential equations. Emphasis will be on methods and applications.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH214 - Multivariable and Vector Calculus (3) ; MATH215 - Multivariable Calculus (4)

courses.title: Intermediate Statistics
courses.description: Z tests, t tests, and chi-squared tests as well as their nonparametric equivalents, ANOVA for one or more factors, multiple linear regression, and logistic regression--all using the R software.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON278 - Statistics for Economists (3) ; MATH221A - Business Statistics (3) ; MATH221B - Biostatistics (3) ; MATH221C - Social Science Statistics (3) ; MATH330 - Engineering Statistics (3) ; MATH221D - Introductory Statistics with R (3) ; Take the following course(s): ; DS150 - Data Intuition and Insight (2) ; MATH119 - Applied Calculus for Data Analysis (4)

courses.title: Experimental Design
courses.description: This course is designed to explore various experimental designs, to analyze data from these designs, and to consider optimal experimental designs. Students will design and conduct major-specific projects.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; MATH325 - Intermediate Statistics (3)

courses.title: Engineering Statistics
courses.description: This course introduces statistical methods for science and engineering. A review of basic statistical concepts of central tendency, dispersion of data, probability laws, hypothesis testing, and confidence intervals will be conducted. It introduces statistical process control, design of experiments, statistical tolerance analysis, and concepts of Six Sigma quality.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4)

courses.title: Discrete Mathematics
courses.description: This course includes the study of topics from graph theory, combinatorics, and logic.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH280 - Problem Solving (3)

courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.description: This course covers systems of linear equations, matrices, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, vectors, vector spaces, linear transformations, and applications.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH119 - Applied Calculus for Data Analysis (4) ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4)

courses.title: Geometry
courses.description: This course consists of the axiomatic treatment of finite geometries, transformation geometry, and Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometries with emphasis on the historical significance of the Parallel Postulate.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH280 - Problem Solving (3)

courses.title: Writing and Technology for Mathematics Instruction
courses.description: This course focuses on creating and editing technical documents and how to typeset mathematics and mathematical figures using a computer. Students will develop the ability to use digital technology to facilitate mathematics instruction and engage students in learning.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH190 - Tutoring Mathematics (1)

courses.title: Mathematics Career Preparation
courses.description: This course will raise student awareness of professional opportunities in the Mathematical Sciences. Students will build a detailed career development plan targeted on specific job opportunities in industries and companies. Students will participate in the various services offered by the Career Preparation center on campus, including resume writing and VMOCK, presentation skills practice, interview preparation and practice, Handshake, career workshops, and BYUI connect. At least four times a semester, students will participate in career preparation seminars given by career mathematical scientists, including BYUI alumni. Here they will learn what the work environment is like, what skill sets are most valued, expectations, and opportunities. Students will work on projects that will build their resumes.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH191 - Introduction to the Mathematical Sciences (1)

courses.title: Numerical Analysis I
courses.description: This course covers error analysis, root finding, interpolation, numerical integration, systems of linear equations, least squares approximation, curve fitting, computing eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and the discrete Fourier transform. The computing environment is Python.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; MATH316 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra (4) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; CSE110 - Introduction to Programming (2) ; -or- CS101 (last offered 2023) ; -or- CS124 (last offered 2023)

courses.title: Numerical Analysis II
courses.description: This course covers numerical methods for solving initial value problems and boundary value problems, numerical methods for solving parabolic, hyperbolic, and elliptic PDEs, and an introduction to numerical optimization. The computing environment is Python.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH411 - Numerical Analysis I (3) ; MATH316 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra (4)

courses.title: Probability and Statistics
courses.description: This is a calculus-based course in mathematical probability intended for statistics, mathematics, data science, economics, and physics majors as well as statistics minors. Topics include: counting, basic probability theory, joint and conditional probabilities, Bayes' Theorem, expectation, moments, probability distributions, joint distributions, conditional and marginal distributions, independence, product moments, linear combinations, univariate and multivariate transformation techniques, and order statistics. Students will derive the cumulative distribution function, expected value, variance, and moment generating function of various discrete and continuous distributions.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH214 - Multivariable and Vector Calculus (3) ; MATH215 - Multivariable Calculus (4) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH221A - Business Statistics (3) ; MATH221B - Biostatistics (3) ; MATH221C - Social Science Statistics (3) ; MATH330 - Engineering Statistics (3) ; MATH221D - Introductory Statistics with R (3)

courses.title: Mathematical and Bayesian Statistics
courses.description: This course is a continuation and expansion of Math 423. The development of probability and statistics will continue with the theory of point estimation, interval estimation, and hypothesis testing. The course will then build fundamental concepts of Bayesian data analysis, when to use Bayesian data analysis and why it works, how to use Bayesian data analysis to build optimal estimates of unknown quantities of interest, and powerful computational techniques that allow you to work with just about any data models.  Bayesian data analysis is very useful for extracting information from large amounts of opaque data. Bayesian data analysis is used in medical research; business, finance, and market analysis; image and video analysis; machine learning; and many other scientific, engineering, and commercial applications.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH423 - Probability and Statistics (3)

courses.title: Applied Linear Regression
courses.description: This course is designed to explore fundamentals of regression, theory of regression models, residuals and residual analysis, multiple regression, remediation, transformations, and ANOVA. Students will use R for statistical analyses.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH325 - Intermediate Statistics (3)

courses.title: Applied Time Series Analysis
courses.description: Virtually every modern data involves collecting data at given time points (examples include commodity prices, river flows, corporate revenues, and global temperatures.) In this course, students will use learn proper techniques for applying time series analysis to a variety of real-world situations. This includes the handling, visualization, modeling and forecasting of time series data in R. Students will gain skills that can increase their employability and value to an employer.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON388 - Introduction to Econometrics (3) ; MATH425 - Applied Linear Regression (3)

courses.title: Modern Algebra
courses.description: This course is for secondary education majors and minors. Number theory, division algorithm, primes, GCD, LCM, proof, rings, integral domains, fields, polynomials, Fundamental Theorem of Algebra, groups, isomorphisms, and how these topics apply to the secondary school mathematics curriculum.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH301 - Introduction to Analysis (3) ; MATH340 - Discrete Mathematics (3)

courses.title: Abstract Algebra I
courses.description: This course is an introduction to groups, rings, fields, vector spaces, and applications.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH301 - Introduction to Analysis (3) ; MATH341 - Linear Algebra (3)

courses.title: Abstract Algebra II
courses.description: This course consists of additional exposure to groups, rings, fields, vector spaces, and applications.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH441 - Abstract Algebra I (3)

courses.title: Linear Algebra II
courses.description: This course covers second semester linear algebra concepts and methods including inner product spaces, orthonormal vectors, unitary matrices, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and matrix factorizations.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH301 - Introduction to Analysis (3) ; MATH341 - Linear Algebra (3)

courses.title: History of Mathematics
courses.description: This course is intended for students majoring in Mathematics Education. An overview of the development of mathematics and its interaction with society will be covered.

courses.title: Real Analysis I
courses.description: This course involves rigorous treatment of calculus. Limits, continuity, differentiation, integration, and metric properties of Euclidean spaces will be explored.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; MATH301 - Introduction to Analysis (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH214 - Multivariable and Vector Calculus (3) ; MATH215 - Multivariable Calculus (4) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH316 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra (4) ; MATH341 - Linear Algebra (3)

courses.title: Real Analysis II
courses.description: This course consists of analysis in the context of metric spaces. Applications involving such tools as approximation, Fourier analysis, and multivariate optimization will be explored.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH461 - Real Analysis I (3)

courses.title: Complex Analysis
courses.description: This course consists of arithmetic, algebra, and calculus operations and concepts applied to complex numbers and functions of a single complex variable.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH316 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra (4)

courses.title: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations
courses.description: This course focuses on formulating and solving boundary value problems modeling heat flow, wave motion, and electric potential.  Methods of solution include separation of variables and eigenfunction expansion, including Fourier series.  Techniques are developed for homogeneous problems and extended to problems with nonhomogeneous PDEs or boundary conditions.  Topics typically include Sturm-Liouville theory and generalization to higher dimensions and non-Cartesian coordinate systems.  Additional topics may include the method of characteristics, transform methods, and quasi- or non-linear equations.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH316 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra (4)

courses.title: Statistical and Data Science Consulting
courses.description: This is a hands-on introduction to statistical consulting. Students will apply skills developed in other statistical courses to provide consulting services to researchers at BYU-Idaho. Students will continue to develop the written and oral communication skills needed to discuss technical statistical content with other researchers. Projects address needs at all stages of the research process. Student activity will be closely monitored by a statistician. This course provides a foundation upon which a student with interest in statistics can provide meaningful service and enhance their skills.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH326 - Experimental Design (3) ; DS350 - Data Wrangling and Visualization (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH425 - Applied Linear Regression (3) ; CSE450 - Machine Learning (3)

courses.title: Secondary Education Math Teaching Methods
courses.description: This course must be taken in the semester before student teaching. This course is designed to help pre-service secondary mathematics teachers apply research-based teaching strategies that lead students to discover, create, appreciate, and utilize mathematics. Students will have many opportunities to teach, prepare lesson plans, learn how to organize and manage classrooms, and connect these activities to state and professional standards for secondary mathematics teachers.  Students will also practice using the principles of the BYU-Idaho Learning Model in their own teaching.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH350 - Geometry (3)

courses.title: Mathematics Education Practicum Lab
courses.description:
Pre-service teachers will serve as teaching assistants under the direction of a mentor teacher in a public school classroom providing an authentic experience with the responsibilities of a professional educator and an opportunity to practice the teaching skills being learned in their methods class.  As teaching assistants, pre-service teachers will work one-on-one or in small groups with select students, help with grading class assessments, aid with record keeping, assist with class activities, create teaching resources, and teach lessons as assigned by the mentor teacher. 

Students will visit local schools daily during the time scheduled for this class. Additional travel time may need to be considered in the students' planning for these visits. Students are responsible for arranging their transportation.

courses.title: Topics in Statistics
courses.description: The content of this course will be determined by the department and the instructor based on student need and interest. Possible subjects that will be explored are time series, survey or spatial sampling techniques, multiple comparisons, nonparametrics, and statistical computing.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ECON388 - Introduction to Econometrics (3) ; MATH325 - Intermediate Statistics (3)

courses.title: Topics in Mathematics
courses.description:
The content of this course will be determined by the department and the instructor, based on student need and interest. Possible subjects that will be explored are Number Theory, Topology, Stochastic Processes, and Actuarial Science.
Students will study an area of mathematics not otherwise covered in the applied mathematics curriculum.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH301 - Introduction to Analysis (3)

courses.title: Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

This course consists of practical experience working in a math-intensive industry.

courses.title: Senior Project in Mathematics
courses.description: Content tailored to individual needs and interests of the students. Investigation and/or application of mathematical principles under the guidance of a faculty member.

courses.title: Introduction to Engineering and Technology
courses.description: Introduces students to civil engineering, mechanical engineering, automotive engineering technology, manufacturing engineering technology, and welding engineering technology. Explores degree programs offered at BYU-Idaho, industry opportunities, and career paths. Engages students in immersive engineering experiences. Discusses the power of a gospel-centered life as an integral part of a career.

courses.title: Engineering Computation
courses.description: Introduces computation in the context of engineering problem solving. Presents fundamental principles of computation, such as computer representation of numbers and round-off error. Covers basic numerical methods, including numerical integration, differentiation, and root finding. Introduces computer programming, including flowcharts, loops, conditional statements, and functions. Emphasizes using MS Excel to solve computational problems and Python to create computer programs.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH109 - Precalculus (5) ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; Take the following course(s): ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3) ; MATH111 - Trigonometry (2) ; ACT 27 or SAT 620 or 2016 SAT 640 or ALEKS 85

courses.title: Parametric Mechanical CAD
courses.description: This course is designed to help students develop employable and certifiable skills in parametric CAD modeling of mechanical components and assemblies.  Students will work toward associate level certification in SolidWorks and have the opportunity to take the CSWA exam.  The course focuses on training students to think parametrically and to strategically capture design intent within 3D CAD models and assemblies.

courses.title: Introduction to Engineering Design
courses.description: Introduces engineering design methods and ethics. Guides students working in teams through multiple design projects that apply design principles, including problem definition, constraints, concept generation, selection, prototyping, and documentation. Explores engineering ethics through case studies of real-world professional challenges. The $50.00 course fee covers prototyping materials in Makers Labs.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME101 - Introduction to Engineering and Technology (1) ; ME172 - Parametric Mechanical CAD (3)

courses.title: Engineering Mechanics: Statics
courses.description: Concepts of forces, moments and other vector quantities, free body diagrams, particle and rigid body statics, trusses, frames and machines, friction, centroids, and moments of inertia. Vector analysis used.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4) ; PH121 - Principles of Physics I (3)

courses.title: Strength of Materials
courses.description: Review of equations of static equilibrium; introduction to engineering stress and strain; thermal loading; stress distributions and deflections resulting from axial, torsional, and transverse (beam) loadings; combined loading problems; stress and strain transformation, Mohr's circle; column buckling.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME201 - Engineering Mechanics: Statics (3)

courses.title: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics
courses.description: The study and application of the concepts of dynamics to particles, systems of particles, and rigid bodies. Scalar and vector analysis used.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME201 - Engineering Mechanics: Statics (3) ; PH121 - Principles of Physics I (3)

courses.title: Materials Science
courses.description: Atomic structure and microstructure of engineering materials, including metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites. Factors influencing the fabrication, processing, and selection of materials in engineering analysis and design. Case studies of engineering material failures.  Use of material selection.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; CHEM105 - General Chemistry I (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ME202 - Strength of Materials (3) ; MET202 - Applied Strength of Materials (2)

courses.title: Mechanical CADD and GD&T
courses.description: This course focuses on mechanical drafting and Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T). Students will learn ANSI and ISO standards and become proficient using SolidWorks CADD to create working drawings which communicate product manufacturing information.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME172 - Parametric Mechanical CAD (3)

courses.title: Early Work Experience and Career Development
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap. 

The ME 298 course is the method of obtaining school credit for relevant employment early in a student's education. Throughout the course, students will complete career development activities in addition to their employment obligations. Students must register for ME 298 during the same semester they are employed. Employment under the supervision of a technician or an engineer would be approved. Full-time employment for the duration of a full semester is preferred while 280 hours of work is a minimum requirement.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME101 - Introduction to Engineering and Technology (1)

courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Student Research Project
courses.description: Under faculty direction, students complete a research project that will expand the student's scientific and engineering experience, help them gain valuable professional skills, and provide opportunities to collaborate with the students and faculty.

courses.title: Mechatronics
courses.description: Introduces the basics of electric circuits, sensors, actuators, feedback control, and programming microcontrollers. Covers basic electrical components and modeling basic circuits for application in mechatronic systems. Covers various types of electric actuators and sensors for use in simple closed-loop feedback systems. Uses a microcontroller to integrate the sensors, actuators, and circuitry into a complete mechatronic system designed to automate a mechanical system.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME142 - Engineering Computation (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; PH223 - Engineering Physics (4) ; PH220 - Principles of Physics III (3)

courses.title: Dynamic Systems Modeling and Control
courses.description: Applies mathematical concepts from linear algebra and ordinary differential equations to the modeling and control of dynamic systems. Focuses on AC electrical circuits, mechanical systems, and mechatronic systems. Students learn to model linear and nonlinear dynamic systems, process data using filtering and estimation techniques, and design basic feedback controllers. The course also introduces MATLAB and Simulink for simulating and solving dynamic system problems. A culminating project requires students to analyze, control, or design a dynamic mechatronic system.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ME305 - Mechatronics (3) ; ECEN250 - Electric Circuit Analysis II (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH316 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra (4) ; MATH341 - Linear Algebra (3)

courses.title: Thermodynamics
courses.description: Fundamentals of classical thermodynamics. Thermodynamic property relationships for ideal gases, vapors, liquids, and solids. First and second law analysis of open and closed systems. Energy and efficiency analysis of power and refrigeration cycles.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; PH123 - Principles of Physics II (3)

courses.title: Kinematics
courses.description: Relative motion of links in mechanisms; velocities and acceleration of machine parts; rolling contact; cams; synthesis of mechanisms. Includes computer-aided engineering techniques.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME204 - Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics (3)

courses.title: Numerical Methods
courses.description: Builds on ME 142 and covers numerical methods for solving engineering problems, including root finding, systems of equations, interpolation, curve fitting, numerical integration and differentiation, and differential equations. Emphasizes applying these methods to real-world problems with effective code documentation.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME142 - Engineering Computation (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; MATH316 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra (4)

courses.title: Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Introduction to fluid mechanics and incompressible fluid flow, fluid statics, fluid dynamics, control volume analysis of fluid flow, dimensional analysis and scale models, internal and external viscous flow, and turbomachinery.  Flow measurement lab included.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ME322 - Thermodynamics (3) ; MATH316 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra (4) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ME204 - Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics (3) ; PH332 - Classical Mechanics (3)

courses.title: Advanced Strength of Materials
courses.description: Builds on topics introduced in Strength of Materials, including stress, deflections, and material failure. Guides students in verifying analytical concepts through numerical simulation using Finite Element Analysis and experimental results.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME172 - Parametric Mechanical CAD (3) ; ME202 - Strength of Materials (3)

courses.title: Advanced Mechanical CAD
courses.description: Trains students in advanced mechanical design techniques and prepares them for three professional-level certifications using SolidWorks, a world-class mechanical CAD application.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME172 - Parametric Mechanical CAD (3)

courses.title: Machine Components
courses.description: Introduces practical analysis and selection of industrial machine components, including fasteners, powertrains, and fluid power systems. Guides students in completing a design project that integrates mechanical components into a functioning system.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ME172 - Parametric Mechanical CAD (3)AND ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ME202 - Strength of Materials (3) ; MET202 - Applied Strength of Materials (2)

courses.title: Work Experience and Career Development
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

The ME 398R course is the method of obtaining school credit for relevant employment in a student's education. Throughout the course students will complete career development activities in addition to their employment obligations. Students must register for ME 398R during the same semester they are employed. Employment under the supervision of an engineer would be approved. Full-time employment for the duration of a full semester is preferred while 280 hours of work is a minimum requirement.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; CE161 - Fundamentals in 2D CADD (3) ; ME298 - Early Work Experience and Career Development (1)

courses.title: Autonomous Control of Dynamic Systems
courses.description: Introduces modeling, simulation, estimation, and control of dynamic systems. Covers state-space and Laplace-domain modeling, state estimation, system identification, and autonomous control of nonlinear dynamic systems. Explores control system design methods such as root locus, pole placement, and frequency-domain techniques. Enhances programming skills in professional software such as MATLAB, Simulink, C++, and Arduino.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME310 - Dynamic Systems Modeling and Control (3)

courses.title: Thermal-Fluid System Design and Analysis
courses.description: Applies principles of thermodynamics and fluid mechanics to design and analyze industrial thermal-fluid systems, including heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems, plumbing systems, and power generation systems. Simulates the role of an engineer-in-training at a mechanical engineering firm. Includes several realistic commercial and industrial project designs.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME322 - Thermodynamics (3)

courses.title: Heat Transfer
courses.description: Covers the fundamentals of conduction, convection, and radiation modes of heat transfer; fundamental equations for steady and unsteady conduction; convection correlations; environmental radiation and radiation properties; and heat exchanger analysis and design. Includes a heat transfer laboratory.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME322 - Thermodynamics (3) ; ME342 - Numerical Methods (3) ; ME360 - Fluid Mechanics (3)

courses.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Introduces computational methods for solving and analyzing problems in fluid mechanics. Covers grid generation, application of initial and boundary conditions, selection of solution algorithms and models, solution generation and convergence, and post-processing, including flow visualization and determination of global properties. Addresses incompressible and compressible flows. Compares results with selected analytical solutions.
courses.corequisiteText: Concurrently enrolled in: ; ME360 - Fluid Mechanics (3)

courses.title: CAE Modeling and Digital Simulation
courses.description: Covers advanced CAD and engineering applications in design, modeling, simulation, and customization. Emphasizes the e use of CAD and engineering software tools. Topics include the engineering design process, advanced solids modeling techniques, kinematic analysis, digital simulation techniques, optimization, and customization techniques.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME180 - Introduction to Engineering Design (3)

courses.title: Mechanics of Composite Materials
courses.description: An introduction to laminated composite materials and structures.  An investigation of the micromechanical and macromechanical behavior of anisotropic plies.  Development of classical lamination theory for predicting the mechanical behavior of laminated composite plates.  Laboratory work involving fabrication and testing of composite laminates.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ME142 - Engineering Computation (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ME250 - Materials Science (3) ; CE310 - Civil Engineering Materials Science (3)

courses.title: Engineering Experimentation and Communication
courses.description: Experimentation for engineering applications, including developing and conducting appropriate experiments; analyzing, modeling, and interpreting data; and professionally communicating results.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; MATH330 - Engineering Statistics (3) ; ME310 - Dynamic Systems Modeling and Control (3) ; ME342 - Numerical Methods (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ENG301 - Advanced Writing and Research (3) ; BUS301 - Advanced Writing in Professional Contexts (3)

courses.title: Fundamentals of Finite Element Analysis
courses.description: Introduces the finite element method. Evaluates the characteristics and limitations of several basic finite elements. Applies the finite element method to structural and thermal problems using commercial software.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete all of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ME142 - Engineering Computation (3) ; Take 1 of the following courses: ; ME370 - Advanced Strength of Materials (3) ; CE321 - Structural Analysis (3)

courses.title: Senior Capstone Design
courses.description: Comprehensive one-semester integrated design experience using the engineering design process and skills gained in engineering science classes. Typical projects include product conception, development, design, and manufacture. Students are required to sign forms that assign rights and ownership of intellectual property to a sponsor and agree to nondisclosure of confidential information.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Take the following course(s): ; ME310 - Dynamic Systems Modeling and Control (3) ; ME360 - Fluid Mechanics (3) ; ME382 - Machine Components (3) ; Take the following course(s): ; MET340 - Manufacturing Quality (3) ; ME382 - Machine Components (3) ; MET331 - Manufacturing Processes II (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Complete 1 of the following ; Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ME423 - Heat Transfer (3) ; ME455 - Engineering Experimentation and Communication (3) ; Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; MET431 - Tool Design (3) ; MET445 - Fundamentals of Composites Manufacturing (3) ; MET465 - Manufacturing Automation (3)

courses.title: Special Problems in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Students complete individual major projects or research in engineering, under the supervision of a faculty member.

courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: A one-semester course emphasizing current topics in engineering.

courses.title: Applied Statics
courses.description: This trigonometry-based statics course introduces students to fundamental principles of forces and their effects on rigid bodies at rest. Students learn to represent forces and moments, analyze free-body diagrams, and solve equilibrium problems.  Emphasis is placed on the practical application of these principles to solve real-world engineering problems and on the effective communication of results.
courses.prerequisiteText: Complete 1 of the followingOption 1: ; Take the following course(s): ; MATH109 - Precalculus (5)Option 2: ; Take the following course(s): ; MATH110X - College Algebra (3) ; MATH111 - Trigonometry (2)Option 3: ; Take the following course(s): ; MATH112X - Calculus I (4)Option 4: ; ACT 27Option 5: ; SAT 620Option 6: ; 2016 SAT 640Option 7: ; ALEKS 85

courses.title: Applied Strength of Materials
courses.description: This trigonometry-based strength of materials course prepares students to analyze the behavior of materials under load.  Students will learn to calculate stress and strain and determine deflections in axially and torsionally loaded members.  Emphasis is placed on the practical application of these principles to solve real-world engineering problems and on the effective communication of results.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; ME201 - Engineering Mechanics: Statics (3) ; MET201 - Applied Statics (2)

courses.title: Manufacturing Processes I
courses.description: This course is a basic introduction to manufacturing processes. Topics include: measuring tools, basic material science, mass reduction processes (milling, turning, drilling, etc.), separating and deforming processes (cutting, shearing, bending, etc.), mass conserving processes (casting and polymer/composite processes), joining processes (thermal, mechanical, and chemical), finishing processes, and emerging technologies in manufacturing.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME172 - Parametric Mechanical CAD (3)

courses.title: Manufacturing Processes I Lab
courses.description: This course is a hands-on laboratory designed to help students gain experience using various machines and processes to fabricate parts.  Specific topics include Lathe operations (turning, facing, threading, chamfering, grooving, and parting); Milling operations (milling, facing, drilling, and chamfering); and Metal Casting.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; MET231 - Manufacturing Processes I (2)

courses.title: Materials Lab
courses.description: Laboratory investigations in material standards, material specifications, and strength of materials.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; ME250 - Materials Science (3)

courses.title: Mechatronic Circuits
courses.description: The current Industry 4.0 revolution requires manufacturing engineers to develop fundamental skills with industrial mechatronic circuits. This course develops practical skills in DC circuits, AC circuits, Pneumatic circuits, Hydraulic circuits, and Electro-pneumatic/hydraulic systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; MET201 - Applied Statics (2) ; ME201 - Engineering Mechanics: Statics (3)

courses.title: Manufacturing Processes II
courses.description: This course explores advanced manufacturing processes with an emphasis on the production of metal components. Topics include machining, material separating, deformation, joining processes, and inspection tools.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MET231L - Manufacturing Processes I Lab (1)

courses.title: Computer Numerical Control (CNC)
courses.description: Automated machine control through Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAM) and Computer Numerical Control (CNC). Students gain practical laboratory experience on CAM, CNC, and manual programming on CNC equipment (mills, lathes, etc.). Principles of machining variables, tooling, and setups will be reviewed.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MET231L - Manufacturing Processes I Lab (1)

courses.title: Manufacturing Quality
courses.description: This course is designed to help students embrace an attitude of "continuous improvement" by implementing Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma tools and methods in their careers, communities, and personal lives.   After learning and practicing Lean/Six Sigma concepts through tutorials, students will have the opportunity to apply their skills in a series of personal application projects, as well as a team project with a client.  Students who successfully meet a designated standard of concept mastery, performance on projects, and a comprehensive exam will have the opportunity to obtain a BYU-Idaho Lean Six Sigma Greenbelt certification.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; MATH330 - Engineering Statistics (3) ; MATH221A - Business Statistics (3) ; MATH221B - Biostatistics (3) ; MATH221C - Social Science Statistics (3)

courses.title: Prototyping Fundamentals
courses.description: This course is an introduction to prototyping.  Students will learn about the steps needed to take an idea from a thought to a full-blown test sample for evaluation.  Different levels of prototypes will be evaluated, depending on the audience and end goal of the prototype.  Students will learn about product testing and evaluation, along with the legal aspects of prototyping, such as patents and copyrights.  The lab component of this course will step the student through the entire prototyping process, resulting in the hands-on creation of an original product.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MET231L - Manufacturing Processes I Lab (1)

courses.title: Manufacturing Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

An internship is a cooperative program between the BYU-Idaho Engineering Technology Department and approved Experience Providers (employers). Professional internships correlate actual work experience in the manufacturing industry with coursework taken at BYU-Idaho. Internships approved by the internship coordinator provide students with knowledge of career opportunities and actual work experience in preparation for employment after graduation. The ideal internship would take place during the student's flex semester and be a full-time, paid employment opportunity. The length of time for the internship experience is intended to be equal to a 14-week semester, 40 hours per week or approximately 560 hours.  Students are strongly encouraged to complete their internship before their last semester.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME172 - Parametric Mechanical CAD (3)

courses.title: Tool Design
courses.description: This course introduces the principles of Tool Design used in manufacturing and production environments. Topics include responsibilities of a tool designer, the design process, economics of design, tooling materials, and tool drawings and specifications.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MET332 - Computer Numerical Control (CNC) (3)

courses.title: Fundamentals of Composites Manufacturing
courses.description: This course is an introduction to composites materials, processing, and manufacturing. The student will learn about resin selection and chemistry, fiber selection, basics of composite mechanics, as well as the major families of processing methods for composites materials. Current trends in the industry and emerging technologies in both industry and academia, including process optimization tools such as simulation, will also be discussed. This course is NOT a laminate design course. This course is intended to be an introduction to many types of composite manufacturing processes.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME250 - Materials Science (3)

courses.title: Plastics: Materials and Processing
courses.description: This course explores the behavior and properties of plastic materials, including material types and key mechanical and chemical characteristics. Students learn about common plastics manufacturing processes, gaining hands-on experience with various methods and equipment. The course also covers plastic product design, tooling, and process selection.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; ME250 - Materials Science (3)

courses.title: Manufacturing Automation
courses.description: The current Industry 4.0 revolution requires manufacturing and mechanical engineers to obtain fundamental industrial automation skills. This course develops practical skills in PLC programming, PLC wiring; HMI programming, 6-axis industrial robot programming, and Machine Vision.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MET231L - Manufacturing Processes I Lab (1)

courses.title: Special Topics in Manufacturing
courses.description: Students complete individual major projects or research in manufacturing, under the supervision of a faculty member.

courses.title: Careers in Marketing
courses.description: Introduces students to the world of marketing and examines the day-to-day experience of a career in the field. Explores career paths in growth areas such as digital marketing, brand management, advertising, and sales. Guides students in identifying the courses needed at BYU-Idaho to earn a degree and begin a career in marketing. Helps students build a map to career success by graduation through networking, resume development, and interview preparation. Identifies courses outside the major that add valuable skills and increase students' value to future employers. The course also helps students identify other fields if marketing is not the right fit.

courses.title: Marketing Foundations
courses.description: Equips students with strategic marketing skills essential for today's digital and traditional business environments. Through hands-on projects, students master market analysis techniques, develop targeted customer personas, and craft data-driven marketing strategies.

courses.title: Beginning Marketing Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap. 

Students must be registered for this course within the first two weeks of the semester they are completing the internship.  For more information on how to register for an internship see the Marketing Department webpage. This course is designed for students working full or part-time in business-related employment to gain introductory experience and understanding of the functions of a successful company.  Students must complete application and approval through the College of Business and Communication Career Services, contract with their employer to work for college credits, and work a minimum of 15 hours per week for a minimum of seven weeks.  Other requirements include writing reports, submitting self- and supervisor evaluations, and adhering to BYU-Idaho standards and policies.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in: ; MKT100 - Careers in Marketing (1)

courses.title: IBC Marketing
courses.description: Provides opportunities to learn basic marketing principles through experiential learning in a student-run business environment known as the Integrated Business Core, or I.B.C. for short. Includes the application and exploration of concepts such as empathetic design, value creation, the 4 Ps, and data-driven marketing decisions.

courses.title: Marketing Management
courses.description: This course is a comprehensive introduction to the principles of marketing. It covers marketing essentials such as consumer research, consumer segmentation, segment targeting and product positioning, new product development and introduction, marketing strategy, branding, marketing communications, pricing, and distribution.

courses.title: Content Marketing
courses.description: Examines how advertisers must condense all that can be said about a product into a few pertinent, succinct, and compelling points and provides practice in this process. Studies historic cases of copywriting issues in advertising and challenges confronting business, government, education, for-profit, and not-for-profit entities. Examines the responsibilities of an account planner.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; MKT100 - Careers in Marketing (1) ; COMM100 - Introduction to Communication (1) ; BUS100 - Business Exploration and Orientation (1)

courses.title: Email Marketing
courses.description: Builds foundational knowledge of how companies use email for marketing, analytics, and customer service. Develops a high-level understanding of email marketing principles and strategies, including email structure and design, and email technologies. Covers targeting techniques, measurement, legal and privacy concerns, and email's role in effective marketing strategies.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; MKT100 - Careers in Marketing (1) ; BUS100 - Business Exploration and Orientation (1) ; COMM100 - Introduction to Communication (1)

courses.title: Social Media Marketing
courses.description: Prepares students to become proficient with various platforms, stay up to date on the latest best practices, and explore the power of social media marketing. Provides students with practical, real-world experiences and proven social media marketing techniques and strategies.

courses.title: Integrated Digital Marketing
courses.description: Introduces general concepts and tactics of marketing and advertising on digital platforms. It provides an overview of the digital landscape and introduces students to display, search, social, and email marketing. Students gain hands-on experience creating advertising and marketing strategies for various digital channels.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; MKT353 - Web Business Creation (3) ; MKT351 - Social Media Marketing (3) ; MKT350 - Email Marketing (3) ; MKT357 - Amazon/Ecommerce Sales and Marketing (3) ; MKT358 - Advanced Google Ads (3) ; MKT330 - Content Marketing (3) ; MKT380 - Market Research and Web Analytics (3)
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; BUS100 - Business Exploration and Orientation (1) ; COMM100 - Introduction to Communication (1) ; MKT100 - Careers in Marketing (1)

courses.title: Web Business Creation
courses.description: This course is for any student interested in building a web-based business. Students go through the necessary steps to build and launch a web-based business that is capable of accepting online payments.

courses.title: Search Engine Optimization
courses.description: Covers key issues in managing and developing marketing databases for segmenting markets, maximizing customer relationships, and developing marketing tactics. Also discusses data mining, CRM, and other database tools that support analysis.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; COMM100 - Introduction to Communication (1) ; BUS100 - Business Exploration and Orientation (1) ; MKT100 - Careers in Marketing (1)

courses.title: Amazon/Ecommerce Sales and Marketing
courses.description: This course is designed to help students learn how to market and sell products on Amazon or other e-commerce marketplaces. Students will learn skills that can help them manage e-commerce businesses for large brands or to sell their own products / resell products as an entrepreneur selling on e-commerce marketplaces like Amazon.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; MKT100 - Careers in Marketing (1) ; BUS100 - Business Exploration and Orientation (1) ; COMM100 - Introduction to Communication (1)

courses.title: Advanced Google Ads
courses.description: This course will give students a deep dive into the Google Ads platform. Students will be given the opportunity to build, optimize and report on the results of Google Search Campaigns, Google Display Campaigns and YouTube Video Campaigns.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; MKT100 - Careers in Marketing (1) ; BUS100 - Business Exploration and Orientation (1) ; COMM100 - Introduction to Communication (1)

courses.title: Category Management and Merchandising
courses.description: Delves into category management and CPG sales in the retail environment. Examines key concepts, including the DPSM (Distribution, Pricing, Shelving, Merchandising) framework, shopper insights analysis, and retail math for SKU selection and pricing. Uses real-world data sets and analytic tools to develop strategies for category growth. Covers effective negotiation techniques for securing product placements and increasing sales. Develops students' proficiency in conducting analyses, making data-driven decisions, and communicating strategies.

courses.title: Professional Sales
courses.description: Provides a comprehensive understanding of professional selling through practical, hands-on experiences and role-plays. Covers essential components of professional selling, including prospecting, identifying customer needs, handling objections, and ethical, customer-focused best practices.

courses.title: Sales Account Management
courses.description: Focuses on the skill sets, tools, technologies, and processes of account management. Includes in-depth work in account planning, including protect and grow initiatives, relationship mapping, get-well project management, renewals, upsell/cross-sell, and negotiations, through specific experiences and a focus on interest-based efforts.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MKT370 - Professional Sales (3)

courses.title: Sales Management
courses.description: Examines the elements of effective sales management through practical, hands-on experiences. Extends students' understanding of leadership, staffing, organizational structure, compensation, coaching, and motivation as they relate to sales organizations.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MKT370 - Professional Sales (3)

courses.title: Sales Business Development
courses.description: Focuses on the skill sets and technologies used by sales business development representatives and sales executives. Includes in-depth work in prospecting through various channels (email, phone, social, video, etc.) and designing multichannel prospecting sequences. Targets ideal customer profiles and specific individuals within each account. Combines best practices with cold-calling role-plays. Covers the transition from BDR to Account Executive, with an emphasis on year one, including deal qualification, sales presentations, and closing skills. Reinforces core skills throughout, including mindset, motivation, and business networking.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MKT370 - Professional Sales (3)

courses.title: Market Research and Web Analytics
courses.description: Introduces students to the principles and practices of research as a foundation for strategic decision-making in marketing, advertising, and public relations. Teaches students to define communication problems, design and conduct ethical research, analyze quantitative and qualitative data, and communicate research insights as compelling narratives that inform creative, messaging, and strategic decision-making. Explains and applies basic statistical functions. Includes computer-assisted data analysis.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; MKT100 - Careers in Marketing (1) ; COMM100 - Introduction to Communication (1) ; BUS100 - Business Exploration and Orientation (1)

courses.title: Advanced Marketing Internship
courses.description:
Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges. However, an administrative fee equal to one credit hour at the current rate of tuition will be charged for an internship course. The fee is in addition to any tuition charges for other classes. Fees are charged independently of tuition and are not subject to the 12-credit tuition cap.

Required for all Marketing students. Students must be registered for this course within the first two weeks of the semester they are completing the internship. For more information on how to register for an internship see the Marketing Department website. Students will find a professional marketing internship in an approved business, complete the application and obtain approval through the College of Business and Communication Career Services, be enrolled in the course, write reports, submit evaluations, and complete at least 270 hours of work in seven weeks or more. During their internship students will gain a greater vision of becoming a marketing professional and establish career networking links. Students will earn one credit and may receive compensation from the employer and letters of recommendation from both the employer and BYU-Idaho.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take the following course(s): ; MKT298R - Beginning Marketing Internship (1)

courses.title: Special Marketing Projects
courses.description: An arranged research or special project course. Contact the department for registration information.

courses.title: Marketing Analysis
courses.description: Focuses primarily on building marketing students' analytical abilities. Builds analytical ability at both the technical level, teaching students to use specific analysis tools accurately, and the conceptual level, teaching students when and under what circumstances to use those tools.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; MKT100 - Careers in Marketing (1) ; BUS100 - Business Exploration and Orientation (1) ; COMM100 - Introduction to Communication (1)

courses.title: Marketing Strategy
courses.description: Explores a variety of marketing strategies through case studies and real-world examples. Teaches students to apply marketing principles in plans they create for other businesses.
courses.corequisiteText: Completed or concurrently enrolled in at least 1 of the following: ; MKT100 - Careers in Marketing (1) ; COMM100 - Introduction to Communication (1) ; BUS100 - Business Exploration and Orientation (1)

courses.title: Introduction to the Army
courses.description:
MS101 focuses on Introduction to the Army and basic Soldier skills. Students receive an introduction to the Army Profession and examine what it means to be a professional in the U.S. Army, committed to the ideal that America and its founding documents remain the most powerful force for good in human history. The overall focus is on developing basic knowledge and comprehension of the Army Leadership Requirements Model (LRM) while gaining a complete understanding of the Reserve Officers’ Training Corps (ROTC) program, its purpose in the Army, and its advantages for the student. Students also begin learning map reading and land navigation. Students will have initial classes on fieldcraft, first aid, and team building that will include a weekly lab facilitated by MS III Cadets and supervised by MS IV’s (Senior Cadets) and cadre.

The course produces a student who understands the basic structure of the US Army, its customs and courtesies, and accepts the Army as a Values-based organization committed to the ideal that America and its founding documents remain the most powerful force for good in human history. Embraces the scholar-athlete-warrior ethos; who is familiar with individual roles and responsibilities in support of team efforts; who demonstrates oral and written communications skills, understands resilience, and develops a commitment to learning. In addition, demonstrates introductory skills in fieldcraft and team building at the squad level.

courses.title: Foundations of Army Leadership
courses.description: MS102 introduces students to the personal challenges and competencies that are critical for effective leadership and being committed to the ideal that America and its founding documents remain the most powerful force for good in human history. Students learn the importance of personal development in life skills such as critical thinking, resilience, holistic health and fitness, and communication process. Students receive awareness training in Antiterrorism and introductory classes in tactics, beginning with Team and Squad Basic Components, Basic Movements, Basic Patrolling, and Battle Drills that will be the foundation throughout their military careers. Students will apply classroom knowledge during hands-on performance-oriented weekly labs and physical readiness training sessions (ending with a diagnostic Army Fitness Test) facilitated by MS III Cadets and supervised by MS IVs (Senior Cadets) and cadre.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; MS101 - Introduction to the Army (3) ; MS101S - Introduction to the Army - Lecture (1)

courses.title: Army Leadership and Ethics
courses.description:
MS201 focuses on leadership and ethics. The course adds depth to the Cadets’ knowledge of the different leadership styles. Cadets will conduct a leadership analysis of famous leaders and a self-assessment of their own leadership style. The Army Profession is presented through the understanding of Culture Awareness, Values, Ethics, and how to apply both to different situations they may encounter as a leader committed to the ideal that America and its founding documents remain the most powerful force for good in human history. Army Values and Ethics and their relationship to the Law of Armed Conflict (LOAC) and philosophy of military service are presented through video clips and historical vignettes, followed by Cadet small group discussions. Cadets will apply classroom knowledge during hands-on performance-oriented weekly labs and physical readiness training sessions facilitated by MS III Cadets and supervised by MS IVs and cadre.
 
The course produces a Cadet grounded in foundational leadership doctrine and skills by leading small units in achieving assigned missions. Utilizes critical thinking and problem-solving during Troop Leading Procedures (TLPs). Committed to physical fitness, applies Army values and understands the importance of the officer’s role in leading change; is knowledgeable in the Army as a profession and is committed to the ideal that America and its founding documents remain the most powerful force for good in human history.

courses.title: Army Doctrine and Decision Making
courses.description:
MS 202 focuses on Army doctrine and decision-making. The course begins with Cadets gaining an insight into analytical techniques, creative thinking skills, and the Army problem-solving process as related to situations faced by leaders committed to the ideal that America and its founding documents remain the most powerful force for good in human history. Troop Leading Procedures and Operations Orders will lead Cadets to an understanding of Army Doctrine and Symbology.  Squad tactics will be covered in classes during Multidomain Operations, Offensive Operations, and Defensive Operations. Cadets will apply classroom knowledge during hands-on performance-oriented weekly labs facilitated by MS III Cadets and supervised by MS IVs and cadre, and participate in weekly physical readiness training (PRT) sessions (ending with a diagnostic Army Fitness Test) planned and conducted by MS IV Cadets (Senior Cadets) and cadre.
 
The course produces a Cadet grounded in foundational leadership doctrine and skills by leading small units in achieving assigned missions. Utilizes critical thinking and problem-solving during Troop Leading Procedures (TLPs). Committed to physical fitness, applies Army values and understands the importance of the officer’s role in leading change; is knowledgeable in the Army as a profession and is committed to the ideal that America and its founding documents remain the most powerful force for good in human history.

Committed to physical fitness, applies Army values and understands the importance of the officer’s role in leading change; is knowledgeable in the Army as a profession and is committed to the ideal that America and its founding documents remain the most powerful force for good in human history.

courses.title: ROTC Leaders Training Course
courses.description: Introduction to military science for students having little or no military experience.  Provides experiences in management, teaching, first aid, physical conditioning.  Qualifies student for ROTC Leadership Development Assessment Course (LDAC).

courses.title: Basic Training
courses.description: Basic Training

courses.title: Warfighting Functions and Army Training Management
courses.description:
MS 301 focuses on training management and the warfighting functions. It is an academically challenging course where you will study, practice, and apply the fundamentals of Training Management and how the Army operates through the Warfighting Functions. At the conclusion of this course, you will be capable of planning, preparing, and executing training for a squad conducting small unit tactics. The semester includes physical fitness development and a weekly Lab which includes hands-on performance-oriented skills using MSIII/peer facilitation overseen by MS IVs (Senior Cadets), supervised by ROTC Cadre.
 
The course produces a Cadet who possesses enhanced individual and collective skills including leader competencies; effectively leads formations at the squad and platoon level in a variety of military and non-military mission context scenarios; effective at receiving and giving peer evaluations; who is committed and disciplined ethically, academically, physically, and socially; and committed to the ideal that America and its founding documents remain the most powerful force for good in human history.
courses.prerequisiteText: Take 1 of the following courses: ; MS202 - Army Doctrine and Decision Making (4) ; MS202S - Army Doctrine and Decision Making - Lecture (2) ; MS290 - ROTC Leaders Training Course (6) ; MS297 - Basic Training (6)

courses.title: Platoon Operations
courses.description:
MS 302 focuses on applied leadership in small unit operations. It is an academically challenging course where you will analyze, test, and relate the fundamentals of direct-level leadership and small unit tactics at the platoon level. At the conclusion of this course, you will be capable of planning, coordinating, navigating, motivating, and leading a platoon in the execution of a mission. The semester includes physical fitness development and a weekly Lab which includes hands-on performance-oriented skills using MSIII/peer facilitation overseen by MS IVs (Senior Cadets), supervised by ROTC Cadre.
 
The course produces a Cadet who possesses enhanced individual and collective skills including leader competencies; effectively leads formations at the squad and platoon level in a variety of military and non-military mission context scenarios; effective at receiving and giving peer evaluations; who is committed and disciplined ethically, academically, physically, and socially; and committed to the ideal that America and its founding documents remain the most powerful force for good in human history.

courses.title: The Army Officer
courses.description:
MS 401 focuses on the development of an Army Officer committed to the ideal that America and its founding documents remain the most powerful force for good in human history. It is an academically challenging course where you will develop knowledge, skills, and abilities required of junior officers pertaining to the Army in Multidomain Operations. You will also learn to plan, resource, and assess training at the small unit level using the Training Management Process. At the conclusion of this course, you will be familiar with the Operations Process and Planning, conducting Unit Training, Multidomain Operations, and Unit Readiness.  The course includes physical readiness training and weekly labs overseeing MS III Cadet facilitated training supervised by ROTC Cadre.
 
The course produces a leader of character possessing a professional identity committed to the Army ethic and profession and is a moral exemplar; is prepared to be an Army leader who is physically fit and thrives in ambiguous environments; a skilled critical thinker, problem solver, team builder; skilled oral and written communicator with knowledge of training management and Army Doctrine; committed to the ideal that America and its founding documents remain the most powerful force for good in human history.

courses.title: Company Grade Leadership
courses.description:
MS 402 focuses on the development of Company Grade Officer committed to the ideal that America and its founding documents remain the most powerful force for good in human history.  It is an academically challenging course where you will develop the knowledge, skills, and abilities required of junior officers pertaining to unit-level leader roles and responsibilities. You will learn about Army programs that support counseling subordinates and evaluating performance, values and ethics, career planning, and legal responsibilities. The course includes physical readiness training and weekly labs overseeing MS III facilitated training supervised by ROTC Cadre.  Successful completion of this course will prepare you for branch-specific training and is a mandatory requirement for commissioning.
 
The course produces a leader of character possessing a professional identity committed to the Army ethic and profession and is a moral exemplar; is prepared to be an Army leader who is physically fit and thrives in ambiguous environments; a skilled critical thinker, problem solver, team builder; skilled oral and written communicator with knowledge of training management and Army Doctrine; committed to the ideal that America and its founding documents remain the most powerful force for good in human history.

courses.title: Directed Study/Projects
courses.description: This course provides senior students with the opportunity to apply the skills they have learned.  Requires simultaneous membership in ROTC and Army Reserve/National Guard.

courses.title: Music and the Humanities
courses.description: This course is designed to acquaint the student with our musical heritage and its relationship to history and the other arts.  The student will acquire a basic musical vocabulary useful for discussing and writing about music. Curriculum to be determined by instructor, i.e., classical emphasis, jazz emphasis, etc. The course is for non-music majors, music minors and some music clusters.

courses.title: Music in Western Civilization
courses.description: This course focuses upon the study of music within the history and humanities of Western Civilization.  In addition to the fundamental knowledge of western civilization students will also develop fundamental listening and writing skills, anticipating the more advanced requirements of the required upper-division music history and literature sequence. Successful completion of Music 102, 301, 302, and 303 satisfies the Foundations World requirement.
